profiles.bio:
• 2022 (New Mexico): Tied for the team lead with 2 INTs, 2 FFs. Played in all 12 games with starts in the final 9 contests (87 tackles, 3 TFLs, 3 PBUs). Made 24 tackles against Fresno State, with an INT.
  • 2023 (Houston): Led team with 98 tackles. Started all 12 games (TFL, 4 PBUs, FF). 
  • 2024 (Houston): First-team All-Big 12 Conference. Tied for fourth in the FBS with 5 INTs. Led team with 8 PBUs. Started all 12 games (74 tackles).
  • 2025: First-team All-SEC. Tied for the team lead with 3 INTs. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts (88 tackles, 0.5 TFLs, 4 PBUs, FF). Suspended for the first half of the team's opener because he was ejected from Houston's final game in the previous season.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Haulcy, aka Mr. Give Me That, is a throwback safety with a compact, densely muscled frame and a pro feel for reading the field. He’s a rare blend of ballhawk and enforcer who can scurry into passing lanes for takeaways or run through a receiver to break up a pass. His pattern recognition and instincts are top-notch and he’s decisive in his reactions. A lack of sustained top-end speed could create mismatches in man coverage. He’s more effective playing forward than he is at guarding large spaces in deeper coverages. He’s rock-steady as a finisher but sees the missed tackle total tick higher as an open-field tackler. Haulcy’s frame and game are pro-ready, though. He projects as a good NFL starter in a zone-heavy scheme.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “His speed concerns me some, but he’s just a really instinctive player all the way around. I know there are differing opinions about him in our building, but I think he’s a Pro Bowler in the right scheme.” - NFL personnel director
profiles.strengths:
• Compact, densely muscled frame.
  • Built like a pro and plays with the poise/eyes of a pro.
  • Outstanding instincts and route recognition fuel on-ball production.
  • Posted 12 pass breakups and eight interceptions over the last two seasons.
  • Operates with good eye balance and is decisive breaking into passing lanes.
  • Closes downhill with good balance and body control.
  • Enforcer in the middle who hits like a bag of concrete.
  • Toggles speed to maintain pursuit leverage and adjust his path to ball-carriers.
  • Generally tackles with good form and plenty of stopping power.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average recovery speed and burst to close.
  • Short arms create smaller margins for error as a tackler.
  • Loses some of his effectiveness when playing downhill.
  • Will have speed mismatches to contend with in man coverage.
  • Average change of direction and reactive agility as an open-field tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted.
  • 2023: Played in 7 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Started all 16 games at RT. 
  • 2025: Started all 12 games at RT. Named to the AFCA Allstate Good Works Team for his community service efforts.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Two-year starter and 2025 team captain with elite personal character but marginal athletic traits. Wagner is smart and makes good use of his length when punching/staying connected to second-level blocks. His lack of foot quickness reduces his range as a run blocker and creates issues getting to his set-points against edge speed in protection. Wagner lacks the body control to adjust comfortably to moving targets, which limits his potential against NFL athleticism. He could be drafted in the late rounds, but I see a relatively low ceiling.
profiles.strengths:
• Generally firm on contact off the snap and into the block.
  • Lands inside hand strikes with good leverage at point of attack.
  • Gives good effort to sustain second-level blocks.
  • Long first stride helps when jump-setting pass rushers off the snap.
  • Delivers pass punch with well-timed hands to maximize length.
  • Uses length as a recovery mechanism to help gather rush movement.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks desired bend and thickness of frame.
  • Will struggle when adjusting to movement.
  • Plays with high pad level and is missing leg drive for displacement.
  • Too plodding to slide and meet edge speed at the junction point.
  • Below-average body control and base width for mirroring inside counters.
  • Lacks agility and footwork needed for NFL recoveries when beaten.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Alabama): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve. Slowed by injury.
  • 2023: Played in 11 games with 2 starts (12-59-4.9 receiving; 3-39-13.0 KR).
  • 2024: Led team with 61 receptions, 884 receiving yards (14.5 per, 5 TDs). Played in all 13 games with 9 starts (3-152-50.7, TD KR). 
  • 2025: Played in 9 games with 5 starts (33-398-12.1 receiving). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Anderson is a short but stocky slot receiver with good speed but below-average hands. Injuries and quarterback play slowed his production in 2025, so a heavier dose of 2024 tape is needed for his evaluation. His routes are rhythmic and fairly disciplined, but he fails to create enough separation from his break points. He has the play strength to compete for the contested throws he’s likely to see against tight press man. Anderson has the talent and toughness NFL teams like to see, but his lack of size/explosiveness could make it challenging for him to earn a spot as a backup.
profiles.strengths:
• Properly tempos and times his routes.
  • Usually maintains vertical separation when he gets it.
  • Routes show discipline to hide break intentions.
  • Lift and timing to challenge high-points despite his lack of height.
  • Shells up when contact is imminent to protect the catch.
  • Able to shake the first tackler and quickly get up the field.
  • Had a kick-return touchdown in 2024.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Shows a small delay in acceleration from release fakes.
  • Average change-of-direction quickness in his breaks.
  • Has speed but is inconsistent to drive and separate versus man.
  • Catch focus and hand-eye coordination are below average.
  • Inconsistent in working back and scrambling to help quarterback.

profiles.overview: Two-year starter with consistent production in the key categories. Graves lacks NFL-caliber size, length and athletic-testing numbers, but he fills stat columns, using hustle and know-how to find the action. He finished his career with an impressive sack total (16.5) but he’s not a consistent quick-win rusher and those numbers are unlikely to translate. He struggles to hold his ground against double-teams/angle pressure as a run defender, while his lack of length hurts his consistency with block shed and tackling.
profiles.strengths:
• Keeps pad level low off the snap and into first contact.
  • Plays with consistent effort and hustle through the whistle.
  • Upper-body turn allows him to slide around blocks when he finds the edge.
  • Good timing to counter from edge to edge as a rusher.
  • Keeps feet moving and hands active to build an extended rush.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks lateral quickness to win the landmark over wide-zone blockers.
  • Gets shoved around and out of his gap by angle blocks.
  • Short arms limit overall tackle range and success rate.
  • Will struggle to crank up pocket push through pure power.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 12 games with 1 start at WR (10-128-12.8 receiving). Tore ACL in spring practice but returned for the season.
  • 2023: Played in 13 games with 5 starts at WR (22-250-11.4 receiving; 1-15-15.0 KR).
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 1 start (4-44-11.0 rushing; 16-155-9.7, 2 TDs receiving; 3-74-24.7 KR). Moved from WR to RB during the season.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Led team with 814 rushing yards (168 carries, 4.8 per), 10 rushing TDs. Started all 13 games (36-254-7.1, 3 TDs receiving; 9-213-23.7 KR). Named to the AFCA Allstate Good Works Team. Team captain.
  • Miscellaneous: Older brother, Austin, played DB at Coastal Carolina before walking on at Clemson to play with Adam. Father, Jerome, played football and basketball at South Carolina State.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Randall, a former wide receiver, is new to his position, but his blend of size, top-end speed and pass-catching ability make him an intriguing prospect. He's an upright long-strider with surprising one-cut quickness and home-run potential. He doesn’t run with pro-level rhythm, recognition or timing, but improvement awaits. He’s willful once he’s downhill, using balance and force to maximize yardage after collisions. His receiving skills create mismatches against man coverage and allow for alignment versatility. Randall is still raw, but RBs with his size, speed and route skill are rare. He offers value as a developmental option with RB2 upside in a zone-heavy scheme.
profiles.strengths:
• Tremendous blend of size and top-end speed.
  • Improved at following blocks as season progressed.
  • One-cut runner who can plant and cut sharply on outside-zone carries.
  • Presses forward through contact for tough yardage and touchdowns.
  • Former wideout with alignment and route versatility.
  • Separates from linebackers and catches with soft hands.
  • Has experience to project as a viable kick returner.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Upright runner getting through the line of scrimmage.
  • Can be clunky with his feet when stacking cuts.
  • Displays indecisiveness without a clear point of entry.
  • Struggles to make decisions moving at top speed.
  • Suffered ACL tear (2022), broken hand (2023) and stress fracture in toe (2024).
  • Has yet to show improved technique/toughness in blitz protection.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games with 2 starts (27 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games with 1 start (46 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Tied for the team lead with 3 INTs (1 returned for TD). Played in all 14 games with 4 starts (73 tackles, 6 TFLs, 6 PBUs, FF). 
  • 2025: First-team All-ACC. Led team with 104 tackles. Tied for seventh in the FBS with 5 INTs (1 returned for TD). Started all 13 games (5.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Moses burst onto the scene with a strong 2024, but his 2025 production was even better. He’s squatty and short-limbed, but he plays with good instincts and quick response times. He’s twitchy to close quickly on catch targets and run fits with fluid change of direction to adjust angles as a tackler. He has adequate range on the back end but taller receivers can play over his head and he lacks the tackle radius for consistent open-field stops when playing deep. Kick coverage boosts his draft value, and sliding into a full-time zone nickelback role could be his best pro fit.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted eight interceptions over the last two seasons.
  • Twitchy athlete with sudden change of direction.
  • Plays safety with eye balance and good positioning.
  • Pounces on quick game and short throws with immediacy.
  • Quick to diagnose and trigger deep into the run fit.
  • Good read-and-reaction to runner’s lane choice.
  • Sticky hands to flip field and his kick-cover talent stands out.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Squatty frame lacks desired length for position.
  • Pass-catchers go up and over him for grabs.
  • Loses track of positioning from depth near the red zone.
  • Knocked to the ground by size near the line.
  • Takes chances pursuing wide and will lose leverage.
  • Limited tackle radius once the ball-carrier hits the open field.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Auburn): Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 9 games as a reserve (1 tackle).
  • 2023: Played in 11 games with 6 starts (31 tackles, 3 INTs, 3 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (63 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, INT, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Led team with 7 PBUs. Played in 10 games with 8 starts (26 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A slender, fifth-year senior cornerback, Harvey’s lack of size could force him inside to nickelback. He has tight hips and can be too eager to chase route fakes, but he does a nice job of staying phased up with vertical routes. He’s outmuscled inside the route and down the field. From zone, he can identify and close with quickness. He’s irritating to receivers when allowed to play the catch point. Harvey is willing in the run game but takes heavy punishment when throwing his body at runners to make a tackle. Harvey has a chance to be drafted, but making a roster will be challenging.
profiles.strengths:
• Generally in-phase when the route begins.
  • Plays with good eye balance and healthy suspicion.
  • Quick transition from diagnose to drive from off coverage.
  • Urgent to shut down quick game and screen throws.
  • Good level of willingness and effort as a run defender.
  • Took just over a month to return from a dislocated ankle during 2025 season.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Tight hips slow both vertical and lateral transitions.
  • Overly responsive to every bend and fake inside the route.
  • Struggles to gather and match against comebacks.
  • Lack of size shows up downfield and at the top of the route.
  • Has trouble ungluing from committed run blockers on the flank.
  • Uses his head to chop running backs down too often.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 11 games with 3 starts (17 tackles, sack).
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 6 sacks. Played in all 13 games as a reserve (27 tackles, 8.5 TFLs with 6 sacks, PBU).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Led team with 6 sacks. Started all 12 games (33 tackles, 7 TFLs with 6 sacks, PBU).
  • 2025: Led team with 10 TFLs, 7.5 sacks. Started 11 games (28 tackles, FF). Missed final 2 games of the regular season due to injury, returned for the bowl game.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Hubbard is a good athlete with adequate burst, change-of-direction quickness and agility. His game against Oregon was a clear indicator that more size and strength are needed to survive run-defending rigors as a down lineman. A full-time spot as an odd-front edge rusher could be in his wheelhouse, though. He can chase down the action and has a nose for making tackles when he’s close to the ball. His rush features athletic elements, but the toolbox needs filling. With more strength and rush development, Hubbard could develop into an average edge defender.
profiles.strengths:
• Agile with plus short-area change of direction.
  • Efforts to beat seal blocks to play-side contain positioning.
  • Slips blockers in tight quarters and crosses their face on slants.
  • Accelerates and holds his speed in run-game pursuit.
  • Flashes solid upfield burst as a rusher.
  • Loose upper half to slip and play off blocks through the turn.
  • Dips and drives through the tackle’s chest as a bull rusher.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs more mass and play strength.
  • Knocked back or widened out by force at the point.
  • Stiff punch from strong tackles saps his rush.
  • Needs proactive hands to stay clean and active.
  • Hasn’t developed a fluid counter for when he hits pocket depth.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (James Madison): Played in 10 games as a reserve and on special teams (5 tackles).
  • 2023 (James Madison): Third-team All-Sun Belt Conference. Led team with 108 tackles. Played in 13 games with 11 starts (6 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, INT, 7 PBUs, blocked kick).
  • 2024: First-team All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 118 tackles. Started all 13 games (5.5 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, 4 PBUs).
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten. Finalist for the Butkus Award (nation's top LB). Started all 15 games for the national champions (97 tackles, 10.5 TFLs with 4.5 sacks, 2 INTs-1 returned for TD, PBU, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fisher is a Mike linebacker who can run the defense as an extension of his coordinator. He’s well-built with leadership and football character that are praised by teammates and coaches. Fisher has the instincts and feel of an NFL player but lacks the needed quickness and athletic ability. He reads play designs and gets to the action at a high rate, but a lack of range, cover talent and plus open-field tackling will make the NFL jump challenging.
profiles.strengths:
• Team leader with mindset emblematic of Indiana football.
  • Stuffed stat sheet with 300+ tackles over the last three seasons.
  • Good recognition of play design and blocking scheme.
  • Frequently beats running back to the gap.
  • Slips blocks with perfect timing.
  • Sneaky but strong when setting picks in rush games.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average speed and athleticism.
  • Change of direction in space is labored.
  • Struggles to leverage wide pursuit due to his speed.
  • Hips are clunky and feet are heavy in zone drops.
  • Has trouble stacking and shedding zone blocks.
  • Lack of short-area agility will lead to missed tackles.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (West Virginia): Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Freshman All-American. Led team with 5 sacks. Played in 10 games with 1 start (32 tackles, 6.5 TFLs with 5 sacks).
  • 2021 (West Virginia): Honorable Mention All-Big 12. Started all 13 games (38 tackles, 8 TFLs with 4.5 sacks).
  • 2022: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Led team with 7 sacks, tied for the team lead with 10.5 TFL. Played in 11 games with 8 starts (38 tackles, 4 PBUs, FF).
  • 2023: Played in 2 games with 2 starts (5 tackles, sack). Missed the rest of the season due to injury (torn ligaments in both feet required surgery).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 13 games (32 tackles, 9 TFLs with 5.5 sacks).
  • 2025: First-team All-ACC. Tied for third in the FBS with 12.5 sacks, tied for fifth with 17.5 TFLs, tied for sixth with 4 FFs. Started 15 games (63 tackles). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Mesidor is an instinctive, high-effort edge rusher with a fluid rush style and a deep toolbox. He bursts upfield and can shrink the corner while punishing oversetting tackles with inside counters. He strings moves together with effortless mid-rush adjustments, utilizing harmonious hands and feet to carve efficient tracks into the pocket. He’s a problem for guards when reduced inside, too. His urgency shows up in run defense, where he uses play strength and short-area quickness to disrupt blocking schemes and stay around the football. He won’t be as long as most edge-setters and his anchor at the point is just average. The talent and motor are obvious, but his age and injury history could push some teams to discount his grade below what the tape shows.
profiles.strengths:
• Blends rabid determination with coaching from Hall of Famer Jason Taylor.
  • Uses finesse or power depending on approach and opponent.
  • Appears to gain momentum and speed at the turn.
  • Effective inside-outside Euro step helps shrink the corner.
  • Recognizes oversets by tackle and attacks them accordingly.
  • Constantly countering once he feels momentum wain.
  • Disciplined in spying quarterback on boot action.
  • Eager to find the football and make a play in run game.
  • Pursues wide with adequate speed and smart angles.
  • Keeps hustle dialed in when chasing plays down the field.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks desired height/length as an NFL edge.
  • Speed-to-power conversion is average by league standards.
  • Base narrows through engagement, leading to imbalance.
  • Desire to chase play direction sets him up for counters.
  • Foot injury limited him to three games in 2023.
  • Will be a 25-year-old rookie.

profiles.overview: Henderson is a skilled and instinctive runner with good size, but he might lack the explosiveness to reach his full potential. His excellent vision, footwork and play strength make him effective inside. He has a rare feel for space in the open field, helping him evade tacklers. He could struggle on wide runs, though, as his lack of burst is likely to condense the field for him. He's a poor pass-catcher but a tough pass protector who can contribute on kick coverage. Henderson will require the right scheme fit to become a contributor in the pros.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses NFL-caliber size, strength and vision.
  • Impressive ability to create as an interior runner.
  • Smooth jump-cut allows him to elude early traffic.
  • Disguises and sets up cuts with patience and know-how.
  • Leg drive and balance to break tackles.
  • Will square up and seek out contact in blitz pickup.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hip tightness creates some minor limitations.
  • Lacks acceleration to outrun NFL linebackers to the corner.
  • Average burst might require him to play faster at the next level.
  • Ball security was an issue in 2025.
  • Hand-eye coordination not where it needs to be as a pass-catcher.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Shorter University): Started all 11 games at RT.
  • 2023 (Shorter University): Started all 11 games (3 at LT, 8 at RT).
  • 2024: Started all 12 games at RT.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 12 games at RT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Herron is a traits-based projection with just two years of FBS experience. He has NFL size and length but the fundamentals and technique are far from finished products. He lacks initial quickness/bend to fit blocks with leverage and generate drive. In pass pro, he must become more active and aggressive with his hands, whether punching or latching into rushers to prevent secondary effort. He figures to show quick improvement if he can receive concentrated coaching. Herron could be drafted late but without more grit and finishing ability, it will be hard to persevere against NFL competition.
profiles.strengths:
• Built big and long with NFL dimensions.
  • Never missed a start over four seasons.
  • Protection showed obvious improvement in-season.
  • Displayed adequate change of direction when mirroring.
  • Basic technical improvement will improve his run blocking.
  • Wide frame can cover and slow linebackers on climbs.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lazy punch lacks heat and is too easy to bypass.
  • Has trouble shoving edge-turners off their path into the pocket.
  • Below-average slide quickness and anchor.
  • Plays too high and with a lack of explosion into contact.
  • Needs to strike with inside hands and run his feet under them.
  • Missing necessary aggression and grit to finish blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022: Team's Most Improved Defensive Player. Played in 11 games with 1 start (16 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, PBU, blocked kick).
  • 2023: Played in 12 games with 1 start (15 tackles, 2.5 TFLs with 1 sack). Started the Texas Bowl versus Oklahoma State.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (36 tackles, 3 TFLs with 0.5 sack, 6 PBUs).
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (49 tackles, 3 TFLs with 2 sacks, 3 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with two years as a starter, Regis is built low, with girthy lowers and shorter arms. He’s a leverage monster who can function as a tree stump in the middle of the defense when he’s first in with his hands. He can post and peek as a two-gapper or drop low to fight off double-teams. He plays with good balance and is technically sound in block take-ons/disengagements. His rush is unimpressive and his lack of length will cause issues at times, but he’s tough, strong and consistent. Regis should become a run-stopping factor as a nose tackle.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He’s mature, he works hard, he does everything the right way. He’s a good player and a great guy to have in your locker room.” - AFC area scout
profiles.strengths:
• Built wide with good bend for optimal leverage and balance.
  • Resets the line of scrimmage when heads-up with centers.
  • Rips a heavy punch through the blocker’s pads and locks out instantly.
  • Splits doubles with a wide base, heavy hands and proper positioning.
  • Technically sound getting into and off of blocks.
  • Reaches the reach block to prevent being sealed easily on zone blocks. 
  • Has moments where he tosses guards and centers aside like rag dolls.
  • Can club pass protection off balance if he catches blocker in an over-set.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Arm length falls below the standard at his position.
  • Finds himself in trouble if he’s tardy with his hand strikes.
  • Gets close but will miss out on tackles due to lack of length.
  • Has trouble finding and exploiting the edges with his rush.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Tyler Junior College): Played in 4 games at TE.
  • 2021 (Tyler Junior College): Played at OT. 
  • 2022 (Colorado): Played in 12 games as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Texas State): Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2024 (Texas State): Third-team All-Sun Belt Conference. Started 12 games at RT. 
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started 14 games at RT. Team was finalist for the Joe Moore Award (nation's top OL).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior whose lack of length is likely to push him inside to guard. Harkey has the mass to play guard but needs to prove he has the core strength to deal with interior bullies. He can operate in both gap and zone schemes. However, he will need better patience/body control to fit and sustain at the desired level. Harkey’s experience at tackle and his athletic tools create a real opportunity to become a successful interior protector provided he can hold up to the bull rush. Harkey projects as a backup guard with starting potential.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses mass for a move inside to guard.
  • Has torque strength in hips and athletic feet as a move blocker.
  • Resets hands and runs his feet on angle blocks.
  • Prioritizes block finishes and plays with some edge.
  • Pass punch is sudden, direct and crisp.
  • Features strong hands to secure the rush.
  • Has athleticism to match with sub-package rushers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Better landmarks and technique needed on zone blocks.
  • Rushes and lunges at blocks, leading to inconsistent body control.
  • Hands could get a little too wide when climbing to linebackers.
  • Could struggle to anchor against bull-rushing defensive tackles.
  • Two-hand punch opens him up to spins and counters.
  • Lacks length and needs to prove he can defend his edges.

profiles.bio:
• 2020-21 (Arkansas-Pine Bluff): Played in all 5 games of the team's spring season as a reserve (9 tackles, 3 PBUs). School did not play in the fall due to COVID-19 concerns.
  • 2021 (Arkansas-Pine Bluff): Led team with 3 INTs (1 returned for TD), 14 PBUs. Started all 11 games (29 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack).
  • 2022: Played in all 14 games with 2 starts (18 tackles, sack, 3 PBUs).
  • 2023: Played in 14 games as a reserve (11 tackles, 2 PBUs).
  • 2024: Redshirted. Missed the season due to injury.
  • 2025: First-team All-MAC. Tied for the team lead with 11 PBUs. Started all 13 games (49 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, INT).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fuller is a long press corner with NFL-caliber size and strength. He’s capable of delaying and redirecting the release but a lack of make-up speed creates problems when he gets out of the gate poorly against speed in man coverage. Fuller might need the scheme to do some of the cover work for him. Cover 2 and deep-zone coverages allow for the best use of Fuller’s size and length, while minimizing pattern-matching in space. If he can become a more dedicated tackler, a conversion to safety could be a consideration.
profiles.strengths:
• Big, long and strong from press positioning.
  • Patient feet allow release fakes to clear.
  • Able to widen out release with his long punch.
  • Reads receiver’s eyes and attacks hands with timing.
  • Beats up the catch space when he’s in position.
  • Has punt and kick-cover talent in his background.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Late reaching in press slows take-off departure to flip and run.
  • Hips and feet aren’t wired for matching complex routes.
  • Struggles staying connected to route breaks from trail.
  • Lack of top-end speed showed up against Kentucky. 
  • Rarely finds the football with his back to the action.
  • Needs to drop his entry point and body-up as a tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 10 games with 4 starts at RG.
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 13 games at RG.
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 13 games at RG.
  • 2025: Second-team All-ACC. Started all 16 games at RG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Cooper is a big and proportional guard. He loses effectiveness when blocking in space, but he plays with good body control and understands how to use his size to neutralize in-line opponents. He has heavy hands and punches quickly into extension in pass pro to subdue rush momentum, making him difficult to circumnavigate. He struggles staying mirrored to athletic rushers with quality setups, though. His issues identifying and responding to rush games are cause for concern. Cooper’s limitations require occasional help, but he has starter upside in the right scheme fit.
profiles.strengths:
• Built wide with excellent length.
  • Covers first- and second-level targets with his size and stays there.
  • Explosive power will be felt from his heavy hands.
  • Climbs up to linebackers with fairly nimble feet for adjustments.
  • Plays with edge in his finish.
  • Punch lands firm, immediately stalling the rush.
  • Difficult to swipe his punch away once he’s extended.
profiles.weaknesses:
• High pad level with unfocused hand placement in the run game.
  • More wall-off than drive blocker due to lack of leverage.
  • Gives ground quickly when seeking wide zone landmarks.
  • Slow processing/reacting to game development inside the rush.
  • Needs to prioritize foot movement instead of reaching.
  • Lack of knee bend greatly diminishes leverage for redirect blocks.

profiles.overview: Thompson is a slightly undersized but explosive interior defender with the potential to take snaps as both a 1- and 3-technique in a one-gapping scheme. He lacks a track record of production and is more of a projection-based prospect. A lack of response quickness post-snap diminishes his effectiveness in the first phase of the rep, so getting his actions timed up to the snap will be critical in unlocking his disruption. He hasn’t learned to convert his athletic ability into a more consistent rush, but he certainly could do that in time. Thompson profiles as a late Day 3 pick with developmental upside.
profiles.strengths:
• Plus upper-body power to punch, separate and shed.
  • Twitchy movements in shadowing runners’ cuts.
  • Exceptional range and closing speed for an interior lineman.
  • Flashes more potential as a rusher than pressure totals would indicate.
  • Pro-day results should put him in play for draft consideration.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks career production relative to his disruption potential.
  • Below-average reaction time off the snap.
  • Frequently beaten to the spot by zone blockers.
  • Unable to hold his ground against big downhill blockers.
  • Hasn’t developed any potent openers to kick-start his rush.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. Big 12 Conference Co-Defensive Freshman of the Year. Honorable Mention All-Big 12. Played in all 14 games with 6 starts (67 tackles, 8 TFLs with 5 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024: Second-team Associated Press All-American. Second-team All-SEC. Led team with 113 tackles, 16.5 TFL. Tied for fifth in the FBS with 4 FFs. Started all 16 games (8 sacks, INT, PBU).
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. Second-team All-SEC. Finalist for the Butkus Award (nation's top LB). Tied for the team lead with 3 FFs. Started 10 games (69 tackles, 7 TFLs with 4 sacks, 2 INTs, PBU). Missed 2 games with a broken hand. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-down linebacker with the playing demeanor and production of a future Pro Bowler. He posted 31.5 TFLs, 17 sacks and eight forced fumbles in his three seasons at Texas, making an impact in every phase. He’s instinctive, athletic and under control, transitioning seamlessly from read to react to finish. He plays with downhill thump to thwart interior blocks and the speed to pursue runners from sideline to sideline. Hill has plus cover talent in man or zone, proven credentials as a blitzer or edge rusher, and finishes plays as a strong, reliable tackler. Consistency and field command make him one of the safer linebackers in the class. His size, speed and versatility allow him to profile as an instant-impact rookie at Mike or Will ‘backer.
profiles.strengths:
• Diagnoses cleanly with no wasted steps.
  • Keys offensive line movement without overreacting.
  • Triggers downhill with force to stonewall climbing blockers.
  • Avoids unnecessary block engagement, staying free to make plays.
  • Changes direction with suddenness and at tight angles.
  • Impressive instincts when covering in space.
  • Gains depth quickly and identifies route structure.
  • Able to pressure the pocket and get home for sacks off the edge.
  • Slippery hips to bypass blitz pickups and attack the pocket.
  • Arrives under control and balanced with time to adjust as a tackler.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Production boosted by a heavy dose of run-blitz calls.
  • Occasionally allows cut-back opportunities to develop.
  • Blitz disguise and trigger timing are below average.
  • Can carry routes a step longer in zone coverage.
  • Missed tackles spiked in 2024 when he came in too high.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Texas A&M): Played in 7 games as a reserve (10 tackles, TFL).
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games with 1 start (10 tackles, 3.5 TFLs).
  • 2024: Played in 6 games with 6 starts (16 tackles, PBU). Missed the end of the year due to injury.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started 12 games (37 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Lucas is an edge defender with NFL size and length but a disappointing lack of collegiate production. His play is more gradual than twitchy. He lacks explosiveness up the field as a rusher and into first contact as a run defender. He plays with occasional flashes, but hints of hesitation in both phases prevent him from sustaining those flashes. There are physical traits and athletic ability to work with but there isn’t enough on tape to project Lucas will stick on a roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Good size with a seven-foot wingspan.
  • Swift stick-and-slip around blocking tight ends.
  • Good athlete with back-side burst to tackle.
  • Rushes from outside and inside.
  • Hits ball-carriers and quarterbacks with heavy pads.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Ducks helmet into first contact when looking to make a tackle.
  • Lacks explosiveness to shock, separate and shed.
  • Decelerates and gathers before landing a blow on blocks.
  • Below-average lateral quickness as looper in twists.
  • Missing rush instincts to find or create openings.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Freshman All-American. Honorable Mention All-ACC. Led team with 56 receptions, 604 receiving yards (10.8 per, 4 TDs). Played in all 14 games with 10 starts (5-8-1.6 rushing; 1-26-26.0 KR; 15-129-8.6 PR).
  • 2023: Redshirted due to injuries. Played in 5 games with 4 starts (22-224-10.2, 2 TDs receiving; 3-14-4.7 PR).
  • 2024: First-team All-ACC WR, Honorable Mention All-ACC RS. Led team with 75 receptions, 904 receiving yards (12.1 per). Tied for seventh in the FBS with 11 receiving TDs. Started all 14 games (7-101-14.4, TD rushing; 17-164-9.6 PR).
  • 2025: Third-team All-ACC WR. Led team with 55 receptions (604 yards, 11.0 per, 4 TDs). Started 10 games (13-78-6.0, TD rushing; 4-44-11.0 PR).  

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Williams is a bona fide ball player with good size and an ability to make mischief when he totes the pigskin. There is freestyling inside his routes that create uncertainty for corners but teams might drill down on attention to detail and better efficiency to keep him on schedule. He’s not a field-stretcher but he plays fast from snap to whistle and has the ball skills to bring in challenging catches. He’s more slippery than explosive with outstanding run-after-catch ability. Williams projects as a productive slot receiver with legitimate run/pass/catch talent that should appeal to creative play-callers.
profiles.strengths:
• Consistently productive in four seasons at Clemson.
  • Possesses rare ability to throw, catch, run and return punts.
  • Sauces up defenders with fakes and tempo changes.
  • Works the middle of the field and has a good feel for soft spots in zone. 
  • Wiggle-and-go to turn hitches/screens into first downs.
  • Running back’s vision and cut quickness with ball in his hands.
  • Stabs and tucks off-frame throws with cat-quick hands. 
  • Loose and fluid making in-air adjustments to win jump balls.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lost games to nagging injuries in 2023 and 2025.
  • Rarely pressed and needs to prove he can beat it.
  • Not a deep hip-sinker for tight turns in his routes.
  • Lacks top-end speed to stretch defense from the slot.
  • Average burst to separate getting out of breaks.
  • Route work will need to become more efficient and focused.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Kansas): Played in 5 games with 3 starts at RG.
  • 2021 (Kansas): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Kansas): Played in all 13 games as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Kansas): Started 11 games at LG.
  • 2024: Started 12 games at RG. Did not play in the team's Las Vegas Bowl loss to USC.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. Played in 13 games with 12 starts at RG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior guard with NFL size and length. Reed-Adams is an adequate athlete in small spaces. However, he loses effectiveness when forced to venture beyond home base. As a downhill blocker, he uses size to compensate for his lack of leverage, but he’s missing the contact balance and body control to sustain with consistency. He lacks command in pass protection but maintains a feel for the rusher’s movement. He usually finds his anchor against a bull rush, but his inconsistency as a processor leads to mistakes against gaming fronts. Reed-Adams has a chance to earn a spot as a backup.
profiles.strengths:
• First contact generally carries adequate weight behind it.
  • Lands on target and immediately runs his feet to seal the block.
  • Does enough on double teams and work-up blocks.
  • Able to redirect his feet and slide with inside moves.
  • Good use of his length to aid in recovery to the rush.
  • Able to find his anchor against a bull rush.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average body composition and base balance.
  • Lacks instincts and loses track of protection assignments.
  • Needs to punch more and catch less against rushers.
  • Jostled around by contact, limiting ability as block finisher.
  • Leverage on drive blocks stymied by poor pad level.
  • Lacks range as a run blocker to land and sustain on the move.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Played in 8 games on special teams.
  • 2024: Played in all 16 games with 2 starts for the national champions (43 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 0.5 sacks).
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. Big Ten Conference LB of the Year, First-team All-Big Ten. Finalist for the Butkus Award (nation's top LB). Started all 14 games (69 tackles, 10 TFLs with 6.5 sacks, 2 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: At 20 years old, Reese is still growing into his frame and his game, but learning from James Laurinaitis (linebackers coach) and Matt Patricia (defensive coordinator) should give him a head start in acclimating to the pro game. He plays off-ball linebacker and stand-up edge with the talent to post impact production from either spot. His third-down versatility adds alignment variety and helps camouflage defensive intent. His run diagnosis and angles of attack are average, but he flows quickly once he triggers, using assertive hands to stack and play off blocks. He’s fast in pursuit and his tackle finishing could become elite. His rush is kinetic and tough for tackles to mirror. It’s under construction, but Reese has already sprouted go-to moves and rush plans that need more refinement. He might need some runway to hit his stride, but his rare blend of traits, explosiveness and versatility could become a perfect storm of chaos once a defense decides how to deploy him.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He can play from depth or rush, but in my opinion, you need to choose one and build from there. – AFC executive
profiles.strengths:
• Dynamic deployment potential as a Mike or hybrid Will linebacker.
  • Still in the process of filling out his frame.
  • Improved patience, diagnosis and downhill flow as season progressed.
  • Hands stay active to help play off, through and around blocks. 
  • Has all the tools to become an NFL edge-setter.
  • Tone-setting hand strikes explode into his targets.
  • Length and speed provide playmaking range a city block wide.
  • Already has three or four go-to rush moves under construction.
  • Pairs a run-and-dip edge move with a speed-bull counter.
  • Fluid and fast to maximize his attack on two-way goes.
  • Comes to balance with good timing and in a tackle-ready stance.
  • Twitchy laterally to bring down slashers in space.
  • Can rush, spy and smother man-cover targets underneath.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Upper-body strength will need more attention.
  • Lack of experience shows itself in reaction time when diagnosing.
  • Needs to cut his hands loose quicker when striking blockers. 
  • Affected by post-snap eye candy and misdirection.
  • Needs better hand work and a counter at the top of his rush.
  • Inconsistent route awareness in his zone drops.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in all 13 games with 5 starts at RT.
  • 2023: Started 9 games at LT. Missed time with injuries. 
  • 2024: Started all 13 games at LT.
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started all 12 games at LT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tall tackle prospect with starting experience at both tackle spots. He’s played against top-tier talent in the SEC, which bolsters his case, but his struggles against Texas A&M and Miami provide an idea of his ceiling. He has good feet and strong hands. He knows how to play but he struggles to bend and drive at the point of attack. Same goes for anchoring or defending his edges against power rushers. Barber projects as a Day 3 pick with a chance of becoming a swing tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• High school hooper with body control and foot quickness.
  • Quick to gain ground on initial sets and punches with timing.
  • Effective use of “snatch-and-trap” to battle longer rushers.
  • Strong hands can clinch and control defenders by their pads.
  • Keeps pads square and eyes to second level before climbing.
  • Hustles to hit his landmarks for back-side cutoffs.
profiles.weaknesses:
• High punch diminishes core power and causes slippage.
  • Struggles with technique and anchor to beat bull rushers.
  • Leaning and oversets see him countered by spin moves.
  • Needs double teams to generate push as drive blocker.
  • Feet lag behind upper body, causing lunging into first contact.
  • Below average knee bend and pad level for adjustments in space.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (2 tackles).
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games with 4 starts (36 tackles, sack, 2 PBUs).
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 8 starts (51 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (53 tackles, TFL, 3 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Brown is well-built and features good play strength. He’s an explosive athlete, but he’s missing the desired instincts in coverage, which might explain his lack of ball production. He has good top-end speed and range from the hash. He’s a physical striker and can be a full-stop tackler, but inconsistent angles to the ball turn into missteps that lead to explosive plays. His size, athletic profile and potential on special teams give him a chance to compete for a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Well-built with above-average wingspan for his size.
  • Showed great speed and explosiveness in pro day athletic testing.
  • Can play in multiple alignments but he’s at his best in a robber role.
  • Able to plant and burst with ideal quickness in coverage.
  • Has the play strength to stack and battle blockers.
  • Explodes through contact as a hitter/tackler.
profiles.weaknesses:
• No career interceptions and just 8 pass breakups in four seasons.
  • Miscalculates positioning to certain routes.
  • Lacks anticipation and instincts in reading routes.
  • Needs to play with better leverage in his pursuit angles.
  • Displays inconsistency as an open-field tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 11 games as a reserve and on special teams (12 tackles, 2 TFLs). Enrolled in January, after spring practices it was decided he would move from QB to DB.
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games as reserve and on special teams (15 tackles, PBU).
  • 2024: Second-team All-MAC. Tied for second in the FBS with 14 PBUs. Started all 13 games (58 tackles, 2 INTs, blocked kick). 
  • 2025: Second-team All-MAC. Tied for the team lead with 11 PBUs. Started all 13 games (42 tackles, 5 TFLs, INT, FF, blocked kick).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Smith’s instincts and production work in his favor, but a lack of length and sustained speed could raise questions. He mirrors well and can turn/run from press, but he struggles with control and timing in off-man transitions. He anticipates well when playing with his eyes forward and has an adequate burst to close. However, short arms will require tighter coverage to bring that ball production to the pros. Smith needs to prove himself a reliable tackler in run support and a capable man matchup option against NFL speed whether he’s aligned outside or inside at nickelback.
profiles.strengths:
• Hips and feet show good patience from press.
  • Able to accelerate quickly when in recovery mode.
  • Route recognition/anticipation improved throughout the year. 
  • Proactive to find the nearest threat in zone.
  • Loves to burst off edges and spoil runs before they start.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Becomes overzealous when he thinks he sniffs out the play.
  • Rarely tries to find the football when routes travel downfield.
  • Could struggle holding up against NFL speed.
  • Ready to hit but won’t always wrap up when needed.
  • Missed tackle total is concerning for a move to nickelback.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Played in 13 games with 5 starts (19 tackles, INT, 4 PBUs).
  • 2024: Second-team All-ACC. Led team with 12 PBUs. Started all 14 games (58 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 INTs, 3 FFs). 
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-ACC. Tied for third in the FBS with 5 FFs (tying school single-season record for a DB, set career record for a DB with 8). Tied for team lead with 9 PBUs. Started 12 games (48 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 3 sacks).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, A.J., played CB at Clemson and was a 2020 first-round pick of the Falcons.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Avieon shares the same bloodlines and coverage temperament as his brother, A.J., a first-round pick of the Falcons in 2020. Avieon Terrell is an athletic, fluid mover with clean transitions and enough speed to stay in phase on most vertical routes. He’s most effective in press-man coverage, where he mirrors releases with timing and discipline, staying crowded to the route. He concedes 50/50s to bigger targets at times, but is a constant catch irritant with good technique on all three levels. He can play wide or inside and is willing in run support, but he lacks ideal size. Terrell projects as an early starter thanks to his polish, ball skills and coverage versatility.
profiles.strengths:
• Blend of athleticism and size to play inside or outside.
  • Stays low and balanced when matching the release.
  • Guards against losing desired cover leverage at all times.
  • Smooth hip flip with quick acceleration into top speed.
  • Competitive energy makes route running laborious for the receiver.
  • Crowds receiver’s chest and finds the football downfield.
  • Closes quickly into the passing lane to harass the catch point.
  • Pulls and rips at the football, forcing eight fumbles during his career.
  • Good effort and urgency playing off perimeter blocks. 
  • Triggers downhill with control to do his part in run support.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Slender build gives ground to bigger wideouts on 50/50 balls.
  • Loses feel for bendy routes from trail positioning.
  • More reactive than proactive in anticipating receiver's break point.
  • Average eye balance and route awareness from short zones.
  • Will take some losses tackling bigger backs in run support.

profiles.overview: Kpeenu leans on physicality and yards after contact over elusiveness, burst or speed. His 28 bench-press reps at his pro day speak to the natural power he carries. It shows in the way he’s able to deny tacklers through force and keep his legs moving, especially near the goal line. He’s a linear runner lacking ideal bend, acceleration and top-end speed, so most of his yardage as a pro would be gained between the tackles. Kpeenu will likely need to prove himself on special teams to compete for a roster spot in camp.
profiles.strengths:
• Powerful with a compact frame and good musculation throughout.
  • Averaged a touchdown every 9.55 carries in 2025 (20 TDs on 191 attempts).
  • Impressive balance and ability to add yards after contact.
  • Catches with soft hands.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Tight-hipped and runs with below-average lower-body bend.
  • Lacks desired agility and can be clunky in small spaces.
  • Below-average speed limits his ability to win outside.
  • Not a natural plant-and-go runner in outside zone.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Kentucky): Freshman All-American. Freshman All-SEC Team. Led team with 50 receptions, 628 receiving yards (12.6 per, 4 TDs). Ranked fourth in the FBS in KR average (16-440-27.5, TD). Played in all 13 games with 7 starts (7-28-4.0 PR).
  • 2023 (Kentucky): Second-team All-SEC RS. Led the FBS with 36.0 yards per KR (16-576), 3 KR TDs. Led team with 43 receptions (539 yards, 12.5 per, 4 TDs). Associated Press All-Bowl Team, TaxSlayer.com Gator Bowl MVP (3-100, TD receiving; 2-26, TD rushing, 100-yard KR TD). Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (12-147-12.3, TD rushing).
  • 2024 (Kentucky): First-team All-SEC RS, second-team All-Purpose. Played in 11 games with 9 starts (29-361-12.4, 3 TDs receiving; 13-50-3.8, TD rushing; 18-449-24.9, TD KR; 1-6-6.0 PR).
  • 2025: Led team with 53 receptions, 532 receiving yards (10.0 per, TD). Set SEC career record with 6 KR TDs. Played in all 13 games with 9 starts (3-33-11.0 rushing; 15-445-29.7, TD KR).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Field-stretching flanker who is light on route and catch fundamentals but heavy on kick-return talent. Teams will need to factor in Brown’s ability to operate as a functional backup against his potential contributions on kickoffs, with league rules enhancing value in that area. A linear route tree might be needed to take advantage of his potential to get open deep or run free after the catch. His speed and return value make him worthy of selection on Day 3.
profiles.strengths:
• Sprinter speed can push safeties into deeper starting spots.
  • Wide catch radius gives him chances on more throws.
  • Puts up a good fight when he’s in position on 50/50 balls.
  • Slashing kick returner who keeps it downhill most of the time.
  • Finished career with six kick-return scores and a 29.4-yard return average.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Fast but lacks route-running fundamentals.
  • Rarely gets cornerbacks stacked once he’s by them.
  • Lacks consistency with his deep-ball tracking.
  • Struggles to improve positioning when the ball goes up.
  • Hand-eye coordination is spotty on all three levels.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Southeastern Louisiana): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve QB.
  • 2022 (Southeastern Louisiana): Played in 13 games with 2 starts (11-78-7.1, TD receiving; 10-83-8.3 rushing). Switched from QB to TE in spring practices, but played some Wildcat QB during the season.
  • 2023 (Southeastern Louisiana): Played in 11 games with 8 starts (29-288-9.9, 3 TDs receiving; 25-133-5.3, 5 TDs rushing; 0-1 passing). Played some Wildcat QB. 
  • 2024 (Oklahoma): Led team with 42 receptions, 324 receiving yards (7.7 per, 2 TDs). Started all 12 games (0-1, INT passing).
  • 2025: Started all 13 games (24-252-10.5, 2 TDs receiving).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sharp converted from quarterback to tight end at Southeastern Louisiana in 2022 before heading to Oklahoma (2024) and then to LSU (2025). He has some separation burst underneath but tends to fight the football and lacks consistency finishing through contact. He’s short-armed and slow to snap his hands into run blocks, allowing defenders to land first and quickly separate. He’s willing at the point but lacks core strength and is better suited to block on the move. He will have to shine in camp to have a chance to stick on a roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Hits accelerator on short out-breakers for breathing room.
  • Conscientious to drop feet in-bounds, catching tight to the boundary.
  • Displays adequate toughness through catch contact.
  • Strikes with low pad level and good hand placement on down block.
  • Finds, adjusts and centers up on block targets in space.
  • Will work with strain once he’s connected.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average arm length and core strength.
  • Beaten to the punch on a fairly consistent basis.
  • Struggles to prevent being discarded by NFL-caliber talent.
  • Fights throws with below-average hands as a pass-catcher.
  • Route tells allow coverage to jump his breaks.
  • Ball security after the catch is a concern.

profiles.overview: Three-year full-time snapper with good size but below-average velocity on his snaps. Gardner showed improvement with velocity and placement in 2025, but the total package might not be up to NFL standards.
profiles.strengths:
• Three-year snapper with good size for the position.
  • Showed vast improvement in 2025.
  • Adequate placement on short snaps.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks desired velocity on his long snaps.
  • Makes punter work a little too often.
  • Below-average open-field athleticism in coverage.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in 12 games with 10 starts at RG.
  • 2023: Played in 5 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Started 12 games at LG. 
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games at LG. Team won the Joe Moore Award (nation's top OL).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Stephens plays with a strong grasp for angles, tempo and timing for his block fits. He’s able to sustain and finish at a good rate despite having average play strength. However, his comfort level and consistency drop somewhat when working beyond inside/outside zone. He’s well-postured and plays with balance in pass pro. His lack of length will become more noticeable once he hits the pros, though. Short arms, average athleticism and scheme-friendly surroundings could temper his draft slotting, but Stephens has a chance to eventually become a starter if he finds the right team fit.
profiles.strengths:
• Doesn’t rush block fits, waiting until he’s balanced and in position.
  • Very good feel for angles and tempo in getting to his landmarks.
  • Makes timely block adjustments against shifting fronts.
  • Stays connected with his hands all the way through block finish.
  • Pass-sets with good posture.
  • Punches instead of catching when throwing his hands into rushers. 
  • Displays sufficient anchor to withstand a bull rush.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Has short arms and average athletic ability.
  • Needs to prove he can succeed in schemes other than zone.
  • Below-average connection accuracy when asked to pull.
  • Two-hand punch can be cleared by well-timed swipes for quick losses.
  • Rarely latches in tight to prevent secondary rush.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve (1-3-33.3 passing; 2-15-7.5 rushing). 
  • 2022: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Played in 9 games with 4 starts (96-169-56.8, 1,117 yards, 7 TDs, 6 INTs passing; 42-79-1.9, 2 TDs rushing). Missed 3 games due to injury.
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big 12. Independence Bowl Offensive MVP (27-43, 259 yards, 3 TDs) in win over California. Played in 10 games with 8 starts (182-293-62.1, 1,757 yards, 15 TDs, 8 INTs passing; 46-3-0.1, 4 TDs rushing). Played through shoulder injury. 
  • 2024: Started 12 games (295-466-63.3, 3,335 yards, 27 TDs, 8 INTs passing; TD rushing). Missed the team's bowl game because he had shoulder surgery after the regular season. 
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big 12. Started 12 games (219-332-66.0, 2,780, 22 TDs, 6 INTs passing). Played through a hairline fracture in his right fibula during the second half of the season.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, James, played RB at West Texas A&M and for two years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Was the head football coach at Lubbock Monterey and Midland Lee before taking over at Eastland to coach Behren.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Morton is a challenging evaluation given his injury history, but I studied his tape from 2024 and 2025 for my analysis here. He appears to lack the functional arm talent to push the ball into windows or beat safeties over the top into sideline buckets. He’s average with his anticipation and field-reading but is willing to get through progressions while trusting his pocket. He’s extremely tough and has the desired level of competitive spirit needed for the position. He can buy time for his receivers when needed and gets what he can when it’s time to run. Morton’s medicals will be critical, but it will likely be an uphill battle for him to make a roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Very tough, playing through a hairline fracture in his right fibula during the second half of the 2025 season.
  • Adequate velocity on intermediate throws when shoulder was right.
  • Twitchy footwork getting to his platform on RPOs.
  • Willing to give every route progression a chance if needed.
  • Reads conflict points of route combinations and quickly delivers.
  • Adequate ability to extend and create second chances.
profiles.weaknesses:
• At times seemed unable to see lurking coverage versus zone.
  • Gets bogged down when defenses change the picture on him.
  • Needs to throw with better anticipation between the hashes.
  • Lacks feel for back-side pressure mounting.
  • Concerning injury history, missing time in multiple seasons.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted.
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games with 3 starts at RG.
  • 2024: Started 12 games (9 at LG, 3 at RG).
  • 2025: Started the first 7 games at RG. Missed the rest of the season with a left knee injury. Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Schrauth is a two-year starter and team captain with the proper demeanor for “tough guy” work inside. He’s tight in his lowers, creating leverage disadvantages and a lack of body control. He needs to play with quicker hands but has good pop when he lands. His strong hands aid in sustaining run blocks and controlling pass rushers. Heavy feet can’t be coached out of him, creating run-scheme limitations and inconsistent mirroring against athletic interior rushers. His intangibles carry value but could be a bit diminished by concerns about his durability.
profiles.strengths:
• Team captain.
  • Grip strength helps to capture defender’s outside shoulder.
  • Works double teams with sound positioning and steady strain.
  • First contact delivers above-average pop.
  • Stays square and climbs with timing on combo blocks.
  • Strong hands snatch and control rushers on short sets.
  • Able to drop a sudden anchor when necessary.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks quickness/range for back-side cut-off blocks and long pulls.
  • Tardy hands allow opponents to beat up his frame first.
  • Limited bend leads to tall pads and deficient body control.
  • Will have trouble mirroring athletic edge-to-edge rushers.
  • Struggles to open his hips and recover position when beaten.
  • Missed nine games over the last two years due to injury.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Coffeyville Community College): 7 tackles in 6 games.
  • 2022 (Coffeyville Community College): Top 10 JC recruit (50 tackles, 4.5 TFLs, 6 INTs, 8 PBUs in 11 games).
  • 2023 (N.C. State): Played in all 13 games with 4 starts (42 tackles, 2 INTs, 3 PBUs).
  • 2024 (N.C. State): Led team with 8 PBUs. Tied for the team lead with 3 INTs. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (55 tackles, 7 TFLs, FF). 
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten Conference. Tied for seventh in the FBS with 5 INTs-1 returned for TD. Started 10 games (51 tackles, 2.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs). Missed the end of the season due to a knee injury.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Compact, ballhawking safety prospect with alignment versatility. Fitzgerald’s consistency of execution is quite different in coverage versus run support. In coverage, he is assignment-oriented, displaying an adequate mix of route balance and response quickness. He’s clear-eyed to recognize takeaway opportunities and has the ball skills to flip the field. He can match underneath but might not have the speed to stay in-phase if the route travels deep. As a run defender, Fitzgerald plays with urgency but issues diagnosing the play and suspect pursuit angles have led to chunk runs, creating an imbalance that affects his draft grade.
profiles.strengths:
• Interception production has followed him at every stop.
  • Good range from the hash to the boundary underneath.
  • Quick to diagnose and jump in-breakers.
  • Reads, triggers and wraps up quickly on short throws.
  • Thick build with good run-through pop on contact.
  • Possesses an NFL-quality closing burst.
  • Willing to fill and strike as a run defender near the line.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Locks eyes into backfield and loses track of man coverage.
  • Takes time to gather and drive from his pedal.
  • Could struggle carrying speed deep when challenged.
  • Takes poor angles to ball-carriers from depth.
  • Loses track of run-play development when stacked.
  • Below-average playing off blocks to tackle.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Freshman All-American. Started all 14 games at RT. Enrolled in January.
  • 2023: Third-team All-ACC. Started all 13 games at RT.
  • 2024: First-team All-ACC. Started all 14 games (1 at LT, 13 at RT).
  • 2025: First-team All-ACC. Started all 13 games at RT. Set school record for most consecutive starts by a non-specialist (54). Set school record for career snaps (school kept track since 1986).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Storm, signed with Texas A&M as a LB recruit for 2026.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Ultimate iron man at right tackle with 54 career starts. Miller has unusual lateral quickness and fluidity in space despite playing too upright. His hands lack accuracy and command in both phases, but he can recover and make blocks with a finisher’s mindset. Miller is rarely beaten by rush games, but he has his edges attacked because of his hand issues. He will encounter difficulties at the next level without better pad level, core strength and cleaner technique. If he tightens up in those areas, Miller can become a solid NFL right tackle.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “It wasn’t surprising that he played in (Clemson’s) bowl game because he doesn’t opt out of anything or miss any games. Has a team-first mindset.” – AFC regional scout
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses long arms, big hands and quick feet.
  • Fluid and accurate working to linebackers on combo blocks.
  • Snap quickness beats defender’s leverage on play-side and back-side zone blocks.
  • More frame-striker than body-catcher on angle blocks.
  • Able to pull across formation with timing to land a blow.
  • Springs into pass sets with a long initial kick slide.
  • High awareness to twists and games, with pitcher/catcher timing on pass-offs.
  • Feet stay active and slide to mirror rush to the top.
  • Scrambles and recovers thanks to above-average agility.
  • Showed strong speed and explosiveness at pro day.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Unsteady footwork robs him of contact balance.
  • Lunges into contact with upper body instead of well-placed hands.
  • Tall pads and average core strength lead to him being tossed off-balance by force.
  • Hand usage in both phases is often wide, wild and slippery on contact.
  • Inconsistent connection between hands and feet in pass pro.
  • Needs to keep feet closer to the ground to avoid being caught and driven mid-shuffle.
  • Rushers eliminate his outside hand by using basic swipes and wrist control.

profiles.bio:
• 2020-21 (Iowa Western Community College): 12 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 1 sack in 6 games.
  • 2021 (Iowa Western Community College): 45 tackles, 6.5 TFLs, 2 sacks in 11 games.
  • 2022 (Iowa Western Community College): First-team JUCO All-American. 2.5 sacks in the team's win in the NJCAA title game. 45 tackles, 13.5 TFLs, 8.5 sacks in 12 games.
  • 2023: Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (6 tackles).
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 4 starts (14 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack).
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (36 tackles, 2 TFLs, 2 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Jamison-Travis has good size/length with adequate upper-body power but is too often engaged in long-form block battles instead of controlling and defeating the block at the point. He shows first-step and hand-strike quickness, but he’s forced to lean into contact to bolster his base, leaving him unable to move quickly with the design of the play. He can make tackles two gaps away but his rush is unimaginative and in need of openers to get things going.
profiles.strengths:
• Good size and length along the interior.
  • Shows first-step quickness into the neutral zone or gap.
  • Athleticism in his rush is more evident as a 3-technique.
  • Transfers power from hips to hands at the point.
  • Gets hands in first and with consistent placement.
  • Adequate short-area quickness with good closing burst.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inconsistent feel and take-on of angle pressure.
  • Entangled with block in front of him and loses sight of play design.
  • Below average in controlling and shedding at the point.
  • Lacks anchor for desired gap integrity as a run defender.
  • Linear rusher with below-average edge-to-edge movements.
  • Needs to develop go-to moves and counters with his hands.

profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with the height/weight/speed numbers to get a look from the slot despite just a single season of major production. Boyd uses his hands and separation burst to create an opening for his quarterback. He’s unpolished and inefficient as a route-runner but has some potential in that area. While he has deep-ball value when that branch of the route tree is utilized, average hands and below-average ball skills when contested could set him back as he pursues a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Speedy from the slot with explosive athletic testing.
  • Uses inside/out stem to beat leverage and bypass coverage.
  • Effective use of hands to stay clear from grabby defenders.
  • Able to separate laterally and vertically.
  • Good feel for getting his feet down inside the boundary.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hasn’t learned to set up breaks with efficiency.
  • Slow adjusting to off-frame throws.
  • Below-average catch focus underneath.
  • Average as a downfield ball-tracker.
  • Struggles to play through contact and make catches.

profiles.bio:
• 2023 (N.C. State): Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (10 tackles, INT).
  • 2024 (N.C. State): Played in 9 games as a reserve (28 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 5 PBUs).
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (27 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, INT, 5 PBUs, FF). Team's Defensive Newcomer of spring practices, also Co-Newcomer of the spring on special teams.
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Cedric, joined South Carolina as a walk-on DB in 2025.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Teams will be willing to take a chance on Cisse’s explosive athleticism and upside, but a refinement runway might be needed to smooth some of the rougher edges. He’s scheme-versatile in coverage and is an A-rated run supporter. Work ethic and athletic testing will work in his favor. However, a lack of instincts and break anticipation could cost him in coverage against quality route runners. His press will become a more effective weapon with technical work and his route recognition should improve with more reps. Cisse’s traits and competitiveness are clear selling points, but a lack of on-ball production and coverage consistency create a more volatile floor.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “You draft him more for tomorrow’s tools and not for today’s tape. The bad reps are going to get corrected. I like his makeup and his speed.” – AFC national scout
profiles.strengths:
• Explosive athletic ability.
  • Has length and strength to become more disruptive in press.
  • Sits on short routes and squeezes work space from off-man.
  • Quick dig-and-trigger to the throw from the top of his drop.
  • Imposes size on catch point when he’s tight in coverage.
  • Long speed to stay in-phase with deep routes.
  • Supports the run like a box safety.
  • Beats blockers with quickness and meets runners at or near the line.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average in route recognition and break matching from off.
  • Struggles to find playmaking positioning with back to the ball.
  • Below-average tracking and adjustments on downfield 50/50 balls.
  • Needs to more consistently read/react to quarterback’s eyes/operation.
  • Ordinary career production on the ball.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 6 games as a reserve (7 tackles, TFL with 0.5 sack).
  • 2023: Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Played in all 13 games with 1 start (28 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 3 sacks) in the Pop-Tarts Bowl versus Kansas State.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (36 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 0.5 sack, PBU).
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (36 tackles, 7 TFLs with 2 sacks). 
  • Miscellaneous: Cousin, Tyrie Cleveland, played WR at Florida and in the NFL.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Stubby but stout, Cleveland fights hard to muddy the A-gaps. He has heavy hands that shock on impact and he’s capable of quickly controlling/shedding. His lack of length requires him to gain an early advantage or risk being neutralized by big, long guards. Limited range as a run defender and an inability to pressure the pocket cap his draft slotting and upside. Cleveland’s strength and anchor should help him clog interior lanes as a rotational nose tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Thick-boned with broad hips and chest.
  • Burrows low and explodes into double-teams, looking to split them.
  • Hands are twitchy and powerful to jolt and command the block.
  • Presses the block, reads the runner and quickly sheds.
  • Excellent contact balance and sits heavy in his spot through contact.
  • Rarely see him knocked to the ground or even off-balance.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average first-step quickness off the ball.
  • Lateral zone blocks consistently get to seal positioning.
  • Gathered in by physical, longer-armed guards at the point.
  • Sluggish change of direction as a tackler inside.
  • Unable to beat protection to the edges due to slower feet.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Texas): Played in 9 games as a reserve (1-32-32.0).
  • 2023 (Oklahoma): Played in 6 games as a reserve (7-241-34.4, 2 TDs). Missed multiple games due to ankle injury.
  • 2024 (Oklahoma): Played in 11 games with 10 starts (19-230-12.1, 2 TDs). 
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Led team with 1,054 receiving yards (57 receptions, 18.5 per), 6 receiving TDs. Started all 13 games (4-14-3.5, TD rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Thompson is a slightly built, vertical threat with rocket boosters in his shoes. With a career average of 39.8 yards per touchdown catch, there is no denying where his value lives. His acceleration phase is long-lasting, creating easy wins over the top and requiring safety involvement in man coverage. He struggles with traditional, non-vertical routes and finishing contested catches. He’s not a catch-and-run specialist underneath but is dangerous crossing the hashes. He’s dealt with injuries dating back to high school, missing significant time in 2023 due to ankle and hamstring ailments. A lack of size and versatility create challenges for his long-term projection, so diversifying his portfolio of offerings might be necessary for him to stick on a roster long-term.
profiles.strengths:
• One of the fastest players in the draft class.
  • Sudden feet allow shifty release against press.
  • Requires additional attention from coverage over the top.
  • Glides on grass, eating up corners before they can flip and run.
  • Seven of his 10 career touchdowns came on plays of 42+ yards
  • Hash-crossing routes offer him a dangerous post-catch runway.
  • His lone career punt return went for 44 yards in 2025.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Coasts into the top of the route instead of snapping it off.
  • Routes are poorly disguised and lack tempo changes.
  • Small frame sees him bullied at catch-points.
  • Has trouble tracking and adjusting to deep throws.
  • Lacks soft hands and steady catch focus.
  • Uninspiring run-after-catch on hitches and screens.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: SEC All-Freshman Team. Played in all 15 games for the national champions (36-1,620-45.0, long 75, 1 touchback, 18 fair caught, 19 inside the 20). 
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games (32-1,403-43.8, 60 long, 2 touchbacks, 21 fair caught, 14 inside the 20).
  • 2024: Second-team Associated Press All-American. Third-team All-SEC. Finalist for the Ray Guy Award (nation’s top punter). Played in 13 games. Would have ranked fourth in the FBS with 47.6 yards per punt but did not have enough punts to qualify (42-1,998, long 60, 5 touchbacks, 14 fair caught, 22 inside the 20). Suffered a knee injury in the SEC Championship Game.
  • 2025: Won the Ray Guy Award. Second-team Associated Press All-American. Second-team All-SEC. Held out of the season opener as a precautionary measure coming off a knee injury. Played in 12 games (46-2,094-45.5, long 66, 4 touchbacks, 25 fair caught, 23 inside 20).
  • Miscellaneous: Played Australian Rules Football until signing with Georgia as a 21-year-old.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Australian punter with adequate drive power and above-average hang time. Thorson gets good leg extension and has the ability to generate consistent lift, allowing the cover team to swarm when punts are returnable. He displayed vast improvement in touch with his coffin-corner kicks in 2025 and checks the boxes to be a Day 3 pick.
profiles.strengths:
• Plenty of leg to flip the field when he needs to do so.
  • Limits returnable punts and yardage on returns.
  • Vastly improved in keeping pooch punts out of the end zone in 2025.
  • Good pooch-flop technique to create check-ups when it lands.
  • Athleticism and toughness to make tackles if necessary.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Touch-to-toe time needs to be a shade quicker.
  • Hasn’t had to punt in inclement weather often. 
  • Punter-only with no kickoff experience.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve.
  • 2023: Team's Rookie of the Year. Played in 12 games with 7 starts (5 at LT, 2 at RT).
  • 2024: Second-team All-ACC. Team's OL of the Year. Started all 13 games (12 at RT, 1 at LT). 
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. Second-team All-ACC. Started 13 games at RT.
  • Miscellaneous: Grandfather, Barry Parker, played basketball at Bucknell. Cousin, Dereck Lively, played basketball at Duke and was the 12th overall pick of the 2023 NBA Draft.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tackle-to-center prospect with well-composed frame, good body control and sound technique. Parker consistently centers his blocks and operates with inside hands/good grip strength. He gets to his landmarks under control as a move blocker, has average drive strength on gap-scheme blocks and constantly covers his target. His underhook punch has some pepper to it, but below-average length makes timing and anchor essential. He plays with a quality mirror and clearly sees rush games. Parker’s measurables are average but he plays like a future starting center with guard flexibility.
profiles.strengths:
• Should offer immediate C/G roster flexibility.
  • Plays with inside hands and grip strength to latch in.
  • Effective landmarks and timing on cut-offs and climbs.
  • Finds center of block fits using footwork and subtle adjustments.
  • Movements in pass/run are very controlled and balanced.
  • Throws underhook punch with good force.
  • Redirects weight to maintain a fluid protection mirror.
  • Sees rush games developing and quickly responds.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average mass and play strength along the interior.
  • Can be beaten by long defenders.
  • Pushes as drive blocker but lacks drive power in his lowers.
  • Average depth of anchor against power.
  • Will have to quicken his punch pace due to lack of length.
  • Average recovery and redirect once rusher hits his edge.

profiles.overview: Fleischmann is a developmental prospect with above-average athleticism but below-average size and production. He doesn’t always play to his speed but that could change if he can find more reps. He can catch in traffic and through contact but needs to work on route fundamentals to better uncover. Fleischmann probably doesn’t have enough tape to warrant a draft pick, but a team might take a flier on his upside as a practice-squad project.
profiles.strengths:
• Displayed above-average speed/explosiveness at his pro day.
  • Adjusts routes to avoid traffic and contact when possible.
  • Good attention to space and has reliable hands.
  • Flashes some separation speed in the open field.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Two seasons of major playing time and one season of significant catch production.
  • Needs to be quicker in settling and opening to the quarterback underneath.
  • Average body control adjusting to off-frame throws.
  • Lacks size and strength to block in-line at the next level.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Played in 38 for the Oregon baseball team (hit .152, 4 RBIs, 14 runs; 4 stolen bases).
  • 2022: Played in 12 games on special teams as a walk-on (2 tackles). Played in 43 games for the Oregon baseball team (hit .182, 3 RBIs, played second base, center field, right field).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games with 2 starts (37 tackles, 2.5 TFLs with 1 sack, FF). Moved from S to ILB. Started 15 games for the Oregon baseball team (hit .200, 2 HRs, 6 RBIs, 12 runs; 7 stolen bases).
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big Ten Conference. Won the Burlsworth Trophy (nation's top player who began his career as a walk-on). Led team with 94 tackles. Played in all 14 games with 13 starts (8 TFLs with 2 sacks, INT, 4 PBUs, FF). Started 54 games for the Oregon baseball team in center field, named to ABCA/Rawlings Gold Glove Team (no errors in 142 chances). Hit .276, 12 HRs, 35 RBIs, 46 runs; 15 stolen bases.
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big Ten. Ranked sixth in the FBS with 136 tackles. Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Started all 15 games (5.5 TFLs with 1 sack, INT, 6 PBUs).
  • Miscellaneous: Drafted in the 13th round of the 2024 MLB draft by the Houston Astros.
