profiles.overview: Three-year starter whose lack of desired long speed and athleticism could pigeon-hole him into a role as a zone corner or big nickelback. Wright has improved his coverage recognition and is physical when he gets his chance. However, he might not have the short-area movement/burst needed to stay sticky with man routes or make plays on the ball in off coverages. His size and stability underneath could allow him to play closer to the line for a defense that asks him to keep the action in front of him. Wright projects as an average backup.
profiles.strengths:
• Three-year starter and team captain in 2025.
  • Has experience playing outside and inside at nickelback.
  • Displayed improved patience in reading routes from off-man.
  • Communicates well when passing receivers off in zone.
  • Adequate eye balance to adjust coverage to route combinations.
  • Balances high-low route responsibilities in zone.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks coordination and foot quickness to successfully press.
  • Infrequent to locate the ball with his back to the passer.
  • Doesn’t run well enough to make up distance when beaten.
  • Below-average hips to transition smoothly with route breaks.
  • Might not have the burst or short-area quickness to find NFL ball production.
  • Steep pursuit angles cause him to lose contain positioning.

profiles.bio:
• 2023 (Auburn): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (3 tackles).
  • 2024 (Colorado): Played in all 13 games with 1 start (24 tackles, TFL, 2 INTs, 6 PBUs).
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started 12 games (50 tackles, 4.5 TFLs, INT-returned for TD, 8 PBUs, FF).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Brandon, plays RB at Southern Miss. Uncle, Roderick, played DB at Auburn and in the NFL.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Press-man bully with an ability to put his stamp on the first and last phases of the snap. Hood plays with a disruptive punch and gets his hands on most releases, but shifty NFL wideouts could create issues for him. He has enough speed to stay phased on verticals and does a nice job erasing space on in-breakers from tight press or off-man looks. He’s disciplined in zone but route switches still cause occasional missteps. Hood plays with aggression in the catch space, taking top positioning by force. Physicality also shows up in run support, where he triggers downhill with stopping power and finishes like an extra safety. Hood needs to sharpen his instincts/technique, but he has the mentality and upside to become a CB2 in a press-heavy scheme.
profiles.strengths:
• Plays with box-safety physicality in coverage and run support.
  • Punches and suffocates outside release against boundary.
  • Demands the catch space on jump-ball battles.
  • Gathers and triggers with adequate fluidity from depth.
  • Operates with discipline/leverage against high/low route concepts.
  • Explodes vertically with extended arms to capture high-point.
  • Run-defense wiring is exactly what coaches want to see.
  • Above-average stopping power when tackling bigger backs.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Could struggle matching twitchy NFL releases.
  • Hips can get sticky on sudden, aggressive transitions.
  • Grabby at break points or vertical routes when he’s out of phase.
  • Gets too dialed in to receiver and loses track of ball flight.
  • Still developing his instincts from off coverages.
  • Leggy with sluggish change of direction as open-field tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. SEC All-Freshman Team. Played in 12 games with 6 starts at C.
  • 2024: Started all 12 games at C.
  • 2025: Started 7 games at C. Missed the end of the season with an ACL injury.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Lew is a team captain recovering from an ACL injury suffered in October 2025. He’s a natural bender with better foot quickness and athleticism than he shows in the Auburn run scheme. He has strong hands and a strong core to neutralize. He can bump and climb with good fluidity. He’s average as a drive blocker and needs to play with better consistency to mirror the rush without over-setting. His frame and game will continue to improve with time. Lew’s toughness, intelligence and leadership give him a slight grade bump and are core traits that should make him a solid starter.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “A lot of the centers this year don’t translate into our game like Lew will.” - NFC personnel director
profiles.strengths:
• Should continue filling out his frame.
  • Good snap/reach and snap/step quickness.
  • Strong hands and core to neutralize/seal at the point.
  • Athletic but patient when climbing up to linebackers.
  • Plays with desired physicality and finish as a run blocker.
  • Identifies rush front and sets protections.
  • Consistent in re-leveraging his hands when needed.
  • Wrestling background shows up with hip roll to anchor.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Early draft entry and 2025 ACL injury limited his career snap count.
  • Lacks leg drive to uproot and turn an odd-front nose tackle.
  • Average footwork to hit landmarks in wide zone.
  • Needs to play with lighter feet in pass protection.
  • Edges become leaky against rush quickness.
  • Oversets open pathways for inside counters.

profiles.overview: Pure zone-scheme center with good experience but a lack of functional mass and strength. Tollison is well-versed as an outside-zone blocker. He has excellent quickness and footwork to find his landmarks, creating a crease for the runner. He plays with high pads and no drive power as a downhill blocker, though. He could struggle with inside-zone duties. He’s adequate in pass protection but anchoring against bull rushers and finding his footing against NFL games up front will be challenging. Tollison was a solid player at Missouri but he appears to lack the size and versatility the NFL game requires.
profiles.strengths:
• Four-year starter.
  • Impressive get-off/footwork to reach and seal in wide zone.
  • Has ability to adjust on second-level targets.
  • Quick snap-to-punch hand quickness.
  • Lands punch with extension and latches hands in.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Frame is lacking functional mass.
  • Plays with high pads and poor leverage at the point.
  • Discarded quickly by powerful nose tackles.
  • Lacks plays strength to press pass rushers off of him.
  • Inconsistent footwork and set depth defending twists.

profiles.overview: Size, speed and production are check marks in Rucker’s favor. He has good straight-line speed but is average as a route-runner and well below average when it’s time to finish catches. I did not see a lot of improvement from him as a ball-winner over the course of six seasons. While he possesses intriguing talent, it’s hard to imagine Rucker building camp momentum given his inconsistency when it comes to reeling in throws.
profiles.strengths:
• Well-built and showed blazing speed at his pro day.
  • Averaged 72 catches and 1,043 yards in the last two seasons.
  • Works back to the throw on curls and comebacks.
  • Utilizes size and strength to stack corners on go routes.
  • Wins vertically with pure speed or double moves.
  • Gives enough effort as a blocker to help in the run game.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Struggled badly to elude or separate against Arkansas.
  • Below-average deceleration and footwork in shorter spaces.
  • Unable to secure contested catches at an adequate rate.
  • Concerning drop rate has followed him throughout his career.
  • Missed all but two games in 2022 with foot injury that required surgery.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Louisiana Tech): Played in 10 games with 7 starts (22-500-22.7, 4 TDs receiving; 5-8-1.6 rushing; 3-61-20.3 KR).
  • 2023 (Louisiana Tech): Tied for the team lead with 4 receiving TDs (46-778-16.9). Started 11 games (9-186-20.7 KR).
  • 2024 (Texas A&M): Played in 10 games with 5 starts (18-269-14.9, TD).
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Led team with 51 receptions, 674 receiving yards (13.2 per). Tied for third in the FBS with 13 receiving TDs (school single-season record). Started all 13 games (7-20-2.9 rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Slender-framed slot target with field-stretching speed and talent to work all three levels of the field. Allen has elements to improve on as a route-runner, but his sudden acceleration and top-end speed create separation on a consistent basis. He’s a menace on go routes and slot fades. He has adequate hands but will end up on the wrong side of contested catches. Elusiveness after the catch could create additional value for Allen, who could become a productive playmaker as a middle-round pick.
profiles.strengths:
• Puts immediate pressure on defense with burst off the line.
  • Short-route tempo bolsters separation.
  • Excellent top-end speed to separate on go routes and slot fades.
  • Was a consistent winner in one-on-one drills at the Senior Bowl.
  • Quick stick-and-stop on stop routes and quickly transitions from catch to run.
  • Provides run-game support with his run-after-catch talent on slot screens.
  • Slips tacklers in tight quarters with jitterbug quickness.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Will need to prove himself against tight press looks.
  • Rounded routes put quarterback’s throws in harm’s way.
  • Inconsistent balance getting out of sharp breaks.
  • Gets pushed around when sharing the catch space.
  • Average path adjustments when tracking the deep ball.

profiles.bio:
• 2023 (James Madison): Freshman All-American. Second-team All-Sun Belt Conference. Led team with 13 PBUs. Played in all 13 games with starts in the final 10 contests (51 tackles, 2 TFLs, 2 INTs).
  • 2024: First-team All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 9 PBUs. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (55 tackles, 4.5 TFLs, 3 INTs-1 returned for TD, blocked kick; 1-12-12.0 PR).
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 10 PBUs. Named Defensive MVP of both the Peach Bowl and Rose Bowl. Started 15 games for the national champions (61 tackles, 4 TFLs, 2 INTs-1 returned for TD, FF, blocked kick; 1-6-6.0 receiving; 1-33-33.0, TD PR).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Ponds is a productive perimeter cornerback trapped in a smaller body, but he’s not lacking in confidence or coverage tenacity. He’s tremendously competitive and winning seems to follow him at each stop. He matches press releases with good slide quickness and has the speed to stay in-phase as routes travel vertically. Eye discipline, instincts and trigger quickness fuel his zone work and catch disruption. Size limitations will likely push him to nickelback, where mismatches against bigger bodies and physical challenges from run games will test his playmaking/durability. Ponds is a likely Day 2 pick who will be an above-average starting nickelback in the NFL.
profiles.strengths:
• Plays zone with excellent eye discipline, route leverage and spacing.
  • Speed to stay in-phase vertically and rarely loses position once he gains it.
  • Outstanding ball-tracker with the ability to irritate downfield catch points.
  • Diagnoses run, slips blocks and quickly gets to ball-carriers.
  • Consistently finishes tackles against the run and pass.
  • Used impressive acceleration to block two punts while at Indiana.
  • Opened playoff blowout of Oregon with a pick-six on the first play from scrimmage.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Struggles to flip hips cleanly when route leverage is beaten.
  • Loses ground to physical receivers at the top of the route.
  • Average plant-and-drive quickness from top of his drop.
  • Lack of length will cost him pass breakups at times.
  • Can be engulfed by big-bodied blockers near the line.
  • Drag-down tackler in space against bigger wideouts.

profiles.bio:
• High school: Top 10 overall prospect nationally. 
  • 2022: Played in 7 games as a reserve.
  • 2023: Started all 14 games at RG. 
  • 2024: Texas named finalists for the Joe Moore Award (nation's top OL). Started all 16 games at RG.
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started all 13 games at RG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-year starter at right guard with experience against NFL-caliber talent. Campbell is tough, strong and smart, but there are clear athletic limitations that create scheme-dependence and could limit his upside. He lacks functional bend and fluidity in space, which limits his range. He’s adept as a second-phase run blocker, with enough technique to neutralize and sustain in-line. He can also drop a sudden anchor to slow bull rushers. Campbell projects as a gap-scheme guard who can provide depth.
profiles.strengths:
• Outstanding durability as a three-year starter.
  • Lacks ideal height but long arms make up for it.
  • Bends and enters first contact with good leverage.
  • Works feet and hips into position to seal his block.
  • Core strength and quick hand resets stabilize base blocks.
  • Able to step on the brakes when bull rush sees early life.
  • Plays with quick eyes and is poised in the face of rush games.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Comes forward with helmet first and excessive lean.
  • Lacks body control and timing on combo blocks.
  • Success level diminishes when asked to block in space.
  • Rarely cinches up and controls rusher with grip strength.
  • Protection could use better posture and base width.
  • Tight hips limit his ability to recover when beaten.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in 12 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2023: Played in all 12 games as a reserve (7-78-11.1, TD).
  • 2024: Played in 12 games as a reserve (12-142-11.8, 2 TDs).
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (34-319-9.4, 2 TDs). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Rogers is an adequate athlete who possesses the play strength and catch-point savvy to compete for a depth-level role. He needs to play with better short-area urgency on routes underneath, but he has the catch radius to bring in off-target and contested throws. While his effort and technique are inconsistent as a run blocker, he flashes the strength/body control to win reps. Rogers is still developing but should be in the conversation as a Day 3 pick.
profiles.strengths:
• Rarely used vertically but appears to have adequate speed.
  • Controlled footwork to stutter and break at the top of the route.
  • Uses hips to partition off coverage from the catch-point.
  • Showed off better movement talent at Senior Bowl practices than he did on tape.
  • Brings in tall, off-frame throws with his 6-foot-9 wingspan.
  • Leg strength makes him tougher to bring down after the catch.
  • Had some success sealing the edge in run game and mirroring pass rushers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Only one season as a starter in college.
  • Upright through routes and telegraphs what is coming next.
  • Needs to sink, open and present to quarterback with better suddenness.
  • Inconsistent knee bend and reactive mirroring as blocker in space.
  • Hands can come in a little too wide in his base blocks.

profiles.overview: Sheffield is a smallish slot receiver with the speed to challenge defenses on all three levels. He plays fast and has the ability to uncover at an even higher rate over the first two levels with improved route work. In terms of his ball skills, he vacillates between impressive contested grabs and disappointing focus drops. Sheffield’s explosiveness and punt-return potential give him a shot as a backup slot, but his lack of size could limit the amount of suitors willing to give him a long look.
profiles.strengths:
• Accelerates quickly off the snap.
  • Has top-end speed to maintain a lead once he’s in position.
  • Runs routes with good play speed and urgent pace.
  • Flashes impressive competitiveness to make catches in tight traffic.
  • Viable punt-return option with short-area elusiveness.
  • Showed great explosiveness in his pro day athletic testing.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Falls well below the size standards for some NFL teams.
  • Can be lackadaisical instead of aggressively conning coverage in his routes.
  • Would benefit from avoiding so much contact at the top of the route.
  • Needs to tighten route turns to close off undercutting angles for defenders.
  • Body-catcher who suffers from focus drops.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Virginia Tech): Played in 7 games with 1 start (19-208-10.9).
  • 2023 (Virginia Tech): Played in 12 games with 7 starts (28-366-13.1).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts (4 at TE, 2 at WR; 27-394-14.6, 4 TDs). 
  • 2025: Second-team All-SEC. Started all 15 games (39-635-16.3, 5 TDs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Wright is a high-cut, tight-hipped tight end who can stretch the field vertically but lacks fluidity and bend for crisp route breaks from speed. He builds speed to threaten defenses, working the vertical limbs of the route tree. He can gain an advantage on linebackers when aligned outside. He’s big and strong enough to improve as a run blocker but needs better technique and commitment in that area. Wright projects as a Day 3 pick who should fight for a role as a TE3/4.
profiles.strengths:
• Hits man coverage with tempo changes to create space.
  • Builds speed to threatening levels down the seam.
  • Manipulates coverage with aggressive fakes at the stem.
  • Instinctive in finding openings and opportunities in space.
  • Locates safety and adjusts accordingly when working downfield.
  • Searches for yards after catch and will find them.
  • Adjusts in space and lands as a move blocker.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Doesn’t fight hard enough to clear clingy coverage.
  • Clunky getting in and out of intermediate breaks.
  • Inconsistent use of frame to box out defenders.
  • Labors adjusting to low and back-hip throws.
  • Run-blocking technique at the point is below average.
  • Needs to become more consistently competitive as a blocker.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Snow College): Second-team JC All-American. 8-114, 2 TDs in 8 games.
  • 2023: Played in 6 games as a reserve and on special teams (1-5-5.0).
  • 2024: Played in all 12 games with 7 starts (2-15-7.5).
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big 12 Conference. Tied for the team lead with 6 receiving TDs (48-620-12.9). Played in all 13 games with 12 starts.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: With just three catches over his first two seasons at Utah, Bentley’s 48 grabs in 2025 came as a surprise. He has the build of an in-line tight end but mostly uses his size to occupy defenders instead of digging into blocks. A heavy portion of his catches came against zone, so he will need to refine his route running and contested-catch technique to prove he can win on his own. Bentley’s NFL future could depend on his ability to play with more tenacity and technique as a run blocker since his catch production from 2025 might not translate.
profiles.strengths:
• Big target with long wingspan.
  • Adequate timing to the linebacker on work-up blocks.
  • Can cover and stay engaged with second-level targets.
  • Extends and adjusts to retrieve high throws.
  • Above-average focus to bring passes in.
  • Hands are soft but sticky with few unforced drops.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs to work with quicker, inside hands as a run blocker.
  • Inconsistent fitting his run blocks with proper positioning.
  • Below-average drive through contact in his lower half.
  • Plays with a lack of tenacity to sustain blocks for long.
  • Allows closing defenders to eat off his plate when contested.
  • Can be a lumbering route-runner in space.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (3 tackles).
  • 2022: Played in 11 games as a reserve and on special teams (6 tackles, blocked kick).
  • 2023: Tied for third in the FBS with 4 FFs. Started all 13 games (86 tackles, 6 TFLs with 2 sacks, INT, PBU).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Led team with 94 tackles (5 TFLs, 2 PBUs, 2 FFs). Started 11 games.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12. Tied for the team lead with 4 INTs (97 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack, 7 PBUs, FF). Started 12 games.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Dedrick, played football at Howard Payne.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Johnson might be a little light in the measurables department, but his play is tough, twitchy and instinctive. He excels playing in short-zone coverage. He has the athletic ability for man coverage near the line and is quick to read/react to throws in front of him. He’s not an ideal fit as a deep-zone defender, though. Johnson could struggle against vertical speed and big slot receivers in man coverage. He can be swallowed by big blockers as a down safety but has the ability to pile up tackles if they don’t get to him first. Johnson is a Day 3 value as a backup nickelback/safety hybrid with core special-teams talent.
profiles.strengths:
• Loves to make tackles, piling up 277 of them since 2023.
  • Fills run fits as down safety with a quick trigger.
  • Appears to have coverage chops to slide into big nickel when needed.
  • Backpedal and transitions are smooth in space.
  • Properly balanced in reading quarterback and route development. 
  • Instincts and recognition keep him dialed into coverage duties.
  • Wired and built for production on punt/kick cover teams.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Height, weight, length fall below NFL standards.
  • Feels a little small playing inside the box.
  • Struggles to avoid or play off of climbing blocks.
  • Slips in coverage when over-extended beyond his base.
  • Will struggle guarding vertical speed and big tight ends.
  • Tackle slippage derived from his lack of wrap-up length.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 8 games with 1 start at LT.
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games with 1 start at RT in the Texas Bowl loss to Oklahoma State.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games at RT. 
  • 2025: Started all 13 games at RT.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Earnest Jr., played DL at Baylor. Brother, Earnest III, played RB at Kilgore College and Texas A&M.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Traits-based tackle with a coveted blend of size, length and athleticism. Crownover’s technique and fundamentals need significant polish. He converted from tight end to tackle in 2022 and is massive but quick. He can find and fit moving targets as a run blocker, but his pad level runs high, creating inconsistent drive power. He’s light on his feet out of the gate with pass-set quickness to protect his corner, but erratic footwork causes breakdowns and excessive pressures. Crownover has rare traits and a higher floor if everything clicks with coaching, but average swing tackle might be his ultimate landing spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses elite arm length and athleticism for his size.
  • Drops hips and explodes under his hands into drive blocks.
  • Body control and agility allow him to adjust to movement in space.
  • Has the foot quickness to feature more jump-sets as a pro.
  • Can sap a rusher's confidence when punch is timed up.
  • Keeps head tucked and back flat during protection reps.
  • Resets hands to reassert length after falling behind.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Technique is still a work in progress.
  • Operates with tall pad level when fitting up run blocks.
  • Secure block needs better thump before working up on combos.
  • Hands frequently land high and/or outside the frame.
  • Elongated pass slides create openings for inside counters.
  • Lacks feel for pocket depth and set points.
  • Footwork and base width become sloppy when redirecting weight.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (TCU): Freshman All-American. Started all 15 games (27 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, FF).
  • 2023 (TCU): Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Started all 12 games (33 tackles, 5 TFLs with 3 sacks).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (35 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 1 sack, FF).
  • 2025: Played in 12 games with 11 starts (27 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, PBU). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Rotational interior defender capable of playing either tackle spot. Williams is on the short side but possesses good length and an ability to stack and shed blocks as a two-gapper. He lacks lateral quickness and playmaking ability beyond smaller spaces, though. He needs to do a better job with his block take-on against down blocks and double teams. While Williams is capable against the run, his ineffectiveness as a pass rusher could limit his draft stock.
profiles.strengths:
• Unusually long for his height with a wide wingspan.
  • Frame stays clean with well-placed punch and easy arm extension.
  • Quality hand work allows him to navigate around the block.
  • Able to post up and peek in on backfield when two-gapping.
  • Displays twitchy upper body to shed block on demand.
  • Impressive contact balance keeps him off the ground.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Gets beat to the spot and sealed by lateral blocks.
  • Needs better feel and take-on plan against doubles teams.
  • Inconsistent keeping pads square through engagement. 
  • Lacks plan and production as a pass rusher.
  • Below-average bend and agility to capture moving quarterbacks.

profiles.overview: Villari is a multi-purpose move tight end with competitive spirit and appealing upside. He’s a former quarterback who has grown into his frame. He’s not strong enough to block in-line, but he has the wiring and effort to project as a space blocker from the slot. The route-running fundamentals are behind but coachable, while his hands and catch radius are already working for him. He has average speed and excellent catch toughness. Villari’s gadget versatility on direct snaps adds a fun twist, but refining his talent as a pass-catcher will determine his long-term value.
profiles.strengths:
• Dynamic skill set with talent to catch, run and pass.
  • Alters speed to sneak separation at break points.
  • Tough in traffic with strong hands to secure combat catches.
  • Can operate zone-read and throw out of that look.
  • Rarely stopped on short-yardage carries.
  • Determined and willful once the ball is in his hands.
  • Shows some strain when connected to a block.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Behind the curve with receiving fundamentals.
  • Still learning to generate leverage as a route-runner.
  • Needs to play with quicker sink-and-show on stop routes.
  • Allows clingy coverage too much leeway into his catch space.
  • Requires more work in the weight room as a blocker.
  • Needs to play with inside hands and better placement.

profiles.overview: Possession receiver with limited range and explosiveness to threaten NFL corners. Key is a detail-oriented route-runner with natural ball skills and soft hands. However, he struggles to beat press, lacks the vertical speed to push cornerbacks onto their heels and is unable to prevent a high rate of contested looks. Key’s best shot will be as a big slot receiver working as a zone-beater, but a lack of special-teams value shrinks his roster chances.
profiles.strengths:
• Shows attention to detail in his route-running.
  • Gets out of his breaks at crisp angles to create space.
  • Catches the point of the football with soft, sticky hands.
  • Makes grabs in heavy traffic without blinking.
  • Possesses excellent awareness of the sideline.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Play strength doesn’t appear to match his listed size.
  • Missing the foot quickness to quickly skip and slide past press.
  • Struggles to ward off physical man coverage. 
  • Unable to open NFL catch windows with burst out of breaks.
  • Lack of vertical speed and second gear shows up on tape.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve (17 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, INT, PBU).
  • 2023: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Played in all 13 games with 3 starts (26 tackles, 6 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, PBU, 2 FFs).
  • 2024: Played in all 16 games with 14 starts (42 tackles, 13 TFLs with 8.5 sacks, INT, 3 PBUs, 2 FFs).
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten. Led FBS with 3 blocked kicks. Led team with 3 FFs. Started all 13 games (42 tackles, 12 TFLs with 8.5 sacks, 3 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Dennis-Sutton is a base defensive end with toughness. He’s effective against the run, but he has limited pass-rushing upside. His predictable, linear rush lacks the burst and bend to beat tackles to the top of the rush and flatten into the pocket. He uses hand violence and brute force to challenge tackles with weak anchors. He’ll get bounced around because his pad level is too high, but he’s tough to finish and finds his way to the action when it’s near him. Dennis-Sutton is equipped to muddy running lanes but might not make many impact plays. He has average upside as an odd- or even-front end.
profiles.strengths:
• Heavy hands jolt tackles and create space to operate in both phases.
  • Uses up-and-over arm action to clear the inside edge.
  • Smooth inside spin opens rush-lane opportunities.
  • Can slide laterally with zone blocks and redirect through them against cutbacks.
  • Displays powerful pull-and-shed technique at the point.
  • Takes on heavy contact but stays in the fight.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Plodding upfield rush lands down the middle of the tackle.
  • Limited bend to flatten and shrink the pocket.
  • Slow to counter when rush stalls at the top.
  • Plays with elevated pad level throughout the rep.
  • Lacks tackle range and can be wiggled into misses by runners.
  • Needs discipline to cut down roughing penalties.

profiles.overview: Broad-framed four-year starter during stints at Troy and North Carolina. King is a scheme-dependent right guard with the pure power to displace opponents and clear downhill run lanes. His effectiveness plummets when asked to venture beyond what is in front of him. He has the size, length and anchor to sit firm against a bull-rush, but athletic rushers with functional counters might always be his nemesis. King displayed improved technique, but his level of pro success could be tied directly to playing at a lighter weight to improve his short-area quickness.
profiles.strengths:
• Girthy frame with drive power to displace defenders.
  • Gets into short pulls with adequate footwork.
  • Pass protects with good base width and square pads.
  • Displays adequate recognition of rush games up front.
  • Length/strength to redirect defenders who find his edge.
  • Unlocks lower half to sink a firm anchor when needed.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average short-area movement limits his range.
  • Struggles getting to cut-off blocks and second-level landmarks.
  • Fairly average thump on initial contact for his size.
  • Average punch quickness and hand usage in pass pro.
  • Below-average slide quickness to seal gaps against athletic rushers.

profiles.overview: Sobkowicz’s production stands out, but his pro-day speed was disappointing and he needs to refine his route-running. His elite short-area change of direction could allow him to run more complex routes from the slot if a team decides to give him a shot inside. He’s not fast but his touchdown production and certain elements of his athletic profile give him a chance of being drafted late on Day 3.
profiles.strengths:
• Averaged 77 catches for 1,060 yards and 12.7 TDs over the past three seasons.
  • Plus early acceleration and short-area quickness.
  • Can stick a foot in the ground and break sharply for complex routes.
  • Above-average execution of his double moves.
  • Pummelled opposition with fade-route wins near the goal line.
  • Above-average body control when elevating to catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Showed below-average speed at his pro day.
  • Too upright getting into his route breaks.
  • Focus drops pop up each year on tape.
  • Could struggle against press corners.
  • Lacks separation needed to play outside.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Maryland): Played in all 13 games with 1 start in the Pinstripe Bowl (22 tackles).
  • 2022 (Miami): Started all 12 games (27 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, PBU).
  • 2023: Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve (3 tackles). Did not receive a waiver to play from the NCAA in the regular season after transferring from Miami because he did not enter the transfer portal and had previously transferred schools. 
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 12 games (32 tackles, 4 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, PBU, FF).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 12 games (45 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: While he’s an enormous interior presence with impressive physical features, Jackson’s inconsistencies are partially rooted in flawed fundamentals and technique. He plays too upright and with inconsistent base width/block take-on, making him more easily cleared from gaps. He might never become a tree stump at the point, but he could see vast improvement in his shed-and-control with quicker hands, improved upper-body power and a full-time move to odd-front end. The tape is uneven with a floor of average backup, but Jackson’s size and length could be considered unmined gold by some teams.
profiles.strengths:
• Enormous presence in the middle with proportional build.
  • Giant hands at the end of long arms spanning a 7-foot-2 wingspan.
  • When he attacks blocks properly, he can consume two gaps.
  • Can reach out and slow runners with an arm even when he’s being blocked.
  • Uses his length and leg drive to crank up bull rush on centers.
  • Moves well enough to bring down the quarterback once he’s in the pocket.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Plays with tight hips and a narrow base relative to his frame.
  • Needs quicker hands and better upper-body power to control blockers.
  • Blockers can crowd his frame and uproot his anchor to clear him out.
  • Below-average core power and contact balance for power swaps.
  • Movement is mechanical and lacking athletic flow.
  • Hasn’t learned to weaponize his length as a rusher.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Stanford): Freshman All-American. Team's Most Outstanding Freshman. Played in 11 games with 9 starts (46 tackles, 8.5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, 2 FFs).
  • 2023 (Stanford): Led team with 6 TFLs, 5 sacks. Played in 10 games with 5 starts (34 tackles).
  • 2024 (Stanford): Ranked fourth in the FBS with 5 FFs. Led team with 8 TFLs, 7 sacks. Played in 12 games with 2 starts (31 tackles, PBU).
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. Big 12 Conference DL of the Year, Newcomer of the Year. Finalist for the Lombardi Award (nation's top lineman). Tied for the FBS lead with 14.5 sacks, ranked second with 19.5 TFL. Played in all 14 games with 13 starts (3 PBUs, 3 FFs).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, DJ, played DE at Harvard.  

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Bailey is extremely hard for linemen to stay in front of. He moves like a slashing two guard, blending explosiveness and fluidity to slip, bend and flow around blocks from multiple angles. His leverage and lower-body flexion create game-over scenarios once he reaches pocket depth with even a minor lead. He can be stalled when a blocker latches his hands in deep, but Bailey’s elusiveness and suddenness make clean clamps a relative rarity. He’s instinctive with natural mid-rush counters, but he must continue developing hand usage and crafting rush plans for when protection shifts his way. Teams can run at Bailey due to his lack of anchor and take-on presence, but his work-around quickness will also lead to tackles for loss. His draft grade is slightly tempered by a lack of desired size/length, but the explosiveness and athletic talent is truly elite. His sack production should carry over to the NFL as an odd-front rush linebacker with Pro Bowl upside.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “Best rusher in the draft. No doubt. But I worry about his size and toughness. If you are taking him high, you need him to play on all three downs.” – AFC executive
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses rare short-area twitch and reactive agility.
  • Makes a lot of plays behind the line of scrimmage.
  • Explosive take-off leaves tackle little margin for error out of his stance.
  • Widens rush track on second step to create space at the corner.
  • Builds speed and momentum as the rush ripens.
  • Has the lean, bend and cornering to shrink-wrap the pocket.
  • Natural rush instincts with quick reaction to blocker’s pass sets.
  • Stacks an outside counter on top of his speed-to-power charge.
  • Fights through redirect blocks to stay connected to his track.
  • Able to flip hips and shoulders to play quickly around run blocks.
  • Runs well and squeezes pursuit angles wide.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Finesse approach against the run due to lack of size/power.
  • Can be caved in or torqued out by kick-outs.
  • Missing escape strength once he's stuck on contact.
  • Average recognition of screens and misdirection.
  • Hand accuracy on swipes and chops is inconsistent.
  • Will need to develop inside counters to exploit oversets.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (West Chester): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (West Chester): Played in all 11 games with 8 starts (39 tackles, 13 TFLs with 5 sacks, FF).
  • 2023 (Louisiana Tech): Played in 10 games with 1 start (16 tackles).
  • 2024 (Louisiana Tech): First-team All-Conference USA. Led team with 10.5 TFLs, 6.5 sacks. Started all 12 games (46 tackles).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Played in 13 games with 9 starts (28 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, PBU). Missed 3 games due to injury.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Blay is a slightly undersized nose tackle who climbed from Division II to Conference USA and finally to Miami, where he played for a national title. He takes on single blocks with adequate power to press and separate, but he can be wiped out by double-teams or angle pressure. He’s quick to close the distance on quarterbacks when he gets some breathing room but lacks early explosion and hand work to quickly open doors. Blay’s path to a roster might come as an undrafted free agent.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses adequate wingspan and good hand size.
  • Plays with solid upper-body power.
  • Good reaction quickness to lateral movement off the snap.
  • Quick to press and separate from blocks at the point of attack.
  • Locates ball-carriers and works off blocks toward the action.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Only one season of plus production on FBS level.
  • Below-average mass for duties at nose tackle.
  • Gets pushed around by double-teams and down blocks.
  • Allows pad level to rise during some engagements.
  • Doesn’t have opening moves to unlock his pass rush.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Washington State): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (Washington State): Played in 9 games with 1 start (11 tackles, TFL, PBU).
  • 2023 (Washington State): Started 11 games (30 tackles, 2 TFLs with 0.5 sack). 
  • 2024 (Washington State): Started 12 games (21 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs). 
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (12 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Devon, played football at Kentucky and Cal-Davis.  

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Gusta has adequate size and good power but he’s not a true gap-control nose tackle and lacks production from a stem-heavy front. He’s an active, effort-based defender who is capable of fighting for his space against single blocks, but his take-on against double teams is average. First-step quickness and violent hands can create pocket pressure despite a low career sack total, though. Gusta has a chance to fight for a spot as a 1-technique.
profiles.strengths:
• Girthy through hips, thighs and calves.
  • Displays power to punch and steer blocks aside.
  • Plays with consistent force and effort on each snap.
  • Fights to beat cut-offs and maintain gap integrity against wide zone.
  • Plays with the same force and effort when fatigued.
  • Violent clubs, slaps and rips are part of his rush package.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Career production underwhelmed.
  • Lacks length to keep big bodies from crowding into his frame.
  • Puts up a fight, but lacks true gap-control technique.
  • Base narrows as a move rusher, leading to balance losses.
  • Short levers make it harder to flip the edge and find the pocket.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Mississippi): Played in all 13 games with 10 starts (37 tackles, 5 PBUs).
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (59 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 5 PBUs). 
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Led team with 9 PBUs. Tied for the team lead with 2 INTs. Started all 16 games for the national champions (45 tackles, 2 TFLs, 2 INTs).
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big Ten. Tied for the team lead with 2 INTs. Started all 14 games (53 tackles, 6 PBUs).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Desmond, played safety at Rutgers.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Igbinosun is an iron man with 53 career starts, fitting the mold of a press corner with good size and long arms. He uses heavy hands and strength to reroute receivers, staying tight on most vertical routes. However, hip tightness, disjointed footwork and average route recognition make pattern-matching a chore in larger spaces or in off-man coverage. Improving his technique and getting him to trust it will be critical in reducing penalties. He is tough, strong and a willing run defender. Traits raise the ceiling to CB2 in a zone-heavy scheme, but his floor as an average backup might be a more likely outcome.
profiles.strengths:
• Carries imposing frame with long arms.
  • Can delay press release with heavy hands.
  • Chokes off landing space on go balls down the sideline.
  • When he’s in position, few catches will be finished.
  • Better technique could unlock a higher ceiling.
  • Ready to fill or set edges depending on what is needed.
  • Proactively looks for chances to support the run.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Finished career with a jaw-dropping 30 penalties, per PFF.
  • Reaches and grabs when route adversity strikes.
  • Lacks fluidity in hips and feet to stay sticky in man.
  • Struggles to recover cleanly when leverage is beaten.
  • Still waiting for him to turn and find the football in flight.
  • More shoulder strikes than wrap-ups in run support.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 14 games as a reserve for the national champions (13 tackles, PBU).
  • 2023: Started all 14 games (29 tackles, 3 TFLs, INT, 5 PBUs).
  • 2024: Third-team All-SEC. Led team with 3 INTs. Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Started all 14 games (58 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs).
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Led team with 10 PBUs. Started 13 games (50 tackles, INT).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Donovan, played DL at Elon and Mercyhurst.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Smooth athlete with good size, length and foot agility as an inside/outside option. Everette started 41 games at Georgia, including several high-leverage affairs. He’s well-built with run-through pop when he wants to dial it up. He’s controlled and patient from press, forcing wider release stems, and does a nice job of mirroring breaks when in-phase. Everette appears to lack make-up speed and sudden acceleration from transitions, so when he gets behind, he tends to stay behind. He’s willing in run support but is more of a drag-down tackler. Everette’s traits are differentiators, but he might lack stickiness against NFL quickness and speed.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “Good size, good hips and willing against the run. I see him as a run-support nickelback.” - AFC regional scout
profiles.strengths:
• Sturdy, thick boundary cornerback with good length.
  • Stays square and waits for release declaration from press.
  • Effective reading and jumping routes from short zones.
  • Agile feet create efficient footwork in pattern matching.
  • Anticipates breaks and blankets comebacks from tight man.
  • Had interceptions in each of the last two SEC title games.
  • Presses the line and sets the edge when uncovered.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Allows too many easy pitch-and-catch throws in front of him.
  • Average acceleration out of transitions.
  • Lacks desired recovery speed when beaten.
  • Grabs and holds become easy calls.
  • Needs better breakdown and control as an open-field tackler.
  • Drag-down tackler with consistently high entry points.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Washington State): Honorable Mention All-Pac-12 Conference. Started all 13 games (44-471-10.7, 5 TDs). Enrolled in January.
  • 2022 (Washington State): Led team with 602 receiving yards (51 receptions, 11.8 per), 5 receiving TDs. Started 12 games.
  • 2023 (Oklahoma State): Started the first 4 games (14-198-14.1, TD). Missed the rest of the year with a wrist injury suffered in bye-week practice.
  • 2024 (Oklahoma State): Led team with 882 receiving yards (52 receptions, 17.0 per, 6 TDs). Played in all 12 games with 11 starts.
  • 2025: Led team with 6 receiving TDs (55-811-14.7). Started all 15 games.
  • Miscellaneous: Uncle is former pro wrestler Don "The Rock" Muraco. Father, Karlos, spent 17 years in the Marines.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Long-striding, vertical-access wideout with steady play and production. Stribling has good size and early acceleration to climb over the top of coverage but lacks short-area quickness to gain separation underneath. His downfield ball skills are above average but he struggles to consistently carve out catch space and fight through contested-catch contact for tight-coverage wins. He has legit speed after the catch once he finds open grass. He’s also one of the most competitive run blockers in the WR class. Stribling projects as an immediate WR4 who could eventually work his way into a starting role.
profiles.strengths:
• Good initial acceleration into his routes.
  • Pays attention to break routes off at crisp angles.
  • Smooth late adjustments to grab advantages downfield.
  • Able to meet throws with good hand extension.
  • Builds speed quickly after catch for chunk plays.
  • Fits into block targets and fights to stick around.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Linear route movements lack unpredictable elements.
  • Leggy with a lack of separation burst from breaks underneath.
  • Average hip sink getting into intermediate cuts.
  • Needs to play with greater fight when contested.
  • Inconsistent finishing his catches through contact.

profiles.bio:
• 2020: Played in 4 games as a reserve (3 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack). Enrolled in January.
  • 2021: Played in 5 games as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve (12 tackles, 2 TFLs).
  • 2023: Played in 12 games as a reserve (15 tackles, 5 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU, FF) behind a stacked DL, including 2024 NFL Draft picks Tyler Davis and Ruke Orhorhoro.
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Played in 11 games with 6 starts (21 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 2 PBUs). Missed most of spring with an ankle injury that lingered into the season. Arrested in February for unlawful possession of a firearm on university property. Also charged with failure to exercise due care while operating a motor vehicle.
  • 2025: Played in 12 games with 6 starts (21 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Capehart started just 12 games over six seasons (and 57 games played) but that’s not an indicator of the impact he can make against the run. He’s big, broad and long with heavy hands and impressive power in his upper half. He can play through lesser guards and adequately occupy his gap against double-teams. He’s light on his feet with good lateral movement but is unrefined as a pass rusher, relying on down-the-middle power. Capehart is not a young prospect, but his traits and run-plugging talent will appeal to teams looking for a solid rotational option on Day 3.
profiles.strengths:
• Thick-bodied with good length.
  • Strikes quickly from leveraged position with heavy hands.
  • Lifts, presses and muscles through blockers.
  • Surprising first step laterally to match zone-block steps.
  • Eats blocks and maintains footing with plus contact balance.
  • Has foot quickness for activation in rush games.
  • Able to generate some pocket push when he’s singled up.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Wins with will over technique at the point.
  • Needs better feel for angle blocks on his edge.
  • Lacks hand usage and openers as a pass rusher.
  • Rarely gets to a workable counter off his bull rush.
  • Comes in too high and slides off of tackle tries.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Hutchinson Community College): 21 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, 2 INTs, 2 PBUs.
  • 2022: Played in all 12 games as a reserve and on special teams (19 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, PBU).
  • 2023: Started the first 5 games (19 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, PBU). Missed the rest of the year due to injury.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (71 tackles, TFL, INT, 3 PBUs).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started 12 games (70 tackles, 4 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 INTs, 4 PBUs).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, DJ, plays WR at Nebraska.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Singleton is a big, long safety best suited for condensed spaces. He sees the field with clear eyes in zone and is assignment-oriented when matching up on tight ends. He isn’t quick enough to stay in phase with NFL wideouts and lacks the instincts/closing burst to consistently finish on the football from depth. It makes sense to play him near the line in run support, as his downhill pursuit angles are often frenetic and come at too high a risk. Special-teams value could be the key to him making a roster as a fourth safety.
profiles.strengths:
• Teammates voted him a single-digit jersey – signifying one of the team’s 10 toughest players – for three consecutive years.
  • Assignment-oriented with discipline to find his coverage.
  • Recovers nicely when cross-faced by in-breaking routes.
  • Adequate field vision and communication from zone.
  • Slows the run game as an add-on defender in the box.
  • Length allows him to make pursuit tackles from a distance.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks man-cover tools against wideouts.
  • Average burst to close from zone perch.
  • Below-average range to play over the top.
  • Comes in way too hot as a downhill run supporter.
  • Off-balance as an open-field tackler.

profiles.overview: Good tester with average size and steady production over the last three seasons. Connors typically gains what is blocked for him, but he can be indecisive without a clear entry point and lacks above-average elusiveness in space. Connors has decent burst once he hits the gas and builds to top speed quickly to eliminate tackle angles toward the perimeter. His receiving totals are primarily a function of leak-out catches and swing passes. Connors is steady and reliable but will need to carve out a clearly defined role to stick on an NFL roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Showed good combination of speed and leaping ability at pro day.
  • Makes first- and second-level cuts without losing speed.
  • Able to hit his top speed quickly in the open field.
  • Keeps runs tight off the hips of blockers to maximize space.
  • Small catch radius but makes impressive adjustments to off-frame throws.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks suddenness in the early stages of the run.
  • Will dance and wait in search of clear points of entry.
  • Average wiggle in short spaces to elude defenders.
  • Takes time to hit it north/south on swings and screens.
  • Lacks functional anchor to block blitzing linebackers.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Purdue): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (1-26-26.0 receiving; 2-3-1.5 rushing).
  • 2022 (Purdue): Played in all 14 games with 1 start (15-149-9.9 receiving; 1-4-4.0 rushing; 14-278-19.9 KR).
  • 2023 (Purdue): Led team with 47 receptions, 629 receiving yards (13.4 per), 7 receiving TDs. Started all 12 games (4-12-3.0 rushing).
  • 2024: Led team with 3 receiving TDs (31-245-7.9). Started 5 games (5-32-6.4 rushing). Missed most of the season with an injury and suffered a concussion in return. Donated $50 per reception to Rob's Ranch, a non-profit to help people with drug and alcohol addiction. 
  • 2025: Started all 13 games (57-620-10.9, 4 TDs receiving).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year slot receiver who is savvy against zone coverage and crafty after making a catch. Burks does a good job of utilizing his straight-line speed when the ball is in his hands. He struggles to win on vertical routes, though. He creates windows underneath by crisply breaking off short routes. He’s a compact, short-armed target who secures catches through contact. However, his production left something to be desired during his time at Purdue and Oklahoma. Comebacks and curls are often swallowed. Coaching and route work could lead to improvement in those areas. Burks lacks standout measurables, but better quarterback play could unlock a more productive player.
profiles.strengths:
• Shaves in-breaking routes with disciplined, tight cuts.
  • Loose hips allow for smoother adjustments to back-hip throws.
  • Displayed vast improvement to finish combat catches.
  • Squares numbers to quarterback and frames his catch point.
  • Plays with pro footwork, dropping both feet near the boundary.
  • Spatial awareness present in route breaks and zone landings.
  • Crafty runner on jet sweeps and after the catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Play speed doesn’t always align with timed speed.
  • Lacks convincing push to sell his curls/comebacks.
  • Short arms put him at a disadvantage on 50/50 balls.
  • Early head turns shorten his drive phase on deep routes.
  • Waits for throws outside the numbers to come to him instead of attacking them.

profiles.overview: Lemieux is very athletic and will have no issues as a pulling center or in getting to his landmarks on outside zone. He’s low-cut and can fit up blocks with leverage but needs to add more bulk. His pass protection is a concern -- even inside. He will need to improve his footwork and patience in order to protect at a functional level as a pro.
profiles.strengths:
• Muscular physique with good lean mass.
  • Athletic with ability to find cut-off positioning as a zone blocker.
  • Pass slides with quick, staccato steps that stay low to the ground.
  • Displays vision and awareness for clean pass-offs versus twists.
  • Explodes his hips and hands into defenders on contact.
  • Good pad level and lift on opponents as a drive blocker.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Too much lunging at rushers on his edge.
  • Will get beaten to the punch too often in pass pro.
  • Needs more mass to withstand an interior bull rush.
  • Difficult for him to stay wide and centered on moving blocks.
  • Rarely clamps hands in or brings opponent tight for control.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 10 games as a reserve (14-57-4.1 rushing).
  • 2023: Led team with 586 rushing yards (137 carries, 4.3 per), 5 rushing TDs. Played in 10 games with 2 starts (3-35-11.7 receiving; 10-284-28.4, TD KR).
  • 2024: Third-team All-ACC RB/All-Purpose. Led team with 1,049 rushing yards (228 carries, 4.6 per), 11 rushing TDs. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts (23-254-11.0, 2 TDs receiving; 11-277-25.2, TD KR).
  • 2025: Second-team All-ACC. Led team with 907 rushing yards (179 carries, 5.1 per), 10 rushing TDs. Started 12 games (28-140-5.0 receiving; 1-18-18.0 KR).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Claiborne is a twitched-up, elusive slasher who can turn minimal gains into explosive runs. He's creative in tight quarters, using lateral agility and sudden feet to escape trouble. While willing to run between the tackles, his lack of size and strength limits his effectiveness in that area. His unpredictable nature -- sometimes pulling runs off-track when profit is available -- might frustrate coaches, but it also generates unexpected chunk plays. He projects as a middle-round, change-of-pace option and complementary back who can inject much-needed juice into a dull, predictable running game.
profiles.strengths:
• Displays adequate blend of patience and urgency as a runner.
  • Hyper-twitchy with ability to plant and cut in an instant.
  • Elite burst to rocket past linebackers and onto third level.
  • Speed to outflank tacklers wide and/or break away in the open field.
  • Makes linebackers pay for missed run fits.
  • Stacks moves, making him hard to dial in on for tacklers.
  • Experienced kick returner with two career touchdowns.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Herky-jerky running style, lacking desired tempo for wide zone.
  • Modest run strength and takes on heavy contact between tackles.
  • Doesn’t run with complete buy-in or trust of the run blocking.
  • Ball security became an issue in 2025.
  • Has stiff hands as a pass-catcher and struggles in blitz pickup.
  • Does too much stutter-stepping as a kick returner.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted. Played in 4 games with 1 start (2-15-7.5 receiving; 1-2-2.0 rushing).
  • 2023: Played in 14 games with 1 start for the national runners-up (5-51-10.2 receiving; 5-28-5.6 PR).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games (63-834-13.2, 9 TDs receiving; 12-80-6.7 PR).
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten. Led team with 62 receptions, 881 receiving yards (14.2 per). Tied for ninth in the FBS with 11 receiving TDs. Played in 12 games with 11 starts (8-104-13.0, TD PR).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Andrew, played WR at Eastern Washington.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Two-year starter with elite ball skills that should supersede athletic/speed limitations. A Puka Nacua comparison might feel strong, but like Nacua, Boston enters the draft with speed/separation concerns and outstanding competitive toughness. Boston gets off the line with good burst and maintains his top speed throughout the route. He could have issues beating press, but releases can also be schemed. He’s very skilled when it comes to winning jump balls and contested throws. Boston also knows how to win in the red zone. Acclimating to NFL competition could take a year, but Boston has the makeup to become a productive possession target with above-average red-zone value.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “I don’t think speed concerns are valid. Anyway, you don’t have to be fast when you are as good as he is when guarded.” – NFC scouting director
profiles.strengths:
• Good early acceleration and plays faster than timed speed.
  • Runs routes with good fluidity.
  • Big-bodied target who plays to his size.
  • Leans on defenders without sacrificing catch readiness.
  • Scored 20 TDs over the last two seasons, proving himself a red-zone mismatch.
  • Pro-caliber ball skills with elite hand strength to finish.
  • Extends for off-frame throws with a spider web-like catch radius.
  • Ball tracking and adjustment timing are top notch.
  • Competitive and strong with his run-after-catch ability.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Production dipped when the competition level rose.
  • Press release is linear and will give NFL CBs opportunities to get hands on him.
  • Flashes early burst but lacks a true second gear.
  • Routes lose steam when he digs his foot in on route turns.
  • Earned separation closes as the route progresses.
  • Might need formation help and stacks/motion to free his releases.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in 11 games with 4 starts (51 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, 4 PBUs).
  • 2023: Started 11 games (67 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, 4 PBUs). Missed 3 midseason games due to an ankle injury.
  • 2024: Third-team All-SEC (76 tackles, 6.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, INT, 4 PBUs, FF). Started 11 games. Missed the final 2 games with a lower-leg injury. Team captain.
  • 2025: Second-team All-SEC. Led team with 89 tackles. Started all 15 games (4.5 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, 4 PBUs, 2 FFs). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Lawson is twitchy and covers ground quickly when scraping to the football or knifing inside to disrupt as a run blitzer. His quick flow and pursuit is countered by a lack of play recognition/patience that can place him in the wrong place at the wrong time. He’s much better at slipping blocks than he is at taking them on. He has the reactive agility to become an above-average open-field finisher, but his wrap-and-drive fundamentals run hot and cold. Lawson’s athleticism shows up in man coverage and when expanding his zone influence. He projects as a run-and-chase Will linebacker with three-down potential but a limited ceiling.
profiles.strengths:
• Two-time team captain.
  • Rapid feet to scrape quickly across the front.
  • Fast trigger and burst allow him to dart into gaps.
  • Sudden and quick-footed as a block slipper.
  • Flows wide and meets lead blocks with a forceful lead shoulder.
  • Reactive athlete who can slide and match a back’s cut decisions.
  • Plus range to expand his zone capabilities. 
  • Elusive blitzer who can stress pass protection.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average pre-snap recognition against motion and movement.
  • A beat late keying blockers and racing to the junction point.
  • Limited feel for blocking schemes leads to inefficient movement.
  • Below-average hand pop to stack and shed climbing blocks.
  • Below-average stopping power and wrap-up consistency as a tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 14 games as a reserve (8 tackles, 2 sacks, PBU).
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in all 15 games as a reserve for the national champions (34 tackles, 6 TFLs with 5 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Started 12 games (23 tackles, 6 TFLs with 4 sacks, 2 PBUs).
  • 2025: First-team All-Big Ten. Led team with 10.5 TFLs, 10 sacks. Started 12 games (30 tackles, 3 PBUs, 2 FFs). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Edge prospect with good size and length. Moore is far more active and engaged as a rusher than he is as a run defender. He has the ability to set firm edges, but his approach against the run can lack urgency. Against the pass, Moore is a bull-rush aficionado, piling up pressures and sacks. He’s strong through the top of the rush but needs to prove he can consistently stress long, well-anchored tackles. When it’s time to finish, he tackles with reliable technique and timing. If Moore cranks up the fire on all three downs, he can become a good full-time player. Either way, he projects as a starter capable of racking up pressures.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “I like that he knows what he does well as a rusher and capitalizes on it.” – AFC national scout
profiles.strengths:
• Good size and length as a rusher.
  • Leveraged hand strike and leg drive propel his bull rush.
  • Downhill momentum is hard to stop once it starts.
  • Gets into the top of the rush with good forward lean.
  • Swallows quarterbacks and runners like a crashing wave once he’s close.
  • Above-average football IQ and awareness of play design.
  • Capable of holding his ground at the point of attack.
  • Plays with a smooth connection between his hands and feet.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Occasionally lacks energy and urgency as a run defender.
  • Rides on blocks instead of working quickly off of them.
  • Average quickness to stack, shed and pursue to the sideline.
  • Below-average first-step quickness in his upfield rush.
  • Limited hand counters cause rush to sputter if he fails to gain early advantage.
  • Lacks knee bend and upper-body swivel while working the turn.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Western Carolina): Second-team All-Southern Conference. SoCon Freshman of the Year. Finished sixth in the voting for the Jerry Rice Award (top FCS freshman). Led team with 826 rushing yards (119 carries, 6.9 per). Tied for the team lead with 4 rushing TDs. Played in 10 games with 1 start (21-212-10.1, TD receiving).
  • 2023 (Western Carolina): First-team All-Southern Conference. Led team with 897 rushing yards (131 carries, 6.8 per), 13 rushing TDs. Played in 8 games with 7 starts (21-283-13.5 receiving). Missed games due to injury.
  • 2024: Second-team Associated Press All-American All-Purpose. First-team All-ACC All-Purpose/RS, Honorable Mention RB. Ranked ninth in the FBS with 1,704 all-purpose yards. Led team with 966 rushing yards (184 carries, 5.3 per), 5 rushing TDs. Tied for the team lead with 52 receptions (579 yards, 11.1 per, 4 TDs). Started 11 games (13-159-12.2, TD PR). Missed 2 games due to injury.
  • 2025: Played in 7 games with 6 starts (60-278-4.6, 2 TDs rushing; 23-317-13.8, 2 TDs receiving; 5-105-21.0, TD PR). Missed games because of leg/ankle injuries, though he attempted to play through them.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Reid is a small, versatile back who made a significant impact on games despite missing time due to injury in both of his seasons at Pitt. He’s listed as a running back but finding manufactured touches no matter the alignment will be the goal. Slot snaps are likely, but his value often rests in his ability to become a “second slot” when running routes out of the backfield. The decision-making and ball-handling aren’t always great as a punt returner. He’s dangerous when the ball is in his hands, though. Durability concerns will be prevalent at all times but the explosives he can generate as a backfield mismatch and return man will earn him consideration.
profiles.strengths:
• Averaged 140 scrimmage yards per game in 2024.
  • Can joystick around tacklers as a runner, receiver and returner.
  • Manipulates defenders into pulling blocks on pitch plays.
  • Short-area cut quickness and stop-start talent leads to missed tackles.
  • Major mismatch on linebackers when working down the seam.
  • Has two touchdowns on just 18 career punt returns.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Diminutive frame creates durability concerns.
  • Unlikely to see much usage between the tackles.
  • Looks for “better deal” instead of keeping runs on track.
  • Unable to play through much contact.
  • Sketchy decision-maker on punt returns.
  • Fights the ball at times when catching punts.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 7 games as a reserve (4 tackles, TFL, PBU).
  • 2023: Started all 13 games (28 tackles, TFL, PBU).
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (27 tackles, 5 TFLs with 2 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games (38 tackles, 5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, PBU, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-year starter with a long wingspan but inconsistencies in his game and a lack of standout production. Eastern plays with loose upper-body movement that helps him slip blocks and find gaps. He uses his length effectively to disengage when he times it right. However, his high-cut frame and below-average pad level create persistent issues anchoring and maintaining gap integrity, especially against zone blocks. He ends up on the ground too often and hasn’t proven he can create consistent pressure as a rusher. Eastern’s size and length might be best utilized in a wider alignment as an odd-front end.
profiles.strengths:
• Three-year starter with long arms.
  • Technique to sink low and corkscrew lowers against double teams. 
  • Slips off blocks and into gaps using loose upper body.
  • Gets into centers quickly with good first step forward.
  • Uses length to disengage and shove free from the block.
profiles.weaknesses:
• High-cut with hips perched high in his stance.
  • Below-average pad level and lower-body mass to anchor the point.
  • Frequently beaten to the spot laterally and sealed against zone blocks.
  • Ends up on the ground more than he should.
  • Tight hips limit lateral agility to excel in rush twists.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 5 games as a reserve (6 tackles).
  • 2023: Played in 7 games as a reserve (6 tackles, INT, 3 PBUs).
  • 2024: Played in 7 games with 6 starts (17 tackles, 2 INTs, 2 PBUs). Missed time due to a shoulder injury. 
  • 2025: Tied for the team lead with 2 INTs. Started 11 games (35 tackles, 2 TFLs with 1 sack, 4 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Moore is a long outside cornerback with good size but limited experience due to injuries. His size and length benefit him from press. He plays with adequate eye balance as a short-zone defender. Moore is a good deep-ball tracker who tilts jump balls in his favor, but he lacks make-up speed to run down coverage mistakes. He’s upright with sluggish hips in transitions and is missing the foot quickness/acceleration to stay connected with quicker route-runners. Improved anticipation and decisiveness should come with more snaps but durability concerns could hurt his draft stock.
profiles.strengths:
• Impressive height, weight and length for an outside corner.
  • Imposing figure from press with length to slow release.
  • Takes cues quickly from passers in short zone.
  • Tracks and adjusts to deep balls at top speed.
  • Figures to be top man on high-point battles.
  • Pulls arms and slaps hands when near the catch point.
  • Good toughness as a tackler in run support.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Started just 17 games in his four seasons.
  • Too much space and not enough squeeze as a zone defender.
  • Upright and sluggish in his lateral transitions with break points.
  • Needs to improve route recognition and decisiveness in coverage.
  • Top-end speed is average to close out stray vertical routes.
  • Missed games in 2022, 2023 and 2024 due to injuries.

profiles.overview: A seventh-year senior, Voisin displays good balance and footwork as a route-runner. He’s unable to outrun quality coverage as a vertical threat and lacks the catch radius/contested-catch talent to win when crowded. While he did a nice job during Senior Bowl practices, Voisin’s age and lack of size/speed create a massive hill to climb as he pursues a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Held his own against Senior Bowl competition in practices.
  • Stabilizes his upper half to disguise route intentions.
  • Split low, allowing for better balance through cuts.
  • Keeps footwork tight getting in and out of breaks.
  • Catches with natural, soft hands.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Has a tough time playing through contact.
  • Rarely sinks hips for crisp stops on comebacks.
  • Sits and waits on throws instead of working back to them.
  • Lacks top-end speed to outrun NFL coverage.
  • Limited catch radius creates a smaller margin for error for QBs.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (New Mexico Military Institute): 68-113-60.2, 916 yards, 10 TDs, 3 INTs passing; 86-449-5.2, 8 TDs rushing in 8 games.
  • 2021 (New Mexico Military Institute): 121-215-56.3, 1,728 yards, 21 TDs, INT passing; 658 yards, 7 TDs rushing in 13 games for the NJCAA national champions.
  • 2022 (New Mexico State): Quick Lane Bowl MVP (17-29, 2 TDs passing; 12-65 rushing against Bowling Green St). Ranked fifth in FBS with 14.4 yards per completion. Played in 12 games with 8 starts (101-190-53.2, 1,450 yards, 13 TDs, 6 INTs passing; 93-508-5.5, 6 TDs rushing).
  • 2023 (New Mexico State): Conference USA Offensive Player of the Year; second-team All-Conference USA (Liberty QB Kaidon Salter was C-USA overall MVP). Started all 15 games (221-366-60.4, 2,973 yards, 26 TDs, 9 INTs passing; 176-923-5.2, 7 TDs rushing). 
  • 2024: SEC Newcomer of the Year. Led the team with 801 rushing yards (192 carries, 4.2), 8 rushing TDs. Started all 13 games (177-298-59.4, 2,293 yards, 20 TDs, 4 INTs passing). Birmingham Bowl MVP (160 yards, 3 TDs passing; 17-84, 2 TDs rushing). Followed NMSU head coach Jerry Kill and offensive coordinator Tim Beck to Vanderbilt (Kill was hired as a consultant to head coach Clark Lea). Won an injunction against NCAA to gain a year of eligibility in 2025, arguing that his time playing at a junior college should not count toward his NCAA eligibility; NCAA subsequently gave all former junior-college players whose eligibility was to run out after the 2024 season another year of eligibility in 2025.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-SEC. Won the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award (given to the nation's top upperclassman QB). Finalist for the Heisman Trophy (nation's top player), Walter Camp Award (nation's top player), Manning Award (nation's top QB, including postseason). Ranked third in the FBS in pass efficiency (170.36), and eighth in completion rate (70.6%, 267-378); tied for eighth in passing TDs with 29, a school record (versus 8 INTs). Also set a school record in passing yards (3,539). Started all 13 games (167-862-5.2, 10 TDs rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Pavia is a short, tough, productive quarterback who plays bigger than his measurables. He elevates those around him and was the main character in Vanderbilt’s shift from doormat to winning program. He’s improvisational, creating explosives that aren’t on the call sheet without playing reckless hero ball. He scans through progressions, throwing with intermediate accuracy, but impatience versus zone can lead to costly mistakes. He can stand and deliver or escape and win with his arm or legs when pressured. However, he lacks ideal mechanics and needs altered launch points for cleaner sight lines and release points. His deep ball is below average. He isn’t explosive or fast, but he’s a force multiplier for the run game, especially near the goal line. Efficiency and success rates check out across most situational filters, but he requires a more tailored scheme. Quarterbacks his size rarely make NFL rosters, but his competitiveness should be a plus as long as he’s willing to accept a role as a backup.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He’s not a bad player at all. Really smart. I don’t know if he can win from the pocket enough but I really love the makeup.” - AFC pro personnel director
profiles.strengths:
• Supremely competitive with good football intelligence and winning makeup.
  • Dual-threat option who creates for his offense on land and by air.
  • Impressive move accuracy (rollouts/scrambles) and third-down conversion rate.
  • Flashes an ability to make anticipatory and timing throws.
  • Big hands allow him to pump, reset and work to alternate options.
  • Able to quicken eyes and decision-making versus pressure without panicking.
  • Matched Fernando Mendoza’s completion rate on intermediate throws.
  • Scramble threat softens coverage structure and creates throwing windows.
  • Productive runner in speed option, midline, zone-read and power concepts.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Rare to see quarterbacks with his measurables make an NFL roster.
  • Production and consistency dipped against quality SEC defenses.
  • Inconsistent patience and decision-making against split-safety looks.
  • Lower half lags behind, leading to sailed throws and missed placement between the numbers.
  • Forced to release throws with upward trajectory due to his height.
  • Floats deep throws, allowing defensive backs to locate them.
  • Too quick to exit the side door instead of sliding and climbing.
  • Average open-field speed and elusiveness.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (North Carolina): Redshirted. Enrolled in January.
  • 2022 (North Carolina): Played in 5 games as a reserve. 
  • 2023 (North Carolina): Played in all 13 games with 8 starts at LT.
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 9 starts at LT.
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started all 15 games at LT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Pounds is a high-cut, smooth-limbed tackle. He plays with a high pad level, spotty body control and inconsistent technique, but he typically battles through those issues at an adequate clip. His run blocking is behind his pass blocking and it’s likely to stay that way. He needs to develop a more consistent pass set to deal with edge speed, but his length and grip strength can effectively end the rush when his timing is right. Pounds’ deficiencies create a lower floor, but he could find work as a swing tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Brings energy from hips to hands with first contact.
  • Initial knock-back power widens the edge.
  • Heavy hands help wash down angle blocks.
  • Pairs a heavy punch with quick resets.
  • Locks out his length and keeps his head back.
  • Uses grip strength to control the rush.
  • Aware of twist development and remains calm.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average body control as a run blocker.
  • Lack of leverage limits double-team movement.
  • Defenders play across his face in the run game.
  • Occasional struggles matching edge speed through the turn.
  • Needs to play with efficient use of hands in protection.
  • Opens post leg to an inside move instead of sliding to cut it off.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 15 games with 5 starts for the national champions (20-180-9.0, 3 TDs receiving).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games with 8 starts (29-355-12.2, 2 TDs receiving; 25-157-6.3, 2 TDs rushing; 6-160-26.7 KR).
  • 2024: Played in 13 games with 12 starts (43-466-10.8, 4 TDs receiving; 9-107-11.9, TD rushing).
  • 2025: Played in all 14 games with 9 starts (27-268-9.9, 2 TDs receiving; 17-109-6.4, 2 TDs rushing).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Micah, joined Dillon at Georgia in 2025 after playing at Vanderbilt and Notre Dame.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Big, strong, explosive receiver requiring specific usage on the next level. Bell is top-notch with the ball in his hands on reverses, jet-sweeps and quick hitches. He has the ability to create chunk runs after breaking tackles. Bell lacks ideal route savvy to uncover underneath and can be too easy for cornerbacks to read. He’s a body-catcher with below-average hands, but he did have better catch tape in 2023 with Carson Beck at quarterback. Bell’s game lacks well-rounded qualities and position-specific skill, but his traits, manufactured-touch talent and kick-return potential should give him a chance to make it as a WR5.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “Some scouts see him as Deebo-lite but I wouldn’t go that far. Yes, you have to get the ball in his hands, but I think he’s a better receiver than he was able to show (in 2025) in that offense.” - NFC national scout
profiles.strengths:
• Well-built receiver with the frame of a big running back.
  • Highly successful weapon on jet-sweeps and reverses.
  • Breaks through open-field tacklers once he gets rolling downhill.
  • Accelerates late in route to create space.
  • Physical through contact in the route and at the catch-point.
  • Run-block potential on perimeter and when cracking down.
  • Has the experience and talent to become a plus kick returner.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Pedestrian catch production over 56 games at Georgia.
  • Routes lack crisp cuts and attention to detail.
  • Doesn’t often adjust route to avoid redirection.
  • Unable to pull the brakes firmly for comeback routes.
  • Body-catcher with below-average catch focus.
  • Struggles to bring in throws outside his frame.

profiles.bio:
• 2023 (Purdue): Third-team Associated Press All-American. FWAA Defensive Freshman of the Year. Big Ten Conference Freshman of the Year. Second-team All-Big Ten. Shaun Alexander National Freshman of the Year finalist. Ranked sixth in the FBS with 74 solo tackles, tied for third with 6 INTs. Led team with 106 tackles. Started all 12 games (2 TFLs, 2 PBUs, 2 FFs). 
  • 2024 (Purdue): Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Ranked fifth in the FBS with 70 solo tackles. Led team with 104 tackles, 7 PBUs. Started all 12 games (4.5 TFLs with 1 sack). 
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten. Started all 15 games (95 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 INTs, 5 PBUs).
  • Miscellaneous: Brothers, Jake and Brennan, played safety at Purdue. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Savvy three-year starter with NFL size, speed and alignment versatility. Thieneman is an extension of his defensive coordinator, aligning and adjusting the secondary to motion and pre-snap shifts. He’s an instinctive, rangy safety who can roll down into big nickel or robber positioning.
