profiles.overview: Bernard is a versatile wideout with ascending production over the last three years.  He has good size, accelerates to top speed quickly and is a smooth route runner with well-disguised breaks and clean footwork getting in and out. He can line up outside or in the slot and is capable of running a full route tree across all three levels. He has impressive run-after-catch ability. Bernard’s second gear as a field-stretcher is fairly ordinary, and he doesn't always play to his size when it’s time to compete for catch space. Bernard projects as an above-average WR2/3.
profiles.strengths:
• Good size, big hands and inside/outside versatility. 
  • Tempo alterations help to bypass and separate from coverage.
  • Able to drop hips and quickly snap off curls/comebacks.
  • Smooth strider with steady turnover working through zone.
  • Gets through route transitions smoothly and at top speed.
  • Above-average focus and footwork near the sideline.
  • Weaponized as a utility option out of the backfield.
  • Plus field vision and cut quickness when the ball is in his hands.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs better physicality and hand-fighting to defeat press.
  • Accelerates quickly but isn't a vertical burner.
  • Positioning would benefit from quicker adjustments.
  • Needs to become more consistently competitive for catch space.
  • Most drops come when working into the hashes.
  • Average feel for coverage positioning on zone beaters.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 10 games as a reserve (10 tackles, TFL).
  • 2023: Played in 11 games as a reserve (11 tackles, 3.5 TFLs).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 3 starts (30 tackles, 6 TFLs with 5 sacks, 2 FFs). 
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 7 starts (33 tackles, 7 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: An undersized 3-technique with disruptive attributes, Halton is best suited for a rotational role in a movement-based front. He plays with synced hands and feet and good lateral agility. His initial quickness makes him quite slippery but a centered block can clear him from the run lane due to his lack of mass/anchor. He’s an energetic, gap-to-gap rusher who can threaten guards on their edges or play his role as an effective twister. Finding the right scheme fit will be critical for Halton in the NFL.
profiles.strengths:
• Able to get skinny and quickly penetrate into gaps.
  • Tracks ball-carriers and slides toward their lane choice.
  • Slips off block engagement with active hands and loose upper body.
  • Above-average reactive quickness as a tackler.
  • Foot agility and body control are made for twists and rush games.
  • Searches relentlessly for a crevice to access the pocket.
  • Edge-to-edge rush attack with good closing speed to get home.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Plays too straight-legged and lacks leverage at the point.
  • Lands hands quickly but struggles to control and shed blocks.
  • Lacks mass/anchor to consistently leverage his gap.
  • Inconsistent in maintaining run fits on lateral engagements.
  • Rush advantages can be muted by athletic guards.
  • Needs hand usage to catch up with footwork in pass rush.

profiles.bio:
• High school: 5-star recruit, top OLB prospect nationally.
  • 2022: Second-team All-SEC. Freshman All-American. Freshman All-SEC. Led team with 13 TFLs (topped all Power 5 freshmen), 7.5 sacks. Tied for third in the FBS with 4 FFs. Played in all 14 games with 8 starts (72 tackles, INT, 2 PBUs). 
  • 2023: Second-team All-SEC. Led team with 13 TFLs, 3 FFs. Started all 13 games after moving to LB from edge rusher (75 tackles, 5.5 sacks, INT, 5 PBUs).
  • 2024: Redshirted. Started the first 4 games (17 tackles, 1.5 TFLs). Missed the rest of the season with a right knee injury. Awarded the No. 7 jersey that has been worn by top players like CB Patrick Peterson (who started the tradition), CB Derek Stingley Jr., WR Ja'Marr Chase, RB Leonard Fournette, DB Tyrann Mathieu.
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Led team with 4 sacks. Tied for the team lead with 8 TFLs, 3 INTs. Played in 12 games with 11 starts (56 tackles, 4 sacks, 3 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Slightly undersized off-ball linebacker with solid 2025 production but less in-game impact than he showed in 2022 and 2023 before his ACL tear in 2024. Perkins is decisive against the run and knifes into the backfield when lanes open. He’s adequate in block take-ons and finishes tackles near the line with good physicality. He can still run but lacks his previous explosiveness in close-outs and pursuit. His instincts in space are average and he can get lost in coverage, but he has the athletic ability coverage requires. Perkins is at his best when deployed in a scheme that allows him to play free and attack the line as often as possible.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 35.5 tackles for loss, 17 sacks and eight forced fumbles in his four seasons.
  • Reads run and scrapes to the line to compress the front.
  • Lands a crisp two-hand punch to stay clean against blocks.
  • Adequate burst in short spaces to close on lane development.
  • Sifts through route development to locate zone landmarks.
  • Triggers a well-timed blitz to harass the pocket.
  • Accelerates through contact to finish tackles near the line.
  • Was a special-teams demon his freshman season.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average burst to chase and squeeze runs to the boundary.
  • Needs to be quicker in defeating skill-position blockers.
  • Linear pursuit to the football leads to missed tackles.
  • Inconsistent breaking down in time as an open-field tackler.
  • Too much confusion on his coverage tape.
  • Average elusiveness to bypass blitz pickup.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Penn State): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Penn State): Played in 13 games as a reserve (19-273-14.4, TD).
  • 2023 (Penn State): Played in 8 games with 6 starts (19-228-12.0, TD). Missed games late in the year with a broken collarbone.
  • 2024 (Penn State): Started 15 games (46-720-15.7, 4 TDs). 
  • 2025: Led team with 61 receptions, 934 receiving yards (15.3 per, 4 TDs). Started all 15 games (3-1-0.3 rushing; 14-113-8.1 PR).
  • Miscellaneous: Nickname is "Tre.”

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Wallace is a leggy long-strider who played deep into the College Football Playoff in consecutive seasons at Penn State and Ole Miss. While his catch production has jumped in the last two seasons, he has trouble beating press and uncovering over the first two levels, which makes it tougher to project continued improvement as a pro. While he’s likely to see a higher number of contested catches, he’s built for it. He shows little concern when working into traffic and battling for 50/50 throws. Wallace lacks route versatility, so a role as a possession slot receiver with zone-beating talent could give him the best chance to succeed.
profiles.strengths:
• Played deep into the College Football Playoff at both Penn State and Ole Miss.
  • Made nine grabs for 156 yards and a score in playoff win over Georgia.
  • Head fakes create some movement from opposing corners.
  • Good urgency when working zone-beaters from the slot.
  • Sharpens his catch focus when working into traffic.
  • Plenty of toughness to finish catches through contact.
  • Climbs the ladder to find high-point positioning.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average foot quickness to consistently slip press.
  • Lack of bend causes drift and loss of momentum at turns.
  • Below-average footwork and burst at break points.
  • Inconsistent making late course adjustments on deep throws.
  • Not enough run-after-catch talent.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Texas A&M): Played in 2 games as a reserve (2-4-50.0, 59 yards, TD, INT passing; 6-43-7.2 rushing).
  • 2021 (Texas A&M): Redshirted. Started the first 2 games (22-35-62.9, 300 yards, 2 TDs, 3 INTs passing; 6-24-4.0 rushing). Missed the rest of the year due to injury.
  • 2022 (Texas A&M): Played in 6 games with 4 starts (104-187-55.6, 1,220 yards, 7 TDs, 6 INTs passing; 29-83-2.9, TD rushing). Benched after A&M lost to Appalachian State.
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Led team with 10 rushing TDs (120-737-6.1). Started all 13 games at QB (226-367-61.6, 2,842 yards, 27 TDs, 16 INTs). Team captain.
  • 2024: Led team with 11 rushing TDs (125-587-4.7). Ranked fourth in the FBS in completion rate (a school-record 72.9%; 196-269, 2,114 yards, 14 TDs, 2 INTs). Started 11 games. Missed 2 games due to injury. Team captain.
  • 2025: ACC Offensive Player of the Year, first-team All-ACC. Finalist for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award (given to the nation's top upperclassman QB) and Manning Award (nation's top QB, including postseason). Led the team with 953 rushing yards (185 carries, 5.2) and 15 rushing TDs. Started 12 games (252-361-69.8, 2,951 yards, 14 TDs, 6 INTs passing). Team captain. Set school single-season records with 3,920 yards of total offense, 252 completions. Set school career records with 674 completions, and by completing 67.6% of his passes. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: King will enter camp as a 25-year-old rookie after spending three years apiece at Texas A&M and Georgia Tech. He’s a long-legged, dual-threat quarterback who displayed admirable resilience in becoming a productive, winning player after suffering through unmet expectations at Texas A&M. He’s a grit-and-guts passer with subpar footwork and mechanics, but he finds ways to make plays when needed. He’s not nearly the passer he needs to be for the pro game, but his talent as a runner and mental toughness could give a boost to his chances.
profiles.strengths:
• Resilient with good mental toughness for the position.
  • Improved his efficiency as a game manager since 2024.
  • Continues scanning for completions when play extends.
  • Adequate touch to layer throws when needed.
  • Capable runner who can pick up tough yards on called runs.
  • Finished career with 37 rushing touchdowns.
profiles.weaknesses:
• High-cut with long legs and lean frame.
  • Will need to play with better ball security.
  • Accuracy and ball placement fall below the mark.
  • Footwork will become wild when pressured in the pocket.
  • Has issues overstriding and lacks drive velocity.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Florida International): Conference USA All-Freshman Team. Played in all 12 games with 6 starts (25 tackles, 3.5 TFLs, 4 PBUs, blocked kick).
  • 2023 (Florida International): Started 11 games (42 tackles, INT-returned for TD, 4 PBUs).
  • 2024 (Florida International): Started 12 games (38 tackles, TFL, INT, 4 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-ACC. Tied for the FBS lead with 1.38 passes defensed per game, tied for seventh with 5 INTs. Tied for the team lead with 13 PBUs. Started all 13 games (47 tackles, TFL).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Masses has taken a lot of snaps but his FBS-leading ball production came out of nowhere. He plays with a ball-hawking mentality, keeping his eyes forward. He’s able to mirror and match releases while disrupting route timing with well-placed jabs from press. He has an innate feel for challenging throws at optimal angles and plays ball over man most of the time. He’s fairly effective at anticipating route breaks but frequently mauls and invites penalties when the route doesn’t go as expected. Masses lacked explosiveness in his NFL Scouting Combine workout, which will need to be balanced against the competitiveness he showed on tape.
profiles.strengths:
• Able to mirror the release and shadow pattern breaks from trail.
  • Stiff jabs at full extension slow receivers and disrupt route timing.
  • Good eye balance between quarterback and route concepts in zone.
  • Has the long speed to carry vertical routes downfield.
  • Drives on seam throws and overlaps coverage from zone.
  • Takes playmaking angles to either force turnovers or disrupt the catch point.
  • Led the nation with 18 passes defensed, including five interceptions.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inconsistent balance and long legs create slower transitions in space.
  • Phases on the top of verticals, creating easier comeback throws.
  • Gets leveraged into prematurely declaring his hips.
  • Grabs, tugs and mauls downfield instead of trusting technique.
  • Needs to turn and locate the football from tight man.
  • Shies away from proper tackling form against big running backs.

profiles.overview: Nwokobia is a down safety with nickelback potential. He’s coming off left shoulder surgery, which prevented him from testing at his pro day. He can handle some man coverage underneath and is opportunistic from zone coverages. He lacks ideal cover talent and range for extended man coverage or single-high asks, though. He’s an adequate run supporter and tackler near the line but needs to improve his finishing rate on receivers after the catch. Nwokobia might not be drafted, but he has the ability to compete for a practice squad spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Plays with good eye balance between quarterback and routes.
  • Finished career with 25 passes defensed and 11 interceptions.
  • Plays downhill into run fits with a steady pace.
  • Stays wide and tackle-ready in the hole.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Allows runs to cross his face and escape wide.
  • Inconsistent tackle finisher when trying to bring down receivers after the catch.
  • Below-average range and field speed to maintain man coverage.
  • Underwent left shoulder surgery in December.

profiles.overview: Big, long tackle with heavy hands but sloppy technique that limits his consistency. World is a high-character player who did a decent job of working around his limitations during his college career. His first contact, whether engaging run blocks or throwing his punch, is firm and purposeful. Elements of his run blocking will translate to the league despite an elevated pad level but his pass protection is filled with holes and requires immediate attention. If he can cut back on quick losses, World has a chance to become an average swing tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Extensive game experience as a four-year starter.
  • Operates with heavy hands in run and pass blocking.
  • Displays ability to adjust and connect to movement in space.
  • Independent hands help create contact with rush.
  • Rifles a very stiff left jab into rusher with ideal timing.
  • Uses length to redirect rusher outside intended rush path.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Tight-hipped with high pads and narrow base.
  • Gets beat inside due to oversetting.
  • Footwork and recoveries are messy at times.
  • Feet and hands lack harmony and lead to lunging.
  • Sloppy hand placement prevents ideal block control.
  • Lack of fluidity diminishes timing for combo blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (North Carolina Central): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022 (North Carolina Central): Third-team All-Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference (MEAC). Played in all 12 games as a reserve (87-421-4.8, 7 TDs rushing; 9-129-14.3, 3 TDs receiving).
  • 2023 (North Carolina Central): Played in 11 games as a reserve (71-321-4.5, TD rushing; 16-229-14.3, 4 TDs receiving; 6-82-13.7 KR).
  • 2024 (North Carolina Central): First-team All-MEAC. Finalist for the Walter Payton Award as the top player in the FCS. Led team with 1,146 rushing yards (196 carries, 5.8 per), 15 rushing TDs. Started all 11 games (30-271-9.0, 2 TDs receiving).
  • 2025: First-team All-ACC. Led team with 1,062 rushing yards (222 carries, 4.8 per), 14 rushing TDs. Started 13 games (43-253-5.9, TD receiving; 1-20-20.0 KR).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Despite lacking ideal size, Taylor is a three-down back with proven production. He runs with compact power and elite balance. He’s excellent on short-yardage carries, scoring tough touchdowns and gaining more than is blocked. He “fields his position” with solid vision and open-field burst, but when defenses slow his feet, they slow his processing. His lateral elusiveness is average in the hole and after catches underneath. His willingness and talent on third downs should create an opportunity as a complementary "thunder" back capable of handling a three-down backup role.
profiles.strengths:
• Logged 418 carries for 2,208 yards and 29 TDs since start of 2024 season.
  • Presses the line deep to coax linebackers into traffic.
  • Sustains top speed to run away and hide in the open field.
  • Delivers right shoulder like a battering ram to thwart tacklers.
  • Sniffs out creases to punch through near the end zone.
  • Can line up in the slot or out wide to mismatch linebackers. 
  • Squares and anchors versus blitzers and mirrors post-contact.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Misses opportunities to burst wide and outflank contain.
  • Too many hops and wasted steps early in the run.
  • Average lateral jump cuts to avoid penetration.
  • Can be a herky-jerky runner getting from cut to cut.
  • Focus drops on swing passes were an issue in 2025.
  • Slow to accelerate up the field after the catch.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (California): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2022 (California): Freshman All-American. Honorable Mention All-Pac-12 Conference. Led team with 65 receptions (755 yards, 11.6 per), 7 receiving TDs. Led all FBS freshmen in receptions. Started all 12 games.
  • 2023 (UCLA): Played in all 13 games with 10 starts (36-597-16.6 per, 4 TDs).
  • 2024 (UCLA): Played in 11 games with 8 starts (22-315-14.3, 2 TDs).
  • 2025: Tied for the team lead with 3 receiving TDs. Started all 12 games (27-406-15.0; 1-10-10.0 KR).
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Michael, played WR at Virginia Tech. Nephew of the late Pro Football and College Football Hall of Famer Floyd Little, who was a three-time All-American RB at Syracuse and first-team All-Pro with the Denver Broncos. Mother, Melodie, is in the Bradley University track and field Hall of Fame.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sturdivant is a traits-based wideout whose production over the last two seasons doesn’t match the potential he shows on tape. His combination of foot agility, vertical speed and ball skills should allow him to run routes as an “X” or “Z” receiver. His routes could use better attention to detail to help increase his elusiveness at break points and free up his catch space. He’s very tough over the middle and will not shrink from combat catches. He can accelerate quickly to add run-after-catch on short throws. His run blocking is adequate but needs more strain. Sturdivant’s ingredients make him a worthy middle-round investment, as his best football could be ahead of him.
profiles.strengths:
• Tall, fast and long with ability to play “X” or “Z” spots.
  • Former sprinter with sustained deep speed to separate vertically.
  • Has the footwork to run a varied route tree on all three levels.
  • Clever in outfoxing the coverage and defeating his leverage.
  • Size and toughness to protect catches through punishing hits.
  • Ball skills to outclass corners when contested outside the numbers.
  • Good post-catch elusiveness to tack on yards after catch underneath.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Never came close to replicating his catch production from 2022.
  • Below-average salesmanship to tilt defenders at break points.
  • Average quickness when gathering and opening on comebacks.
  • Plays with some route drift, making it easier on the coverage.
  • Run blocking could use just a little more strain and grit.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Contra Costa College): First-team all-conference.
  • 2022 (New Mexico): Honorable Mention All-Mountain West Conference. Started all 12 games at LT.
  • 2023 (New Mexico): First-team All-Mountain West. Started all 12 games at LT. 
  • 2024: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games at LT.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big Ten. Started 12 games at LT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Durable four-year starter with ideal size and length who needs to become more of an impediment on each snap. Davis possesses good play strength but issues with footwork and body control limit his consistency in sustaining blocks. He has adequate lateral/second-level range for move blocks and surprising drive power when he finishes his block. Davis has had some impressive reps against pro-caliber rushers over his last two seasons, but developing better timing, accuracy and placement with his hands will be critical as he competes for a role as an NFL swing tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Carries good size with massive wingspan and big hands.
  • Good timing and consistency on his pin-and-climb combos. 
  • Power to torque and turn defender out of run gaps.
  • Drives feet and looks to finish blocks when he has the advantage.
  • Uses vertical sets with awareness to the B-gap against T/E twists.
  • Patience and independent hands allow him to gather spin counters.
  • Good athleticism to mirror inside moves and find targets in space on screens.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Leads with his helmet and upper body far too often.
  • Body control and contact balance are below average.
  • Poor hand placement limits block sustain/consistency in both phases.
  • Opens outside hip way too early against speed rushers.
  • Allows rushers into his chest without popping and gathering.
  • Lethargic hands allow rushers to counter and eliminate the punch.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Played in 6 games as a reserve (7-93-13.3, 2 TDs). 2 TDs in Holiday Bowl versus Louisville.
  • 2024: Tied for fifth in the FBS with 12 receiving TDs (43-525-12.2). Las Vegas Bowl MVP (7-127, 3 TDs receiving). Played in all 13 games with 8 starts. 
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in 11 games with 9 starts (49-745-15.2, 4 TDs). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Lane is a red-zone stalwart with elite length and ball skills to mismatch cornerbacks when he’s given room to work. He struggles playing through contact and sees an unusually high number of contested catches, but his catch radius, hand-eye coordination and focus give him a substantial advantage as a ball-winner. He might need releases schemed against heavy press teams and certain limbs on the route tree will be dead for him. Lane has the confidence and talent to become a productive pro and red-zone specialist, though.
profiles.strengths:
• Runs downfield routes with gliding strides.
  • Shows plus catch focus and creates late separation when contested.
  • Gets easy wins when pinning corners on fades.
  • Makes impressive late adjustments for quick grabs.
  • Long arms and big hands created viral catches.
  • Light on his feet to slip first the tackler after the catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Departure will be delayed by a jamming press.
  • Routes are typically run at a single speed.
  • Slow to break off and open quickly on stops and comebacks.
  • Coverage tends to blanket him through lateral break-points.
  • Really struggles to play through route contact.

profiles.overview: Dingle offers a height/weight/speed option at inside linebacker. He’s a three-year starter who often relies on athleticism over instincts. His overall production in the impact categories is relatively light and he’s below average in coverage. The size, athletic testing and play strength are all positives, but Dingle is lacking in snap-to-snap execution, production and three-down versatility.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses a good blend of size, speed and strength.
  • Good peripheral vision and awareness of incoming angle blocks.
  • Uses proactive hands to strike and separate on the second level.
  • Dips low and wraps around the legs as an interior tackler.
  • Has the traits to compete for a special-teams role.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average instincts and trigger quickness.
  • Makes mistakes with run fits and gets caught in the trash.
  • Average bend diminishes ability to leverage his gap through contact.
  • Would benefit from better pacing and patience with lateral scrapes.
  • Lacks fluidity in coverage situations.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (California): Redshirted as a walk-on.
  • 2023 (California): Freshman All-American as go-to target of Fernando Mendoza. Started all 13 games (35-407-11.6, 2 TDs).
  • 2024 (California): Honorable Mention All-ACC. Led team with 56 receptions, 623 receiving yards (11.1 per, 2 TDs). Started all 13 games.
  • 2025: Started all 13 games (33-346-10.5, 3 TDs). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Endries is a quarterback-friendly “F” tight end who still needs time in the weight room. His route-running can be monotonous and short-area separation uninspiring, but he’s tough, has a rebounder’s feel for boxing out defenders and is a consistent ball-winner even when coverage is draped all over him. He builds speed and is tougher on man coverage when allowed to stretch his legs on longer routes. Run-blocking is a roller-coaster ride of bad losses and quality wins. He lacks the play strength to block ends and whiffs in space on occasion, but he also gets his share of wins on split-zone, lead pulls and combo climbs to the linebacker. Endries should develop into an NFL starter.
profiles.strengths:
• Started every game over his three seasons.
  • Led Cal in receiving in 2024 as Fernando Mendoza’s top target.
  • Plays through contact at the release and at the top of the route.
  • Builds speed to stress man coverage on intermediate routes.
  • Bodies up tight man coverage and catches with hand extension.
  • Sudden hands to stab and secure hot or high throws.
  • Adjusts and centers defensive ends on split-zone blocks.
  • Stays after blocks in space once he connects.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs more functional mass and play strength.
  • Run-blocking angles and landmarks are inconsistent.
  • Below-average quickness in and out of breaks.
  • Few drops, but too many double-catches in 2024.
  • Lacks make-you-miss elusiveness and reacceleration after the catch.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Weber State): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (1 tackle).
  • 2022 (Weber State): Played in all 13 games with 11 starts (28 tackles, 8 TFLs with 6 sacks).
  • 2023 (Weber State): First-team All-Big Sky Conference. Ranked fifth in the FCS with 10.5 sacks, tied for fifth with 4 FFs (56 tackles, 12 TFLs, INT, 5 PBUs). Started 11 games. 
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Started all 13 games (51 tackles, 10 TFLs with 5 sacks, INT, 2 FFs). Team captain.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12. Led team with 13.5 TFLs, 10 sacks (55 tackles, PBU, 2 FFs). Started 12 games. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Two-time team captain with four productive seasons between Weber State and BYU. Kelly is a burly linebacker with adequate play speed and desired aggression. His reaction time is average but his struggles to find his leverage and fit as a run defender pop up too often on tape. He has a strong punch but short arms and can get stuck to blockers who sink their hands in. He’s adequate in coverage but above average as a blitzer and has some juice when he rushes off the edge. Kelly might need to star on special teams to find a role as an even-front linebacker with third-down value.
profiles.strengths:
• Delivers firm punch on climbing blocks.
  • Adequate speed for most sideline-to-sideline pursuits.
  • Possesses quality play strength and some nasty in his demeanor.
  • Quick to close and pounce on pass-catcher from man/zone.
  • Displays good feel as a blitzer and is able to trim the corner off the edge.
  • Has plug-and-play traits as a four-phase special-teamer.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average eye quickness and reaction time to his keys.
  • Will turn his pads and overrun his fits against wide runs.
  • Needs to leverage his gaps through better positioning.
  • Inconsistent technique and execution to get rid of a block.
  • Has some trouble finishing tackles with consistency in space.
  • Was a non-factor against the Texas Tech running game.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Florida): Played in 8 games as a reserve and on special teams (3 tackles).
  • 2023 (Florida): Played in 8 games as a reserve with 1 start (17 tackles, TFL). Missed the end of the season due to an ACL injury.
  • 2024 (Florida): Played in 12 games with 8 starts (60 tackles, 4 TFLs with 1 sack, INT, FF).
  • 2025: Played in 12 games with 11 starts (52 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, PBU).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Pyburn is a muscular outside linebacker with short arms and unremarkable athleticism. He’s been a non-factor as a pass rusher during his career, but he gets after it as a run defender. Pyburn has some heat in his hands, jarring blockers and playing off of them to make tackles in his vicinity, but his lack of length will make it tougher to set edges against longer NFL tackles. As a backup with a lack of rush and cover talent, special teams will need to become his money-maker to stay in the league.
profiles.strengths:
• Densely muscled with thick limbs and a burly neck.
  • Sturdy base, upper-body strength and contact balance to battle at the point of attack.
  • Plays through and around blocking tight ends with explosive hands.
  • Gets off blocks and hustles to the ball to tackle.
  • Activates counter spin underneath when he reaches pocket depth.
  • Plenty of experience on special teams.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hasn’t shown the knack or ability for getting to the quarterback.
  • Lacks go-to moves or hand counters to create opportunities.
  • Easy to find, punch and widen to take him out of the rush.
  • Inconsistent tracking play development in the backfield.
  • Below-average length to punch and separate from NFL tackles.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Missouri): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (Missouri): Played in 10 games (46-1,951-42.4, long 68, 4 touchbacks, 18 fair caught, 15 inside the 20).
  • 2023: Third-team All-ACC. Played in all 13 games (62-2,766-44.6, long 64, 5 touchbacks, 24 fair caught, 18 inside the 20; 1 tackle).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Would have ranked sixth in the FBS in gross punting average but did not have enough kicks to qualify. Played in all 13 games (33-1,509-45.7, long 64, 3 touchbacks, 10 fair caught, 11 inside the 20).
  • 2025: First-team All-ACC. Ranked fifth in the FBS with a school-record 47.1 yards per punt (59-2,780, long 64, 6 touchbacks, 25 fair caught, 14 inside the 20). Set school career record with 45.8 yards per punt. Played in all 12 games.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, John, punted at USC. Cousin, Ryan, punted at Colorado State and led the NFL in punt yards as a Titans rookie in 2022. Uncle, Paul, punted at Stanford.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Four-year punter who improved at his craft in each season. Stonehouse has a solid leg but lacks booming power. He strikes the ball with adequate consistency and direction but needs to push his hang-time higher to avoid punt returns. Stonehouse’s ability to hang around could depend on his ability to bolster his “inside the 10” numbers instead of being overly aggressive in trying to push punts as close to the goal line as possible.
profiles.strengths:
• Hang-time improved with each season.
  • Delivers directional punts with relative consistency.
  • Makes the ball cut or deaden on his nose-drop punts.
  • Punts with adequate power when backed up.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Might need to quicken his operation time as a pro.
  • Allows too many returns as an open-field punter.
  • Greedy on pooch punts, pushing them up against the goal line.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 12 games with 1 start (22 tackles, 2 TFLs, 3 PBUs, FF). 
  • 2023: Missed the season after tearing his right ACL during a spring scrimmage. 
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (42 tackles, 6.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, FF).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Played in all 12 games with 10 starts (30 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 2 sacks). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: One-gapping 3-technique whose 2024 tape might have been a better representation of what he’s capable of than his 2025 tape. Marshall is a twitchy, athletic interior defender capable of creating disruption, but he doesn’t pop on tape enough. He’s not going to hold his ground and leverage gaps, so he’ll need to become better at utilizing his first-step quickness and hands to create early advantages. If Marshall can elevate his grit and urgency, he has a chance to become a rotational defender.
profiles.strengths:
• Compact frame with plus agility and overall athleticism.
  • Moves with good lateral quickness off the snap.
  • Capable of becoming a pest in the gaps if coached for it.
  • Adequate power in hips and hands to attack/neutralize base blocks.
  • Explosive closing speed in the pocket and down the line.
  • Rush hands are heavy enough to batter and dislodge the punch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs to become more willing to take on the heavy lifting against the run.
  • Ducks helmet and leans into first contact at the point of attack.
  • Didn’t show enough physicality against Kansas State’s O-line.
  • Should be creating more consistent chaos with his tools.
  • Hasn’t developed enough go-to moves or rush counters.
  • Too many centered rush attempts stifle his production.

profiles.overview: Kuwatch is a fifth-year senior who had only 14 career tackles before a 2025 breakout season (109 tackles, 10 TFLs, 5 sacks). He has good size and tested well at his pro day but lacks fluid on-field athleticism. His limited experience shows up in his need for improved block take-ons, but he does have a feel for finding running backs. Kuwatch has a chance to make some noise in camp and could compete for a practice squad spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Good size with impressive tackle production in 2025.
  • Posted NFL-caliber testing numbers at his pro day.
  • Good patience to wait and mirror runner’s cuts against zone blocks.
  • Plays firm behind his pads and with good physicality.
  • Gets low, squares up and wraps the legs as a tackler.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Only one season with significant production.
  • Lacks proportional wingspan relative to his height.
  • Needs to become more proactive attacking blocking schemes.
  • Below average take-on technique at the point of attack.
  • Below average lateral agility and foot quickness in space.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Virginia): Played in 12 games as a reserve QB/WR/TE/RB (10-56-5.6 rushing; 8-65-8.1 receiving).
  • 2022: Played in 12 games as a reserve and on special teams (29 tackles, 3 TFLs, FF). 
  • 2023: Redshirted. Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Played in 5 games with 4 starts (32 tackles, TFL, INT, 2 PBUs). Missed 8 games due to a Lisfranc (foot) injury suffered in the opener. Independence Bowl Defensive MVP (8 tackles, INT, FF) in win over California. 
  • 2024: First-team All-Big 12 Conference. Ranked third in the FBS with 77 solo tackles, tied for seventh with 127 tackles. Led team with 10.5 TFLs, 5 sacks. Tied for the team lead with 3 FFs. Started all 13 games (INT, 4 PBUs).
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-Big 12. Won the Bronko Nagurski Trophy (nation's top defender), Lombardi Award (nation's top lineman), Bednarik Award (nation's top defender) and Butkus Award (nation's top LB). Finalist for the Walter Camp Award (nation's top player), Lott IMPACT Trophy (nation's top defender with Integrity, Maturity, Performance, Academics, Community, Tenacity). Finished fifth in the Heisman Trophy voting. Led the FBS with 7 FFs. Led team with 128 tackles. Started all 14 games (11 TFLs with 1 sack, 4 INTs, 6 PBUs).
  • Miscellaneous: Wife, Emma, is a helicopter pilot in the U.S. Army. Father, Joe, served in the U.S. Army.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Rodriguez arrived in college as an offensive “athlete” and leaves Texas Tech as a bigger-than-life, stat-stuffing linebacker. He’s uniquely productive, with elite tackle, interception and forced fumble production. He’ll occasionally bounce out of a run fit when chasing action, but he has the burst to race back inside and finish. He’s slippery working off blocks and navigating combo climbers. His lateral pursuit leaves the station on time and with a fast take-off. Rodriguez displays ballhawking instincts and outstanding hands but busted coverages were part of the package in 2025. His unbridled urgency and “make every play” mindset can inflate missed tackle totals, but the production should outweigh the occasional headaches. He projects as a long-term starting inside linebacker.
profiles.strengths:
• Combines high tackle totals with plus on-ball production.
  • Posted 13 career forced fumbles, including FBS-leading seven in 2025.
  • Keys quickly and races to the junction point.
  • Rarely caught flat-footed in his lateral pursuit.
  • Constant movement makes him hard to hit for linemen.
  • Won’t drift deep into traffic without a plan of action.
  • Punches and plays off the block with excellent technique.
  • Has the instincts, eyes and ball skills of a greedy safety in coverage.
  • Field command and performance inspire those around him.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Can be knocked around inside the box by size.
  • Will occasionally false-step in the diagnose stage.
  • Will take a big bite on misdirection and play-action.
  • Coverage busts were costly in 2025.
  • Comes in hot to the catch, leading to overruns.
  • Lacks desired length for consistent wrap-ups.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted due to an Achilles injury.
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (47-272-5.8, 3 TDs rushing; 5-65-13.0, TD receiving; 10-344-34.4, TD KR).
  • 2024: Played in all 16 games as a reserve (120-746-6.2, 7 TDs rushing; 4-10-2.5 receiving).
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. Finalist for the Paul Hornung Award (nation's most versatile player). Tied for the FBS lead with 2 KR TDs. Played in all 12 games as a reserve (113-674-6.0, 11 TDs rushing; 6-87-14.5, 2 TDs receiving; 12-450-37.5, 2 TDs KR).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tempo-driven back with smooth hips, elite vision and a nose for the end zone. Price is a more natural runner than his heralded teammate, Jeremiyah Love, but Price lacks Love’s pure explosiveness and pass-catching talent. Price is highly instinctive, stacking moves to contour to run-lane spacing and avoid tacklers for as long as possible. He moves like a zone back but has average downhill burst for a one-cut runner. Price is an average run finisher, but he has the leg strength and contact balance to carry on when hits aren’t flush. His feel for finding the right path is rare and helps bolster his touchdown totals. Limited third-down value could cap his draft slotting, but his talent as a runner should make him an excellent complementary back.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “Stuck it out behind (Jeremiyah) Love and was a great teammate. He’s talented. I just wish he had more third-down value.” -- NFC personnel director
profiles.strengths:
• Buttery smooth with free-flowing movements on all levels.
  • Short-area footwork to make cuts with little hesitation or delay.
  • Vision and processing keep him one step ahead of the defense.
  • Able to pull the run off-track and recalibrate the route.
  • Runs with exceptional spatial awareness between the tackles.
  • Sneaky set-ups help him eliminate contain angles to the edge.
  • Gets to his top speed quickly.
  • Loose hips allow for sharp cuts across the grain.
  • Took three kickoffs to the house on just 22 career returns.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Fumbled near the goal line three times in 2025, losing two.
  • Average acceleration and top-end speed.
  • Contact power on the second level is average.
  • Eludes with cuts but has average wiggle in tight spaces.
  • Lacks dynamic production on third downs.
  • Suffered left Achilles rupture in summer of 2022.

profiles.overview: Rangy former safety still in the infant stages of learning the off-ball linebacker spot. Dugger has a stretched-out frame with exceptional length and room to add more muscle throughout. He’s inconsistent when it comes to diagnosing blocking schemes/play designs and needs significant work with block take-ons inside the box. He has the speed to run down wide-flowing backs and is an above-average wrap-and-finish tackler in space. The production and traits are intriguing, but Dugger needs more schooling and physical development before becoming an NFL linebacker.
profiles.strengths:
• Racked up 125 tackles – including 13 for loss – in 2025.
  • Has room on his frame for more muscle mass.
  • Rare length at linebacker with a 7-foot wingspan.
  • Has the range and athleticism to successfully track wide runs.
  • Effectively uses his length in wrapping and finishing in the open field.
  • Improved his feel for zone coverage as last season progressed.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Long-limbed but still too lean in his lower half.
  • Struggles to consistently read keys and diagnose play design.
  • Lacks base strength to maintain balance through contact.
  • Hasn’t learned to leverage his length against climbing blocks. 
  • Once blocked, tends to stay blocked.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Tulane): Played in 12 games with 10 starts (55 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, 2 INTs, 2 PBUs).
  • 2022 (Tulane): Started 8 games (20 tackles, TFL, 3 PBUs). Missed the end of the season due to a torn ACL and meniscus.
  • 2023 (Mississippi): Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve (2 tackles).
  • 2024 (Mississippi): Played in 12 games with 11 starts (38 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, 12 PBUs). Played CB, nickel, S.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in all 15 games with 13 starts at nickel (39 tackles, TFL, 2 INTs, 6 PBUs, FF).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Braxton, was a Florida 3A state champion in the 300-meter hurdles and ran track at Oregon and Florida State.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Canady carries a slender frame with short arms but is brimming with confidence as a sticky slot option. He plays with a rare feel for route breaks, frequently sliding his feet to cut direction in advance. He quickly closes distance with a twitchy burst and well-timed contact upon throw arrival. He’s quicker than fast and best from short zone/off-man alignments, allowing his instincts to do their thing. He gets jostled around by bigger players at the top of the route and will have his tackling tested by opposing run games out of 11 personnel. Canady is worth a late Day 2 or early Day 3 pick as a future starting slot corner.
profiles.strengths:
• Smooth transitions playing from a pedal or shuffle.
  • Impressive closing acceleration to receivers and throws.
  • Light on his feet anticipating and shading break points.
  • Very decisive and committed in his coverage decisions.
  • High-end competitor who brings real juice to the field.
  • Rarely out of phase, ending catches with immediacy.
  • Hustles into contain positioning when action spills wide.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Possesses a slender frame with short arms.
  • Displays small delays flipping hips and sprinting.
  • Gets knocked around at the top of the route by size.
  • Lack of length could limit interception opportunities.
  • Will have trouble ungluing from big perimeter blockers.
  • Drag-down tackler, lacking desired stopping power.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 3 games as a reserve.
  • 2023: Played in 12 games with starts in the final 9 contests at RG.
  • 2024: Started 12 games at RG. Injured in the team's ReliaQuest Bowl loss to Michigan. 
  • 2025: Played in 10 games with 4 starts at RG. Missed part of training camp and season opener with a concussion.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Roberts is a powerful guard-only prospect with elite body composition but technique that falls below the NFL mark. He has legendary weight-room strength that will flash on tape, but he struggles to play under control and cleanly fit blocks. Quick losses populate the tape as often as good wins. Roberts isn’t a bad athlete, but he lacks bend and body control that sees him end up off-balance too often in both phases. His pass protection can be improved with better patience and posture, but the mental busts could be a problem. Roberts’ traits give him a chance. Sticking with a team might be a challenge, though.
profiles.strengths:
• Elite body composition with lean mass and a huge wingspan.
  • Possesses rare strength.
  • Even with subpar technique, he can move defensive players.
  • Gets easy wash downs on angle blocks when catching them flush.
  • Upper-body power can stop the rush cold when hands lock in.
  • Rush attempts down the middle will go nowhere.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Footwork fitting up his blocks is uneven and unsound.
  • Below-average body control and bend at the point and in space.
  • Ends up on the grass way more than he should.
  • Gaming fronts create confusion and busts in protection.
  • Takes quick losses when rushers counter his lunging.
  • Dealt with injuries in each of the last two years.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve. Enrolled in January.
  • 2022: SEC All-Freshman Team. Started all 13 games at LG.
  • 2023: Started 12 games (3 at C, 9 at RG).
  • 2024: Started 10 games at LG. Missed 2 games due to injury.
  • 2025: Started all 12 games at C.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Durable fifth-year senior who has made 47 consecutive starts. Burton is built to play center but could offer swing potential at guard. He has adequate play strength and good quickness for a zone-blocking scheme. He gets beaten to first contact by length and will struggle to put up a sustained fight against two-gappers at the point. He can slow a bull rush but needs to do a better job of protecting his edges and operating with consistent posture. Burton’s best fit will be with a zone-heavy running game as a late draft pick or undrafted free agent signee.
profiles.strengths:
• Hits NFL marks for measurables at his position.
  • Wins the lateral race to his zone landmarks.
  • Climbs quickly with athletic adjustments in space.
  • Uses core power and grip strength to secure his blocks.
  • Alters punch timing and approach, using independent hands.
  • Adequate anchor drop to slow bull rushers when tested.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Weight gets too far forward as a run blocker. 
  • Pressed and pulled aside by two-gappers.
  • Gets beaten into the frame more than he wins.
  • Ducks helmet into contact with pass rushers.
  • Has troubling redirecting long rushers off his edge.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Maryland): Freshman All-American. Led team with 6.5 TFL. Tied for the team lead with 4 sacks. Started 12 games (58 tackles, 4 sacks, PBU, FF).
  • 2023 (Maryland): Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started 11 games (37 tackles, 3 sacks, INT, PBU).
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (66 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 PBUs).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Played in 12 games with 11 starts (32 tackles, 10 TFLs with 4 sacks, 3 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Barham logged most of his snaps at off-ball linebacker, but his 2025 tape showed explosiveness that will attract teams seeking a developmental rush ‘backer in an odd front. He’s raw as a rusher, relying heavily on athleticism, but the missing elements are teachable. Whether outside or inside, he’s a professional block-beater with the tools to stack or slip blocks, though his edge-setting needs work. His bend and reactive agility create unlikely tackle chances that few can find. His intensity and motor are top-tier but he needs to play with better discipline to avoid negative snaps. With explosive traits and inside-outside versatility, he projects as an impactful future starter once his technique catches up.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “His position is just going to depend on scheme. For what we do, he’s going to play off the ball but I’m sure there will be teams who put him on the board as an edge.” - AFC national scout
profiles.strengths:
• Impresses off the bus with prototypical size, length and musculature.
  • Pairs disruptive traits and playing style with a salty demeanor.
  • Capable of lining up as an inside linebacker or stand-up edge.
  • Delivers knock-back pop to blockers and can quickly shed.
  • Plays through or around blocks without losing positioning.
  • His first three steps are sudden and threatening as a rusher.
  • Dips, rips and flattens the edge against slower tackles.
  • Elite bend and reactive agility allow him to tackle from unlikely angles.
  • Smooth and rangy with his spot drops in coverage.
  • Remarkable stop-start quickness when changing direction.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Takes chances inside that lead to loss of contain for the defense.
  • Frenetic playing style can lead to missteps and missed tackles.
  • Buzzes over top of the pocket instead of finding the drop depth.
  • Rush features reactive movement but lacks instinctive hand counters.
  • Aggression can work against him with 15-yard penalties.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Central Arkansas): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (4 tackles). Suffered a torn meniscus.
  • 2022 (Central Arkansas): Played in all 11 games as a reserve (37 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 1 sack, FF).
  • 2023 (Central Arkansas): Led team with 84 tackles. Started all 11 games (7 TFLs with 4.5 sacks, FF). 
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Played in all 12 games with 8 starts (58 tackles, 7 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, 2 PBUs, 2 FFs). 
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12. Led team with 105 tackles. Started 12 games (6 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, 3 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Golday is a big, explosive linebacker with a game best suited for work near the line of scrimmage. He attacks climbing blockers with heavy, aggressive hands. He also shows the strength to stack, compress gaps and finish with authority. While his performance at the point of attack stands out, he can be a little late diagnosing play design and needs to work with a more preemptive downhill trigger at times. He’s more powerful than elusive as a blitzer and is average in coverage. Golday’s traits, explosiveness and field demeanor should make him an early special teams standout with the potential to eventually start at Sam or inside linebacker.
profiles.strengths:
• Explosive athlete with impressive size.
  • Attacks blocks and constricts run flow with heavy hands.
  • Scrapes with tempo alterations to leverage the run.
  • Effective use of hands to play off blockers and make sudden tackles.
  • Comes to balance and has good stopping power as a tackler.
  • Not easily manipulated out of his zone by the quarterback’s eyes.
  • Can immediately step in as a kick-cover talent.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average quickness to diagnose and read the play design.
  • Will work under blocks and lose the angle on occasion.
  • Needs a quicker downhill trigger to blow up the blocking scheme.
  • Long legs with average short-area agility in coverage.
  • Could struggle covering running backs if asked.
  • Linear pass rusher with below-average elusiveness.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2023: Played in all 12 games with 8 starts.
  • 2024: First-team Associated Press All-American. Started all 13 games.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-SEC. Finalist for the Rimington Trophy (nation's top C). Started all 12 games.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Jack, played OL at Tennessee-Martin.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Two-year team captain and three-year starter with plenty of game experience against high-end talent. Slaughter lacks desired build/mass but plays with adequate play strength and solid technique. He’s consistent at finding and sustaining his outside zone blocks. He works to neutralize opponents on downhill blocks but is unlikely to move pro bodies around. He has the feet for gap control in pass pro but will struggle some against pure bull rushers. What he lacks in traits he makes up for with awareness and football IQ, which gives him a chance to become an NFL backup.
profiles.strengths:
• Accelerates and runs feet through contact on outside zone blocks.
  • Has ability to reach and seal play-side 1-techniques.
  • Quick eyes allow him to adjust assignments suddenly when needed.
  • Typically strains through the block until he gets to the finish line.
  • Light on his feet to slide and protect against edge-to-edge rushers.
  • Lands firm hands into pass rusher to set the tone for the rep.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Narrow shoulders with below-average mass for the position.
  • Rarely gets much displacement when asked to drive block.
  • Has to guard against lunging at linebackers on second level.
  • Occasionally a step slow responding to incoming twisters.
  • Might not have the anchor to handle bull rushers heads-up.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Middle Tennessee State): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Middle Tennessee State): Played in 12 games with 3 starts (37 tackles, TFL, 4 INTs-1 returned for TD, 3 PBUs, FF).
  • 2023 (Middle Tennessee State): Played in 11 games with 10 starts (71 tackles, 3 TFLs, 5 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024 (Tennessee): Played in all 13 games as a reserve (22 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 PBUs).
  • 2025: Second-team All-ACC. Tied for seventh in the FBS with 5 INTs. Defensive MVP of the College Football Playoff semifinal win over Ole Miss (5 tackles, 2 PBUs). Started all 16 games (76 tackles, 4 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, 6 PBUs, 2 FFs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A productive, fifth-year safety prospect, Thomas is wired to play forward and race into the action wherever it is present. He overflows pursuit and has too many missed or broken tackles on his stat sheet, but his impact against the run is a net positive. He has good ball production but is fairly average in coverage. He can be way too quick to overlap or bite on bait, which allows receivers to get behind him from single-high and split-safety alignments. Thomas has the potential to develop into a starter as a likely middle-round pick.
profiles.strengths:
• Disguises intentions, dropping down late as an add-on defender.
  • Times up snap count to rocket off the edge and into the backfield.
  • Ready and willing to explode into lead blocks.
  • Triggers from depth to meet the action near the line.
  • Career production includes 16 pass breakups and nine interceptions.
  • Above-average range and reaction as short-zone defender.
  • Sees block and route development with impressive peripheral vision.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Allows receivers to get behind him more than he should.
  • Burst to close and make-up speed in coverage are below average.
  • Loses pursuit leverage when he’s too hurried running the alley.
  • Tight-hipped and lacking desired lateral burst and agility.
  • Ignites his tackle try before closing enough distance.

profiles.overview: When healthy, Catalon has been an impactful starter, but he's a seventh-year senior with an extensive injury history. He plays with physicality near the line and is an imposing hitter. He shows good field awareness and ball skills but lacks vertical speed and ideal length. Special-teams cover talent gives him a boost but his age and injury history could be stumbling blocks.
profiles.strengths:
• Violent striker.
  • Gets his head around to locate downfield throws.
  • Plays with good awareness and ball skills.
  • Toughness to play near the line full-time.
  • Comes downhill and through tackle targets in run support.
  • Productive tackler on kick-cover teams.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Stubby build with a lack of ideal wingspan.
  • Durability and history of shoulder injuries could be a concern.
  • Lacks acceleration to stay connected to vertical speed.
  • Below-average length to defend against jump balls.
  • Hip tightness limits lateral agility as an open-field tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Florida): Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Florida): Played in 2 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Started all 12 games at RG.
  • 2025: Started all 12 games at RG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A two-year starting right guard, Farmer's run blocking is ahead of his pass protection. He isn’t broad or girthy, but he features a compact point of power and good core strength. He’s a plus drive blocker capable of leveraging and finishing his work but sees diminishing returns when blocking in space. Farmer will block what is in front of him in protection but frequently stalls his feet when punching, allowing active rushers to slip into his edges and find the pocket. He’s capable when working duo and man-to-man blocks downhill, but his ceiling will be defined by his improvement in pass protection.
profiles.strengths:
• Stays low with pad level in proper position.
  • Drives through hips to lift and push base blocks.
  • Shows off knock-back pop on lead pulls.
  • Feet stay busy through contact.
  • Patient with hands and rarely lunges after the rusher.
  • Gets good extension to maximize length when punching.
  • Good anchor drop after initial bounce into pocket.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Stays low but can get too far out over his toes.
  • Hands can drift wide of the frame as a run blocker.
  • Has trouble finding cut-off angles up to linebackers.
  • Lacks awareness of developing games in protection.
  • Needs to keep feet active through his pass punch.
  • Struggles staying mirrored to and redirecting attacks on his edge.

profiles.overview: Seventh-year senior with enticing disruption potential but only a single season of meaningful production. Hunt primarily played the 5-technique in Cincinnati’s odd front, but he’s suited for work as a penetrating nose tackle in an even front. He’s a plus athlete with quickness to beat blockers to the spot and dart into gaps or around base blocks. He has the foot quickness to test the gap-to-gap range of a center when aligned inside. His age, production and injury history might hurt his draft chances, but his style of play and athletic ability give him a chance to compete as a rotational, one-gapping nose tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• First-step quickness to threaten gaps as a penetrator.
  • Leverage and burst to play through seal blocks laterally.
  • Drives upward hand strikes into first contact with good pop.
  • Shows foot quickness to work around base blocks and threaten edges as a rusher.
  • Was a plus tester across the board at his pro day.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Only one season of production as a full-time starter.
  • Below-average anchor to sink and fight back against double-teams.
  • Lacks control and overruns tackles/sacks once he’s in the backfield.
  • Injury history is part of his evaluation.
  • Will be a 25-year-old rookie.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Bowling Green): Played in 9 games as a reserve (7 tackles).
  • 2023 (Bowling Green): First-team All-MAC. Led team with 4 INTs, 6 PBUs. Started 12 games (52 tackles, TFL).
  • 2024: Tied for the team lead with 3 INTs. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts (4 at CB, 7 at S; 45 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, PBU, blocked kick).
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big Ten Conference. Tied for the team lead with 4 INTs. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts. (72 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 2 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-year starting split-field safety with adequate size but deficient speed. Huskey piled up interceptions, showing his ball skills and instincts. However, he’s slow to accelerate from transitions and lacks quality make-up speed, so receivers can get open and stay open when he’s forced to match them. He’s not a thumper but does his job near the line of scrimmage as a run defender. Huskey’s ball production and willingness in run support will be counter-balanced by his lack of speed/short-area quickness in coverage. A back-end roster spot could be his ceiling.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 11 interceptions in the last three seasons.
  • Aware of route development but plays the quarterback.
  • Able to slip or defeat blocks near the line of scrimmage.
  • Runs the alley with timely gathering for control into tackles.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Slow to find the accelerator on his lateral transitions.
  • Lacks top-end speed to carry routes vertically.
  • Loses ground and pursuit angles as the run progresses wide.
  • Struggles making sharp change of direction in downhill run support.

profiles.overview: McMurray is a fifth-year senior and nickel cornerback with slightly below-average size but adequate quickness. He’s a trustworthy tackler in run support and plays with consistent toughness. McMurray tends to play reactive football in zone coverage and can be a step slow in shading break points from off man. He lacks anticipation and instincts, limiting his on-ball opportunities. Teams will like his wiring but his lack of size and ball skills hurt his chances.
profiles.strengths:
• Shows twitchiness once he triggers.
  • Good change of direction to flow with routes and runs.
  • Fights hard to work off of or around blockers.
  • Very willing and tough in run support.
  • Targets and wraps the legs to finish off running backs.
  • Has experience as both a gunner and jammer.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lone collegiate interception came in 2022.
  • Below-average instincts and route anticipation.
  • Struggles to trust his eyes and trigger with timing from zone.
  • Has trouble finding positioning to play downfield throws.
  • Mindset for run-support duties but carries a leaner frame.

profiles.overview: Stroman is an aggressive player who might need to star on special teams to make a squad. He can handle some man coverage but struggles on the back end, where technique and route recognition are not his strong suits. He needs to play with more patience on downhill run fills but he strikes ball-carriers with force. He fits as a “robber” where he can play forward against short throws and race in against the run. He has immediate special teams value and elements of his game on defense might be worth continued development.
profiles.strengths:
• Rockets downhill, erasing distance from split-safety perch to support run.
  • Makes pursuit adjustments on the move to center and strike the runner.
  • Drives through the running back’s thighs to make quick stops.
  • Burst to close provides hope for better on-ball production.
  • Runs through pass-catchers underneath with a full head of steam.
  • Traits and skill set are made for kick/punt cover teams.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Missed all of 2024 with an injury and made just 12 career starts.
  • Has trouble navigating traffic caused by bunch formations.
  • Magnet for play-action fakes and is pulled out of position.
  • Takes steep angles rushing toward his man-cover duties.
  • Plays with a lack of technique on the back end.
  • Rushes into a run lane without allowing the runner to declare.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Hawaii): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (Hawaii): Played in 11 games with 6 starts (27-333-12.3, TD).
  • 2023 (Hawaii): Played in 5 games with 3 starts (10-125-12.5, TD).
  • 2024: First-team All-Southland Conference. Ranked third in the FCS with 1,290 receiving yards (85 receptions, 15.2 per) and tied for third with 14 receiving TDs. Started all 14 games. Went viral for a TD celebration where he stood on his head, inspired by a dance move from the movie "Stomp the Yard." NFL WRs Drake London and Amon-Ra St. Brown repeated the celebration the following day.
  • 2025: First-team All-Southland Conference. Ranked fourth in the FCS with 7 receptions per game and 10th with 84.7 receiving yards per game. Led team with 70 receptions, 847 receiving yards (12.1 per), 8 receiving TDs. Started 10 games (4-50-12.5 rushing). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Productive two-year starter at Incarnate Word after transferring from Hawaii. Walthall is an explosive athlete with a second gear as a vertical target. He needs coaching to develop his press release and more route polish to find increased separation as a pro. He has a good feel near the boundary and makes acrobatic catches but lacks ideal hand strength to secure catches through contact. Walthall has tools to tinker with but it’s unclear if he can handle the step up in competition that awaits him.
profiles.strengths:
• Explosive leaper and former Texas state champ in the triple jump.
  • Quick change of direction to beat man coverage on underneath routes.
  • Smooth but sudden transitions in his route breaks.
  • Able to drop hips and open quickly on comeback routes.
  • Capable of rising tall and pulling in spectacular grabs.
  • Good feel for boundary, deadening feet to dot the turf.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Unable to do much against talented Stephen F. Austin cornerbacks. 
  • Hasn’t developed an NFL-caliber release versus press.
  • Needs to work back sooner to underthrown passes.
  • Doesn’t consistently utilize best play speed in his routes.
  • Not strong enough as a run blocker.

profiles.bio:
• 2020: Played in 7 games with 6 starts (76-152-50.0, 718 yards, TD, 4 INTs passing; 73-20-0.3, 3 TDs rushing).
  • 2021: Played in 6 games with starts in the final 3 contests (81-117-69.2, 860 yards, 7 TDs, 3 INTs passing; 33-83-2.5, 3 TDs rushing).
  • 2022: Started 9 games (152-231-65.8, 2,014 yards, 18 TDs, 4 INTs passing; 77-419-5.4, 7 TDs rushing). Missed 4 games with a shoulder injury. Threw for a school-record 544 passing yards in the AutoZone Liberty Bowl against Arkansas, tied the school record with 5 TDs passes. Team captain.
  • 2023: Redshirted. Started 3 early-season games (56-75-74.7, 705 yards, 5 TDs, INT passing; 27-74-2.7 rushing). Missed the rest of the season with a back injury. Team captain.
  • 2024: Big 12 Conference Co-Scholar-Athlete of the Year. Ranked sixth in the FBS with 14.4 yards per completion. Started all 12 games (171-300-57.0, 2,454 yards, 14 TDs, 12 INTs passing; 93-447-4.8, 6 TDs rushing). Team captain.
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (198-319-62.1, 2,531 yards, 22 TDs, 7 INTs passing; 117-404-3.5, 4 TDs rushing). Finalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy, aka the Academic Heisman. Became first four-time team captain in school history.
  • Miscellaneous: Nickname is "JD6", his initials and jersey number. Started "MOM2JD6 Foundation" in honor of his mother, Star, to aid single mothers raising athletic children through mentorship, training, financial aid and community resources.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior who was unable to live up to the promise shown earlier in his career. Daniels hasn’t shown the ability to consistently dissect defenses and win with accuracy from the pocket. He has a decent arm but lacks consistent mechanics, timing and three-level ball placement. The vast majority of his interceptions were due to a lack of coverage recognition. Daniels’ running ability helps, but he appears ill-prepared for an NFL passing game.
profiles.strengths:
• Shows ability to throw with adequate anticipation.
  • Enough arm talent to push the ball vertically when needed.
  • Throws with decent touch on deep fades.
  • Plus escapability to break the pocket or extend plays.
  • Moves the sticks as a scrambler and on designed runs.
  • Above-average vision and cut quickness as a runner.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Forces throws into no-win windows.
  • Poor feel for the range of deep safeties.
  • Footwork unravels on occasion, even without heavy pressure.
  • Below-average ball placement on short/intermediate timing throws.
  • Inconsistent finding and hitting intermediate zone windows.
  • Disappointing accuracy when extending pass plays.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. SEC All-Freshman Team. Played in all 12 games with starts in the final 11 contests (76 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, INT, 6 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024: Tied for fourth in the FBS with 5 INTs. Played in all 13 games with 11 starts (48 tackles, 3 TFLs, 5 PBUs).
  • 2025: Second-team All-SEC. Led team with 10 PBUs. Tied for team lead with 2 INTs. Started 11 games (54 tackles). 
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Gerald, plays DB at South Carolina.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Kilgore is a big, long defensive back with nickelback or down safety value depending on scheme fit. He's played an overhang "Star" role, covering slot receivers and supporting the run, but he’ll be at his best in the pros covering tight ends and containing run games near the box. He could see split-field safety snaps if a staff trusts him on the back end, but he will be better off paired with a rangy single-high safety. Missed tackles need to be cleaned up but his wingspan, agility and play strength should keep his tackle totals high from year to year. Kilgore has the traits, ball production and versatility to counter the burgeoning tight end craze, making him a likely Day 2 pick with early starting potential.
profiles.strengths:
• Big defensive back with long arms and explosive lowers.
  • Posted eight interceptions and 21 pass breakups in his three college seasons.
  • Can stall tight ends and big slot receivers from press.
  • Rangy zone cover man with good vision and anticipation.
  • Closes quickly and lands a heavy blow on receivers after the catch.
  • Swallows receiver with long arms and full wrap when making a tackle.
  • Has plenty of stopping power as a run defender.
  • Plus balance and reactive agility as an open-field tackler.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Good play speed for a safety but not for a cornerback.
  • Average transition burst matching route breaks.
  • Turns the motor down when he’s away from the play.
  • Below average playing off of blocks for a player his size.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (33-223-6.8, 2 TDs rushing).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games as a reserve and on special teams (41-201-4.9, TD rushing; 4-73-18.3, TD receiving).
  • 2024: Led the team's RBs with 668 rushing yards (145 carries, 4.6 per, 7 TDs). Played in all 13 games with 7 starts (16-155-9.7, TD receiving).
  • 2025: Played in 11 games with 8 starts (130-504-3.9, 3 TDs rushing; 19-109-5.7 receiving). Suffered a dislocated collarbone in fall camp and a lower-leg injury in the Iron Bowl against Auburn.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Miller has pro-caliber size but while some runners get what is blocked, Miller didn’t always take what was there for him. He’s a segmented runner with adequate power but lacks the vision, burst and decisiveness to rip through creases inside. He’s a hard runner and can get tough yards after contact here and there. He’s not talented enough as a blocker or pass-catcher to play on third downs, so starring on special teams might be required to become an NFL backup.
profiles.strengths:
• Good build with low center of gravity and strong lower half.
  • Creates lateral space with jump-cut.
  • Able to plant and cut sharply downhill on wide runs.
  • Gets through the line with good bend and forward lean.
  • Uses off hand to ward off closing tacklers in space.
  • Had success covering kicks and punts in 2023.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Segmented running style slows downhill progress.
  • Lacks desired vision and feel for lane development.
  • Below-average burst to outflank defenses and turn the corner.
  • Indecisive runner with a lack of spatial awareness.
  • Breaks some tackles but doesn’t create many misses.

profiles.overview: Stocky and strong with a lot of experience but a concerning decline in production in the last two seasons. Haynes might be on the short side but he’s plenty durable to handle interior carries. His pro day testing showed off a big burst gear but his indecisiveness when reading the front tends to dull that burst. He has quick feet and good stop-start quickness but failed to elude tacklers over the first two levels often enough in 2025. He has stiff hands and struggles with pass-pro duties, so he might need to prove himself as a kick returner to compete for a spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Stocky but well-built and strong in his lower half.
  • Good stop-start quickness to recalibrate his run.
  • Shows an ability to make sharp cuts across the grain.
  • Displays an aptitude for running routes underneath.
  • Showed rare burst at his pro day.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Production has diminished in consecutive seasons.
  • Dances and slows when processing block development.
  • Below-average wiggle to elude second-level tacklers.
  • Lacks feel for setting up blocks and creating opportunities for himself.
  • Catches with stiff hands and subpar hand-eye coordination.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Alabama): Redshirted. 
  • 2022 (Alabama): Played in 2 games as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Alabama): Played in all 14 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2024 (TCU): Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Started 12 games.
  • 2025: Third-team All-ACC. Started all 16 games.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Blake, was an All-American OT at Texas and played 9 years in the NFL after being selected in the first round of the 1995 draft by the Panthers.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Undersized center prospect with NFL bloodlines, admirable grit and above-average intelligence. Brockermeyer has the technique and core strength to fight as a downhill blocker but his impact in the run game is likely to be limited to occupying/neutralizing. In protection, his success rate climbs against pure bull-rushers thanks to his hand usage and protection know-how. However, a lack of length will limit his ability to redirect athletic rushers if they find his edge. Brockermeyer was outstanding at the Senior Bowl, but he’s a one-position player, so he’ll have to fight hard for a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Very precise with initial hand placement as a run blocker.
  • Keeps feet churning to stay engaged and occupy the defender.
  • Capable lead puller with the mobility to climb and cut off inside ‘backers.
  • Plays with steady balance and consistent base width in protection.
  • Maintains arm extension and feel for A-gap leakage in pass pro.
  • Inside hands and core strength help him set a firm anchor.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks ideal size and can be mismatched by true 0-techniques.
  • Lacks pop on contact to set the tone as a run blocker.
  • Doesn’t generate enough leg drive to displace on single blocks.
  • Could struggle to stay latched to longer, NFL-caliber two-gappers.
  • Below-average lateral range to save his edge against athletic rushers.
  • Needs to stay square and catch-ready when passing off twists.

profiles.overview: Interior defender with heavy hands and a frame for additional mass. Thompson is experienced and capable of playing in even or odd fronts. Tight hips limit his bend at the point of attack, creating inconsistent leverage, but the play strength and hand usage are in place. He’ll give effort as a rusher but he lacks tools to create NFL pressure. Thompson projects as a late-round pick or undrafted free agent.
profiles.strengths:
• His strongest run-stopping performance came versus talented Ohio State team.
  • Quick read and lateral response to zone steps by O-linemen.
  • Displays solid pop into first contact.
  • Lands accurate hands and quickly presses into extension.
  • Shuffles feet to work his way around turn-out blocks.
  • Activates his hands early in the rush rep.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average feel for pressure on his edges.
  • Knocked off balance and out of position by double-teams.
  • Needs to drop pad level and widen base when battling move blocks.
  • Tight-hipped with limited lateral strides to work rush edges.
  • Unable to manufacture enough openings into the pocket.
  • Suffered an Achilles injury in 2020 and missed all but one game in 2024 with a pectoral injury.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (24 tackles, TFL, FF).
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games with starts in the first 9 games (62 tackles, 6 TFLs with 2 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 1 start (17 tackles).
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started all 13 games (44-533-12.1 receiving; 1 tackle). Moved from LB to TE prior to season.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Kanak went from run-first high school quarterback to college linebacker, then flipped to tight end for his final season. He’s undersized and his run blocking isn’t on a functional level yet. As a receiver, there is plenty of room for improvement as a route-runner, but he already shows the toughness, hands and catch focus of a veteran at the position. A lack of size and versatility makes him a niche prospect, but the production, special-teams value and likely improvement as a route-runner could get him drafted.
profiles.strengths:
• Impressive catch production for a single season at tight end.
  • Keeps his pace up throughout the route.
  • Sits quickly and shows his numbers in short zone.
  • Excellent hand-eye coordination and catch focus.
  • Adjustments to off-frame throws come naturally.
  • Experienced four-phase special-teams option.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Small and lacking length even by H-back standards.
  • Has trouble separating from man coverage underneath.
  • Very limited catch radius requires an accurate passer.
  • Starting at ground floor with run-blocking technique/fundamentals.
  • Appears to lack willingness for collisions necessary as move blocker.

profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior and team captain with 41 career starts spanning every position on the offensive line. Kump relies on his upper-body power and tenacity to make up for his athletic limitations. While he’s physical as a run blocker in tight quarters, it appears he lacks the foot quickness to handle athletic interior rushers at the pro level.
profiles.strengths:
• Big center with outstanding length and 11-inch hands.
  • Fits run blocks with good hand placement and base width.
  • Connects and chops his feet through the whistle.
  • Good recognition against internal twists and blitzes.
  • Throws punch with purpose in pass pro.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average snap-to-step quickness in run game.
  • Movements in space are segmented and clunky.
  • Struggles adjusting to movement as both run and pass blocker. 
  • Leans and loses against early movement to his edges in protection.
  • Unable to match up against athletic rushers one-on-one.

profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with enough flashes to warrant a longer look. Loving has average size and short arms but his elite testing numbers are evident on tape. He has knock-back pop and can stall out single blocks while giving a good fight against double-teams. He can be a step slow in shedding blocks and will find himself engulfed when he’s not first in with his hands. His foot quickness and rare acceleration allow him to burst to ball-carriers and quarterbacks at a high rate of speed. Loving’s rush is fueled by athleticism over skill and he’ll need to improve the latter to win at a higher rate in the league. He has late-round potential and could surprise in a roster battle.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses a rare blend of quickness and explosiveness.
  • Plays with knock-back pop and ability to battle double-teams.
  • Slide quickness to elude blocks in short spaces.
  • Flashes big-time burst to run down the line and capture ball-carriers.
  • Acceleration inside the pocket to close out against quarterbacks.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Short arms fall below the NFL standard.
  • Play is too upright and lacks proper knee/hip bend.
  • Unable to consistently shed blocks with timing.
  • Struggles to create vertical rush openings on his own.
  • Needs to improve hand usage and craft go-to rush moves.

profiles.overview: Right tackle prospect with average size and length. Williams plays with a taller pad level than teams will like and displays some tightness in his lower half.
