  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts (13-108-8.4). Team's Most Improved Player of the Year on Offense.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in 11 games with 6 starts (24-248-10.3, TD). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: German-born prospect with average athleticism in space but above-average grit at the point. Klein’s tape shouldn’t be viewed as a finished product considering his relative lack of game experience in the sport. He needs to block with inside hands but displays a sturdy core and strong hands to do his job in-line. He builds speed with long strides and will catch what is provided. More muscle mass is needed, but Klein has a chance to become a Day 3 pick as a backup “Y” tight end.
profiles.strengths:
• Voted team captain for 2025.
  • Creates leverage points to strike from.
  • Accelerates through contact and runs his feet.
  • Strong hands allow for longer sustains once he’s in.
  • Efficient eluding traffic and keeping routes on time.
  • Adjusted catch-timing to the barrage of fastballs he saw.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Relatively new to the game, making just 12 college starts.
  • Light production includes one career touchdown.
  • Long-legged and gradual through route turns. 
  • Must become more forceful at clearing out catch space.
  • Hands fly out wide into contact on too many run blocks.
  • Forward lean diminishes mirror effectiveness in pass pro.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Georgia): Played in 13 games as a reserve for the national champions (4 tackles, sack).
  • 2023 (Georgia): Played in 12 games with 1 start (12 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 1 sack, FF).
  • 2024 (Florida State): Played in all 11 games with 9 starts (25 tackles, 6 TFLs with 4 sacks, FF).
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 9 starts (21 tackles, 5 TFLs with 2 sacks, PBU).
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Marvin, was a two-time All-American and Florida State Athletics Hall of Fame LB who won the Butkus and Lombardi Awards and finished fourth in the 1992 Heisman Trophy voting before playing in the NFL for 10 years. Cousin, Fredrick, also played LB at Florida State.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Jones is a former five-star recruit who played at three schools (Georgia, Florida State, Oklahoma) over the last three seasons. He has good size and comes from NFL bloodlines. His play strength and aggression at the point of attack are average, but his hands stay active and he gets off blocks when needed. So far, Jones has not been able to convert his traits into high-level production. His rush plan and toolbox do not stand out on tape.
profiles.strengths:
• Comes from NFL bloodlines with a father who played in the NFL for 10 seasons.
  • Sets up workable spin counter at the top of the rush.
  • Adequate closing speed when chasing quarterbacks.
  • Lands hands first and sets an adequate edge.
  • Plays off blocks when he’s ready to pursue or tackle.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average pad level and leverage at the point.
  • Needs to play with better strength and aggression versus the run.
  • One-speed rush rarely creates uncertainty for tackles.
  • Tightness prevents desired bend-and-flatten at the edge.
  • Lack of short-area agility and entry accuracy leads to missed tackles.

profiles.overview: Randolph is a 38-game starter carrying a compact build and above-average power. He has a strong core and contact balance that allows him to meet strength with strength at the point. His hands stay inside and he’s consistently in a state of leverage. He has limited range, though. Longer defenders can separate and work around him for quick wins. He has trouble matching post-snap movement in the run game and edge attacks in protection. Randolph’s strength and experience are checkmarks in his favor, but there might be too many holes in his overall game right now.
profiles.strengths:
• Has big, strong hands and a compact frame.
  • Strong at the point of attack with above-average contact balance.
  • Latches in with his hands and stays connected to the block.
  • Hand placement, leverage and powerful hips help him clear run gaps.
  • Keeps his inside hand in leveraged position during protection.
  • Absorbs bull rushers without giving much ground.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average foot quickness and athleticism.
  • Lacks snap-to-step quickness in the run game.
  • Players with length can separate and earn quick wins against him at the point.
  • Below-average slide quickness to seal gaps in pass pro.
  • Mirroring loopers after pass-offs will be challenging.
  • Tight hips limit his ability to open and recover.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Louisville): Played in 1 game as a reserve walk-on.
  • 2021 (Louisville): Played in 9 games as a reserve (9 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, FF).
  • 2022 (Louisville): Played in 13 games as a reserve (18 tackles, 7 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU, 2 FFs). Placed on scholarship prior to the season.
  • 2023 (Louisville): Played in 10 games with 2 starts (22 tackles, 6 TFLs with 5 sacks, 2 PBUs, FF).
  • 2024 (Louisville): Redshirted due to a knee injury. Had a bone graft placed into his knee.
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (33 tackles, 6 TFLs with 5 sacks, PBU).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Reiger is a tall, linear edge rusher with a slender frame. He doesn’t look like a pro pre-snap, but he certainly plays like one after the snap. He lacks the size/anchor to consistently set the edge and can be controlled when tackles latch on, but he’s unusually talented to work off contact for quick wins at the point of attack. He’s a short-striding rusher who takes similar tracks at similar speeds and is more pressure-creator than sack-finisher at this time. However, altering his approach (tempo and angles) and adding a better inside counter could create a bump in his sack production. Reiger needs more mass and refinement but could become a good rotational odd-front edge in time.
profiles.strengths:
• Upfield movements are highly efficient in both phases.
  • Inside spin at pocket depth finds pressures.
  • Hands and feet to hit well-timed inside rush moves.
  • Quick wins at the point with footwork or shock-and-slip move.
  • Twitchy and strong when he wants to shed the block.
  • Relentless in his pursuit of the ball-carrier.
  • Uses big hands and good length to disengage when captured.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Short-strider who needs more steps getting to the corner.
  • Not equipped for consistent speed-to-power conversions.
  • Rush hands are active but lack displacement power.
  • Knocked around when he ends up inside the box.
  • Strong in-line tight ends can neutralize him at times.
  • Gets widened off his spot by kick-out blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Wake Forest): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Wake Forest): Played in all 13 games as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Wake Forest): Played in 12 games with 11 starts at RG.
  • 2024 (Wake Forest): Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 12 games (11 at LG, 1 at C).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started 11 games at C. Missed final game due to injury. Team Captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-year starter with average size and good power. Gulbin is better at climbing to linebackers than he is at moving laterally to seal in the run game. He can be outreached at the point, but he stays tight to his block to reduce length disadvantages. He excels when washing away targets on inside-zone plays with strong leg drive. He anchors well in protection, but he must stay square and be more alert to loopers on twists. Short arms reduce his margin for error but his consistent body of work suggests he has a chance to make a roster as a center who can swing to guard in a pinch.
profiles.strengths:
• Very consistent during three-year run as a starter.
  • Hand placement and leg drive make it easier to clear out gaps. 
  • Takes good angles to linebackers and adjusts to their movement.
  • Pushed the Michigan front around with his drive blocking.
  • Base width and posture stay steady through protection rep.
  • Dense and firm on contact to set solid anchors against power.
  • Powerful shoves redirect blitzers off their track.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Short arms create smaller margins for error near his edges.
  • Must stay very tight to his block to maintain engagement.
  • Average lateral range to make play-side cut-off blocks.
  • Gets overextended when setting too heavy on his outside foot.
  • Chases the picker too deep against twist games.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Michigan): Redshirted.
  • 2021 (Michigan): Played in 8 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2022 (Michigan): Played in 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (2-15-7.5). 
  • 2023 (Michigan): Played in 7 games as a reserve and on special teams. 
  • 2024: Played in all 14 games with 8 starts (24-368-15.3, 4 TDs.
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (31-436-14.1, 4 TDs). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior who broke out at SMU in his final two seasons after four quiet years with limited snaps and production. Hibner’s ankle tightness limits his change-of-direction quickness and ability to uncover underneath. He builds speed when working the seams and as an open-field runner. He has adequate hands and ball skills to make catches when contested. Hibner has the demeanor and tenacity for pro-blocking duties. However, he’s undersized and needs to work on his hand placement to improve his consistency of results. Hibner is a Day 3 talent with roster potential as a move tight end or true H-back.
profiles.strengths:
• Threatens vertically with build-up speed as seam-runner.
  • Maximizes catch radius with good extension and catch timing.
  • Adequate contested-catch talent with good feel for boundaries.
  • Top speed makes him hard to catch in the open field.
  • Determined and gritty as a point-of-attack blocker.
  • Good patience and radar to land blocks on second level.
  • Core special-teams talent is part of his profile.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Has trouble slipping around route redirection.
  • Tip-toe strides limit ability to quickly get in and out of breaks.
  • Below-average burst and separation from change of direction.
  • Struggles to elude the first tackler after catches underneath.
  • Inconsistent hand placement leads to uneven block sustain.
  • Needs to cut back on the leaning and lunging into block fits.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted as a walk-on. Played in 1 game as a reserve TE.
  • 2022: Played in all 14 games with 1 start at TE (5-78-15.6 receiving).
  • 2023: Team's Most Improved Player on Offense. Played in all 15 games with 3 starts for the national champions as TE/H-back (2-19-9.5 receiving).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts at FB (3-24-8.0 receiving). Team captain.
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Played in 11 games with 8 starts at FB (2-11-5.5 receiving). Team captain. Missed the last two games of the season with a foot injury.
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Ben, started for 4 years on the OL at Michigan and has 53 career starts in the NFL. Max and Ben are the only brothers in Michigan history to be 2-time team captains. Brother, Jack, pitched for Michigan's NCAA runner-up squad in 2019 and works in the New York Mets front office.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Like his brother Ben before him, Max is a two-time team captain at Michigan. While Max is smaller than Ben -- an offensive lineman for the Buccaneers -- Max is equally committed as a run blocker. He fits blocks with good centering and strikes with initial pop. He has a hard time sustaining and clearing lanes on a consistent basis, though. He can handle basic zone-beater and play-action catches. He’s also above average in pass protection from the backfield. In a league with limited fullback opportunities, Bredeson will have his work cut out for him as he pursues a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Two-time team captain.
  • Viable safeguard with his pass pro in the backfield.
  • Stalks and centers run block, exploding hands into contact. 
  • Good balance as a run blocker with a wide base and active feet.
  • Attempts to make finishing his block a top priority.
  • Typical fullback toughness after the catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lack of length can turn him into a one-pop blocker.
  • Hands land high, diminishing ability to sustain blocks.
  • Average adjustments to moving targets on second level.
  • Not a “clean-up man” as a lead blocker in the hole.
  • Average hands and relative non-factor as a pass-catcher at Michigan.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (East Los Angeles College): Played in 1 game.
  • 2022 (East Los Angeles College): Top 10 overall JC recruit. Played LT/RT.
  • 2023: Played in 6 games with 5 starts (4 at RT, 1 at LT).
  • 2024: Started all 14 games at RT.
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Started 12 games at RT.
  • Miscellaneous: Born in Nigeria, moved to Compton when he was 13 years old. Did not play football growing up. Played soccer in Nigeria.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: An ascending, traits-heavy tackle prospect, Iheanachor is a former high school hooper and late-comer to football. He has good length and excellent lean mass. His hands and footwork need refinement, but his range and play strength should translate to any run scheme. There is work to do with pass-protection technique, but strong performances against Texas Tech’s rush duo last season and at the Senior Bowl suggest Iheanachor might be more game-ready than I previously anticipated. In a year light on high-end tackles, Iheanachor’s measurables, athleticism and upside could push him up the board.
profiles.strengths:
• Impressive blend of size and athletic ability.
  • Lateral quickness and body control made for an outside-zone scheme.
  • Adequate timing and technique on combo blocks.
  • Basketball feet to mirror rushers and off-ball linebackers.
  • Displayed his potential against dynamic rush duo from Texas Tech.
  • Twitchy pass slides with adequate range to meet speed.
  • Rush anchor will set in once footwork improves.
  • Dominant at times during Senior Bowl practices.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hitch in his punch causes hands to ride outside the frame.
  • Struggles with protection recognition against gaming fronts.
  • Wide hands open him up for holding penalties.
  • Needs better pad level to improve leverage as a drive blocker.
  • Shoves second-level blocks instead of sticking and sustaining.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Purdue): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2023 (Purdue): Played in 5 games with 4 starts (22-196-8.9). Missed the rest of the season due to injury.
  • 2024 (Purdue): Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 51 receptions, 685 receiving yards (13.4 per), 4 receiving TDs. Started all 12 games.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big Ten. Played in all 14 games with 12 starts (43-448-10.4, 2 TDs).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Luke, plays TE at Purdue.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Highly athletic, pass-catching tight end capable of earning volume targets on the pro level. Klare can live beyond the typical targeted depth for most tight ends thanks to his route inventory and ability to generate separation across the field. He’s best from the slot but can widen out when a matchup presents itself. Hands and ball-tracking are below average but his production could make teams forget the drops. He improved as a run blocker as the season progressed, but “functional” might be the finish line there. In a league craving impact tight ends, Klare has a chance to inject life into an offense hunting mismatches.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He doesn’t have Dalton Kincaid’s catch skills, but he could have that kind of production with how athletic he is.” - AFC executive
profiles.strengths:
• Loose-limbed and athletic with a full route tree available to him.
  • Speed to climb past unsuspecting safeties on vertical shots.
  • Able to adjust routes at a high rate of speed.
  • Separation burst across the field creates chunk-play chances.
  • Aligns wide to mismatch defensive backs on back-shoulder throws.
  • Rarely leaves yards on the field with his run-after-catch.
  • Athletic and fluid working from block to block in space.
  • Improved his body control and fit accuracy on lead pulls.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Not strong enough for adequate block sustain at the point.
  • Hand placement as a run blocker needs significant work.
  • Not a natural pass plucker and fights certain throws.
  • Needs to identify throws and move faster in making adjustments.
  • Needs to prioritize ball security on his run-after-catch.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 4 games as a reserve (3 tackles, 0.5 TFL).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games as a reserve (13 tackles, 2.5 sacks, PBU).
  • 2024: Played in 13 games as a reserve (22 tackles, 8 TFLs with 5.5 sacks, 3 PBUs, safety, FF).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games (26 tackles, 9.5 TFLs with 6.5 sacks, 6 PBUs, 2 FFs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Llewellyn is a tall, well-built base end, but it appears he lacks the play strength and anchor to carry his production into the league. He plays with a lack of knee-bend that limits balance on contact and anchor through engagement. He’s better at playing into gaps and playing off of blocks when his feet are active. He lacks explosiveness as a pass rusher but has access to a variety of rush plans and moves that can create opportunities inside the pocket. Llewellyn projects as an even-front end, but average backup could be his ceiling.
profiles.strengths:
• Plays into gaps with decisive forward charge.
  • A regular in the backfield, with 32% of his career tackles resulting in a loss.
  • Uses active hands to work off of move blocks.
  • Well-timed long-arm strike creates space for his rush.
  • Two-hand swipe is quick and strong.
  • Sets up his helicopter-like inside spin.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Run out of his gap by forceful drive-blockers.
  • Doesn’t transfer much power from hips to hands.
  • Average change-of-direction quickness in space.
  • Below-average ground gain in his first three rush steps.
  • Speed-to-power conversion is underwhelming.
  • Not a natural bender, causing inconsistent contact balance.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve for the national champions. Enrolled in January.
  • 2022: Played in 7 games as a reserve for the national champions.
  • 2023: Played in 13 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 5 starts at RG.
  • 2025: Started all 14 games at LG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Morris has a rare blend of intelligence, power and movement talent, but the profile is a little too uneven. He plays with a sky-high pad level and outside hands. He’s very strong in his upper body and is relatively light on his feet as a move blocker. His broad frame can be tough to get around in protection, but his inconsistent base width could lead to leakage against athletic rushers. Playing at a lighter weight would make him quicker/more efficient and could be the key to making it in the league.
profiles.strengths:
• Freaky weight-room strength shows up on the field.
  • Athletic for his size with ability to adjust in space.
  • Uses size and nimble feet to climb and cover linebackers.
  • Stones the rush when landing hands directly into frame.
  • Uses grip strength to cinch up rushers who crowd him.
  • Keeps his pads over his shoes when passing off twists.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Pops upright after snap and stays that way throughout the play.
  • Use of outside hands limit ability to control and sustain.
  • Inconsistent generating explosive contact at the point.
  • Base narrows when mirroring the rush.
  • Deadens feet on contact, allowing some leakage into gaps.

profiles.overview: Enormous collegiate right tackle who might need to prove he can bump inside to make an NFL roster. Pettus is tall and very broad but lacks the natural sit-down anchor associated with many players his size. He lacks fluidity as a pulling blocker and when fitting up run blocks off the snap. He might not have enough slide quickness to handle NFL edge speed. Even with a move to guard, Pettus will need to improve his body control and footwork to effectively utilize his size.
profiles.strengths:
• Was a 40-game starter over four collegiate seasons.
  • Big, broad frame with a 7-foot-1 wingspan.
  • Able to latch into rushers with big, strong hands.
  • Has the mass and power to create early movement.
  • Adequate job of neutralizing base blocks in run game.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks fluidity from snap movements into block fits.
  • Below-average body control to sustain his run blocks.
  • Heavy feet in his diagonal and vertical pass slides.
  • Struggles with redirecting against inside moves.
  • Needs to play with firmer hands in pass protection.

profiles.overview: Despite his lack of size, Coats has proven to be an extremely combative cornerback who fights hard for every inch of the workspace. He turns 25 this summer, which could hurt his draft chances, but the tape is solid. He possesses good speed and quick feet. He plays with sound awareness/instincts in both man and zone. Coats’ lack of length appeared to create anxiety on some deep throws, which led to pass interference penalties, but that issue could be mitigated with a move inside to nickel. Coats might not be drafted, but his competitive nature deserves a look by a pro team.
profiles.strengths:
• Loose hips and good short-area foot quickness.
  • Runs well and displays easy change of direction.
  • Good feel for route combinations in zone.
  • Combative and competitive at the catch point.
  • Consistently locates the football down the field.
  • Stays balanced and tackle-ready in run support.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Gets overpowered by big receivers in press coverage.
  • Grabs and makes unnecessary contact downfield.
  • Very average at finding angles for pass breakups.
  • Can be dragged a little as a tackler in the run game.
  • Will be a 25-year-old rookie.

profiles.overview: Productive edge defender and 42-game starter over five seasons at Central Michigan. NFL teams will take notice of Heldman’s 2025 spike in TFLs/sacks and his size/testing profile. He’s well-built and can hold his own against single blocks at the point of attack. However, he’s inconsistent with early play recognition and initial footwork to beat the block. He’s strong on the edges of his rush but lacks ideal fluidity/bend in his lower half and has a fairly predictable rush menu. Heldman could earn an opportunity to compete in a camp thanks to his size, testing and 2025 production.
profiles.strengths:
• Good combination of size, athletic testing and production.
  • First with his hands and keeps pad level low through engagement.
  • Displays adequate play strength to shed and tackle.
  • Plays through redirection at the top of the arc when cornering.
  • Hands stay active throughout the rush rep.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs better first-step recognition against lateral blocks.
  • Didn’t face NFL-caliber tests against his 2025 competition.
  • Doesn’t always play with the quickness he shows in testing.
  • Squared-off upfield rush is easy to find for a tackle's punch.
  • Below-average counter quickness and rush instincts.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted as a walk-on. Passed on a scholarship from Rice.
  • 2022: Played in 13 games with 1 start (26 tackles, 0.5 TFLs, PBU). Awarded a scholarship before the Alamo Bowl.
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Tied for the team lead with 3 INTs. Played in all 14 games with 9 starts (48 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, 2 PBUs, blocked kick). 
  • 2024: Started all 16 games (78 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, 2 INTs, 10 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-SEC. Started 10 games (70 tackles, sack, 2 INTs, PBU). Missed 2 games with a broken thumb. Won the Wuerffel Trophy (community service). Named to the AFCA Allstate Good Works Team for his community service efforts. Finalist for the Burlsworth Trophy (nation's top player who began his career as a walk-on).
  • Miscellaneous: Grandfather, Eddie Johnson, was an All-American swimmer for Texas.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior who has played in 53 games with 36 starts. Taaffe has a good feel for play design and is assignment-oriented. He’s quick to read and trigger downhill to contest short routes from split safety and robber looks. However, he lacks range to play over the top and speed to carry vertical threats downfield. His run-support angles improved in 2025, but he’s undersized and still falls short as an open-field tackler. Taaffe’s football IQ and special-teams value might need to do the heavy lifting to overcome average traits and athleticism.
profiles.strengths:
• Gets back end of the defense lined up and is a strong communicator.
  • Shows good awareness to play design and his assignments. 
  • Responsive to what his eyes are telling him.
  • Descends on crossing routes with timing to strike or quickly tackle.
  • Posted seven interceptions over the last three seasons.
  • Above-average ball skills when he’s in position.
  • Productive special-teams player throughout his career.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs more weight on his frame for demands of the position.
  • Can be baited shallow and beaten high on levels concepts.
  • Displays below-average man-cover talent.
  • Lacks top-end speed to drive and range off the hash.
  • Below-average reactive agility as an open-field tackler. 
  • Made troubling mistakes as a run defender late in the season.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (USC): Played in 6 games with 4 starts (7-109-15.6, TD).
  • 2022 (Mississippi): Played in 7 games with 6 starts (17-156-9.2, 3 TDs). Missed time with a broken collarbone.
  • 2023 (Mississippi): Played in 3 games as a reserve (4-65-16.3, TD). Suspended for the first half in the opener for undisclosed reasons. Left the team in September. Entered the transfer portal after the regular season. 
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Played in 11 games with 5 starts (30-395-13.2, 3 TDs). Suspended for 1 game. Did not play in the team's Texas Bowl loss to LSU.
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big 12. Finalist for the John Mackey Award (nation's top TE). Started 11 games (50-694-13.9, 6 TDs).  

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Long, rangy tight end offering rare arm length, good speed and some alignment versatility. Trigg moves like a big wideout with surprising hip sink, foot quickness and fluid transitions to run after the catch. He wins vertically against linebackers and overwhelms defensive backs with size, high-point talent and massive hands that fuel highlight-reel catches. He’s still developing as a route-runner and struggles to finish catches through heavy contact. His frame and pad level limit in-line blocking, but he can wall off or stalk block from the slot. Trigg’s field-stretching potential and air space dominance in the red zone should lead to production as a pro.
profiles.strengths:
• Rare arm length, hand size and wingspan for a tight end.
  • Will run past linebackers and beat them up the seam.
  • Has the sink and footwork of a big wideout getting out of breaks.
  • Impressive timing, body control and extension to big-boy defenders at the high-point.
  • Makes highlight-reel grabs look easy at times.
  • Has become a living nightmare for man defenders in the red zone.
  • Ricochets off contact to keep run-after-catch going.
  • Able to wall off and stay connected as a blocker in the slot.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Gets jostled off course by route redirection.
  • Lacks salesmanship to move defenders with leverage and head fakes.
  • Can get lazy at the top of his route, allowing easier close outs.
  • Allows defenders to blitz his work space and jar catches loose.
  • Doesn’t fit his lead blocks with good pad level or purpose.
  • Wild hands fly outside the frame when fitting up move blocks.

profiles.overview: A versatile slot receiver, Wortham can run, catch, throw, and return kicks, though he lacks elite size and explosiveness. He has good hands but needs to improve in altering route tempo and hiding break points from the coverage. Wortham, who played quarterback in high school, is capable of being used in Wildcat looks, zone-read concepts and quick-game throws or gadget passes. He can return kicks but is an average threat in that department. His versatility stands out, but convincing a team he’s a plus in any one area will be the key to making a legitimate push for a spot in camp.
profiles.strengths:
• Good athlete with versatility to throw, catch, run and return kicks.
  • Instinctive and natural navigating traffic as a route-runner.
  • Good change of direction and balance with the ball in his hands.
  • Hands are natural and typically reliable when throws are on target.
  • Gadget-play ability opens a new slate of misdirection for creative play-callers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average re-acceleration to elude tacklers after making a cut.
  • Needs to do a better job of disguising impending route breaks.
  • Short wingspan requires optimal accuracy/timing from his quarterback.
  • Lacks north/south juice as a kick returner.

profiles.overview: From a traits standpoint, Kamara might not be as exciting as other late-round hopefuls, but his tape is likely more physical and consistent. He’s very rugged and gets right to his action on each snap. He’s not sudden but consistently works around blockers using harmonious hands and feet. He lacks length and is below average taking on blocks at the point. He has some closing burst in his rush, but the get-off and counter work is average. Kamara has physical limitations, but he knows how to play ball and has toughness that will appeal to NFL teams.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 17.5 sacks and 33.5 tackles for loss from 2023 to 2024.
  • Footwork off the snap is highly efficient and effective.
  • Subtle hands and upper-body turn help him slip around blocks. 
  • Delivers violent, stinging chops to tackle’s outside hand as a rusher.
  • Developed a workable spin counter.
  • Steady through his base to play through contact.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks NFL size and length along the edge.
  • Build-up rusher who lacks explosiveness in tight spaces.
  • Below-average burst to threaten the edge.
  • Needs to improve hands for better block take-ons.
  • Average bend limits his anchor and change-of-direction quickness.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Buffalo): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (23-132-5.7, TD).
  • 2022 (Buffalo): Led team with 625 rushing yards (150 carries, 4.2 per), 7 rushing TDs. Played in 13 games with 2 starts (23-135-5.9, TD receiving).
  • 2023 (Buffalo): Played in 11 games with 4 starts (90-362-4.0, 2 TDs rushing; 13-35-2.7 receiving). 
  • 2024 (New Mexico State): Led team with 8 rushing TDs (157-725-4.6). Played in 12 games with 4 starts (9-74-8.2, TD receiving; 4-87-21.8 KR).
  • 2025: Second-team All-SEC. Ranked ninth in the FBS with 6.4 yards per carry. Led team with 1,070 rushing yards (167 carries, 6.4 per). Tied for the team lead with 8 rushing TDs. Started all 12 games (28-226-8.1, TD receiving).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Washington made stops at three different colleges and showed improvement with each move to a new school. He’s fast with loose hips and adequate agility. He’s not very sudden in tight quarters and is a step slow to see it and go when the hole opens. He can glide and swerve around interior traffic once he’s on the move, though. He has breakaway speed in the open field and is capable as an inside/outside runner. Running to his size with a greater degree of aggressiveness will be the key as he makes the jump. Washington has the traits and talent to become a solid rotational back.
profiles.strengths:
• Blends imposing size with impressive straight-line speed.
  • Agile feet and loose hips allow for smooth change of direction.
  • Has burst to keep the run wide and beat flowing pursuit to the corner.
  • Reads blocks and moves fluidly through lane development inside.
  • Size allows him to run through cornerbacks in run support. 
  • Able to drive through tacklers and fall forward for additional yardage.
  • Can do damage with big plays on swing passes.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs to gather steps getting into downhill cuts in outside-zone schemes.
  • Can be a step slow to see the opening and trigger downhill.
  • Needs to become more willful and aggressive between the tackles.
  • Lacks sudden acceleration for ideal escapability in small spaces.
  • Fumbles have been an issue over the last two seasons.
  • Has size for pass protection but is missing consistent grit.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Hutchinson Community College): 2-16, TD in 3 games.
  • 2022 (Alabama): Played in 6 games as a reserve (2-18-9.0).
  • 2023 (Alabama): Played in 13 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (22-301-13.7, 4 TDs).
  • 2025: Started 11 games (26-253-9.7, 2 TDs). Missed last two regular season games with a lower-body injury. Suffered pectoral injury in spring practice, requiring surgery.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Kitselman has good size and will play as a connected tight end on the next level. He needs to play with better hand placement and pad level, but he’s willing to put in work in-line or as a move blocker. He has above-average play speed in space and showed an ability to run a variety of routes. He has enough speed to stress man coverage into the second level. His separation underneath is average, though. Drops, double-catches and issues securing contested throws were evident in 2025. Kitselman has Day 3 draft value and could find work as a TE3/4.
profiles.strengths:
• Doesn’t shy away from run-blocking duties.
  • Keeps feet chopping through contact for longer connection.
  • Adjusts his track to land with some pop as a move blocker.
  • Runs a more expansive route tree than most tight ends.
  • Snaps off breaks with crisp cuts at the top of the route.
  • Enough speed to stress linebackers on seams and overs.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inconsistent centering block fits near the line.
  • Stays busy as base blocker, but the strain is average.
  • Needs to keep his hands inside opponent’s frame.
  • Acceleration out of breaks is below average.
  • Drops and double-catches showed up in 2025.
  • Needs more toughness boxing out on contested targets.

profiles.overview: A four-star recruit who spent his first five seasons at Ohio State, Melton finally came into his own during his lone year at Virginia in 2025. He has the measurables of an NFL edge rusher with good size and length. He needs more reps at the position, though. His explosiveness is average, but he plays with good awareness and works his way into the action. Melton is an average bender who does an adequate job of setting up his rush with foot fakes. He lacks high-upside traits as a rusher but should continue improving with better hand usage.
profiles.strengths:
• Possesses NFL-caliber size and length.
  • Adequate get-off and timing to attack the turn.
  • Gives inside and outside fakes to help set up his rush.
  • Effective inside move fueled by pad level and efficient footwork.
  • Uses length to separate from and discard blockers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average weaponization of hands with his pass rush.
  • Average bend makes him easier to redirect up the arc.
  • Needs more strength to improve edge-setting and block take-ons.
  • Lack of explosiveness in pro-day testing was a bit concerning.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Played in 8 games as a reserve.
  • 2024: Played in all 14 games with 5 starts at LT.
  • 2025: Second-team All-SEC. Played in all 14 games with 13 starts at LT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Freeling offers coveted length and athleticism at right tackle. With only one season as a full-time starter, filling out his frame and improving his technique should be early priorities. His quickness brings first-phase positioning advantages, but he needs more play strength to carry that over to block sustain and finish. Lunging and deadening feet post-punch must be coached out of his muscle memory in pass protection so his athleticism and length can do their jobs. Independent hand usage and a reliable “snatch and trap” could instantly bolster his success rate. There is some buyer beware on tape, but if smoothed out, he has the ceiling of a quality NFL starter.
profiles.strengths:
• Long-limbed with a frame that can add mass.
  • Possesses plus athletic ability for the position.
  • Has the initial quickness to make all the move blocks asked of him.
  • Continues pressing forward to stay connected longer to blocks.
  • Protection improved noticeably as the season progressed.
  • Good fluidity when switching off and mirroring twisters.
  • Redirects feet quickly to meet inside moves at the B-gap.
  • Runs like a tight end as a lead blocker and to spring slip screens.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inconsistent feel and execution for run-blocking landmarks.
  • Unable to prevent ends from working across him against his will.
  • Inconsistent hand placement/resets cause him to slide off blocks.
  • Leans and lunges at the corner instead of continuing to slide feet.
  • Stiff outside leg limits quickness to hit set points.
  • Protection is missing independent hands and a more diverse approach.

profiles.overview: Bamba is a perimeter cornerback with impressive size, elite top-end speed and good short-area burst. Despite his advantageous measurables and explosiveness, he comes up short with on-ball production due to his lack of coverage feel and instincts. Bamba has struggled to stay connected to receivers and needs more technique work. Teams might want to develop him as a press-man corner, but he appears to be better suited for work as a zone corner who can press, redirect and play the run. Bamba is a project, but he could find a practice squad.
profiles.strengths:
• Rare blend of size and speed.
  • Play strength to disrupt releases and route timing through force.
  • Works cleanly through early route combinations in short zone.
  • Speed allows him to recover from missteps.
  • Range and length to bring down runners/receivers quickly in space.
  • Has ability to become a more impactful/productive run defender.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Made just eight starts in four seasons at BYU.
  • Below-average technique and discipline in press-man.
  • Struggles with indecisiveness in his read/reaction from off-man.
  • Below-average fluidity in change of direction when shadowing routes.
  • Needs his feet under him to prevent imbalance when planting and driving.
  • No interceptions in 36 career games at BYU.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Independence Community College): 12 tackles, 2 sacks in 7 games.
  • 2021 (Hutchinson Community College): 50 tackles, 19.5 TFLs, 12 sacks in 11 games.
  • 2022 (Houston): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (0.5 TFL).
  • 2023 (Houston): Played in 9 games as a reserve (7 tackles, TFL).
  • 2024 (Houston): Played in 1 game as a reserve (2 tackles).
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. MAC Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-MAC. Led the FBS with 21 TFLs, tied for the lead with 14.5 sacks, tied for sixth with 4 FFs. Started 13 games (55 tackles, PBU). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tucker’s rush ability far exceeds his run defense. He’s an instinctive, skilled rusher with an uncommon feel for a player with so few reps. He uses quickness and bend to buzz the edge, while marrying hands and feet for quick wins. He dominated weaker competition but more polish will be needed for his jump to lining up across from bigger, longer tackles. He gets swallowed and controlled at the point of attack, and that will persist without substantial improvement. Despite limited career production, the rush tape is impressive enough for Day 3 consideration and an opportunity as a designated rusher.
profiles.strengths:
• Quick get-off and presses forward with his rush.
  • Accurate, well-timed hand swipes eliminate blocker’s punch.
  • Able to bend and flatten at the corner or slip inside the tackle.
  • Impressive efficiency and harmony between hands and feet.
  • Has speed for play-side and back-side pursuits.
  • Athletic with short-area footwork to finish tackles.
  • Flashed cover talent in his limited reps in space.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Only one season as a full-time player at the FBS level.
  • Will need to implement an inside counter at the apex of his rush.
  • Can be smothered by length against jump-sets.
  • Plays under the block and loses contain positioning.
  • Poor hand placement and block take-on technique.
  • Struggles to punch, extend and post up as an edge-setter.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Iowa Western Community College): 11 tackles, INT, 2 PBUs, blocked kick.
  • 2021 (Iowa Western Community College): 20 tackles, TFL, 2 PBUs.
  • 2022: Played in all 15 games with 2 starts at safety (49 tackles, 2 PBUs).
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Led team with 84 tackles, 4 sacks. Started all 12 games (6 TFLs, 2 PBUs, blocked kick).
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (81 tackles, 6.5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, INT, PBU, FF).
  • 2025: Started all 13 games (88 tackles, 4 TFLs with 2 sacks, 2 INTs, PBU, FF).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Chiddi, played DE at Kansas State. Twin sister, Nneka, played basketball at Grand Canyon University and UNLV.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Obiazor is an assignment-sound inside linebacker with good tape and average short-area athletic ability. His box-score output has stayed nearly identical for three straight years, mirroring his week-to-week reliability. He has a high football IQ with decisive, accurate diagnosis and leverages his run fits by slipping blocks or holding firm with his anchor. A lack of ideal short-area quickness and pursuit burst might require Obiazor to take more chances as a pro. He’s a former safety who sees the field clearly but is average in coverage. He profiles as a dependable backup and core special-teamer.
profiles.strengths:
• Split low with impressive balance through contact.
  • Football smart and quick to diagnose blocking schemes/play design.
  • Highly efficient block-beater in tight quarters.
  • Will punch and work around or under blocks.
  • Sheds blocks with good timing to make the tackle.
  • Meticulous tackler with accurate aim and proficient wrap-up.
  • Former safety with good eyes and awareness in zone.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Loses ground when pursuit spills wide.
  • Feet are a little heavy when moving laterally.
  • Below-average reactive agility to mirror runner’s cuts.
  • Might need to play more proactively than reactively as a pro.
  • Below-average change of direction and range from zone.
  • Average man-coverage talent against NFL targets.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Nebraska): Did not play.
  • 2021 (Nebraska): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (2-14-7.0).
  • 2022 (Nebraska): Played in all 12 games with 4 starts (6-52-8.7, TD).
  • 2023 (Nebraska): Played in all 12 games with 7 starts (5-51-10.2 receiving; 1-11-11.0 rushing).
  • 2024 (Nebraska): Played in all 12 games with 6 starts (6-102-17.0). 
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts (19-198-10.4, 3 TDs; 3-5-1.7, TD rushing).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Ian, played OL at Nebraska.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Skip the stat page for Boerkircher because what he offers won’t be found there. He has average size and strength but compensates with willingness as a blocker and a taste for contact that isn’t always easy to find. He can line up in-line, land on targets in space and finish his blocks. Despite pedestrian production over five seasons, his tape shows an ability to challenge man coverage, secure contested catches with sticky hands and accelerate through contact as a runner. He’s flown under the radar but projects as an alignment-versatile combo tight end with the talent to start in the NFL.
profiles.strengths:
• Flashes quickness to uncover against man underneath.
  • Sure-handed with the ability to make sudden adjustments on the throw.
  • Survives and thrives when faced with punishing catches.
  • Dips and drives into first contact from his hips.
  • Delivers first strike with inside hands into the defender’s frame.
  • Releases and scoops linebackers as a play-side zone blocker.
  • Finishes blocks and runs after the catch with the same energy.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Light production levels as a pass catcher.
  • Can do a better job of working back on the throw.
  • Inconsistent footwork on his double-teams with tackles.
  • Needs to come to balance more quickly as a blocker in space.
  • Room for improvement with his block sustain on second level.

profiles.overview: Voorhis is a little undersized and not very long, but he posted impact production in the FBS for the first time in 2025. He’s fairly instinctive as a rusher and made noticeable additions to his rush menu last season. While he collected tackles for loss in 2025, he’s below average at beating run blocks and securing his gaps. He lacks traits, explosive testing and sustained production but his consistency as a rusher is worth keeping an eye on.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 17 tackles for loss, including 12 sacks, in his impressive 2025 season.
  • Sets up a softer edge with an inside/out rush approach.
  • Operates with violent chops and swipes at the top of the rush.
  • Good ankle flexion allows him to squeeze the rush arc.
  • Low-cut and difficult to knock off-balance.
  • Back-side closing burst helps to halt runs before they start.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average size and length.
  • Lacks pro-level juice to beat most NFL tackles to the corner.
  • Square rusher lacking elusiveness and upper-body turn.
  • Gets engulfed and wired to blocking tight ends in run game.
  • Lacks length to help save contain positioning on wide runs.

profiles.bio:
• High school: 5-star recruit, top 30 overall prospect nationally. 2021 Gatorade National Player of the Year, Maxwell Football Club's National Offensive Player of the Year as a senior (2,059 yards, 44 rushing TDs). 
  • 2022: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference RB, Honorable Mention RS. Led the team with 1,061 rushing yards (156 carries), freshman school-record 12 rushing TDs. Ranked seventh in the FBS with 6.8 yards per rush. Played in all 13 games with 8 starts (11-85-7.7, TD receiving; 14-349-24.9, TD KR).
  • 2023: Third-team All-Big Ten RB, Honorable Mention RS. Led team with 8 rushing TDs (171-752-4.4). Played in all 13 games with 7 starts (26-308-11.9, 2 TDs receiving; 13-313-24.1 KR).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Ranked seventh in the FBS with 1,805 all-purpose yards. He and Kaytron Allen became the first Penn State RB duo to each rush for 1,000 yards in a single season. Played in 15 games with 12 starts (172-1,099-6.4, 12 TDs rushing; 41-375-9.1, 5 TDs receiving; 14-331-23.6 KR).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten RS. Set school records with 5,586 career all-purpose yards, 55 total career TDs. Played in 12 games with 4 starts (123-549-4.5, 13 TDs rushing; 24-219-9.1, TD receiving; 7-145-20.7 KR).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Well-built back with explosive speed whose 2025 season was flat after a strong 2024. Singleton is a linear runner who plays like his brake lines have been cut, affecting his ability to gather and elude tacklers or cut on demand. He has the speed to make defenses pay but displayed a lack of vision and instincts to put himself in position to do so, relative to his teammate Kaytron Allen. His size and speed will get attention, but his ability to return kicks and play on third downs could ultimately earn him a roster spot as a RB3.
profiles.strengths:
• Enticing blend of size, speed and overall explosiveness.
  • Easy acceleration to gain advantages on outside runs.
  • Tremendous power in his hips to drag tacklers with him.
  • Dangerous pass-catching option on angle and wheel routes.
  • Understands protection duties against the blitz.
  • Good mirror and hand usage to keep rusher in front of him.
  • Full-time kick returner over his first three seasons.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average vision and feel for lane development.
  • Relies on very clear points of entry to make his mark.
  • Struggles to gather his weight and cut quickly on wide runs.
  • Despite speed, had few explosive carries in 2025.
  • Lacks elusiveness and runs to contact far too often.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Played in 9 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams (14 tackles, INT, PBU).
  • 2023: Played in all 12 games as a reserve (11 tackles, PBU).
  • 2024: Redshirted to maintain eligibility. Played in 5 games (including the bowl game, which does not count toward redshirt eligibility) as a reserve and on special teams (5 tackles).
  • 2025: Started all 12 games (42 tackles, 6 TFLs with 2 sacks, PBU). Team captain. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Barrett isn’t overly explosive and athletic, but it’s hard to ignore his “slow power” and the way he helped clog the drain as a run-stuffer in 2025. He’s well-built with room to add even more mass. Barrett lacks first-step quickness and sudden hands, so he’s best-suited as a block-eater and two-gapper. The production won’t pop and he won’t add much as a rusher, but Barrett can add depth as a rotational nose tackle for teams looking for more congestion in the middle.
profiles.strengths:
• Broad through his chest and waist with a burly lower half.
  • Built for creating barriers to run lanes inside.
  • Presses blocker into an extended, ineffective position as two-gapper.
  • Has the take-on pop to dissuade the double team.
  • Drives through sealed blocks, caving them into the gap.
  • Makes it difficult for blockers to sustain and finish against him.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average hand quickness getting into first strike.
  • Eats blocks but lacks agility to make plays beyond his gap.
  • Below-average change-of-direction quickness.
  • Upright and straight-legged as a pass rusher.
  • Lacks short-area athleticism to make tackles in his gaps with consistency.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Western Kentucky): Played in all 12 games as a reserve (16-39-2.4 rushing; 3-5-1.7 receiving; 5-84-16.8 KR).
  • 2021 (Western Kentucky): Led team with 617 rushing yards (101 carries, 6.1 per, 2 TDs). Played in 12 games with 1 start (12-58-4.8 receiving).
  • 2022: Played in all 13 games with 1 start (139-779-5.6, 5 TDs rushing; 22-169-7.7, TD receiving).
  • 2023: Redshirted. Played in the first 4 games as a reserve (20-146-7.3, 2 TDs rushing; 10-78-7.8 receiving). Missed the rest of the season with a torn ACL.
  • 2024: Played in all 14 games as a reserve (118-540-4.6, 6 TDs rushing; 24-136-5.7, 2 TDs receiving; 8-232-29.0 KR). 
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 829 rushing yards (129 carries, 6.4 per, 6 TDs). Started 12 games (19-98-5.2, TD receiving; 6-126-21.0 KR).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Sixth-year senior with three seasons of steady play and production for the Ducks. Whittington is a downhill runner who plays behind his pads and takes care of the football along the interior. He lacks speed to widen the field and fluidity to create for himself when there is no clear point of entry. He’s tough and relatively decisive, with a knack for falling forward and adding yards through physicality. Whittington’s age and lack of true third-down value might work against him in his pursuit of a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Quick jump-cut with ability to escape sudden foot traffic.
  • Runs with good bend and leverage.
  • Plays behind his pads and accelerates through contact.
  • Rarely bounces it unnecessarily wide or off track.
  • Experienced as a kick returner over the last two years.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Plays at a single tempo with limited speed change.
  • Average acceleration for outside runs.
  • Cut transitions are segmented and labored.
  • Too many drops and double-catches out of backfield.
  • Will turn 25 years old before camp begins.

profiles.overview: Rucci is a tall, long right tackle prospect who made his mark at Penn State in the last two years after three uneventful seasons at Wisconsin. He has a proportional frame with room for more muscle mass, which will be important to add due to his lack of ideal play strength and anchor. His footwork and punch timing are too inconsistent at this time but could be correctable with more work. He’s an average athlete in pass protection but shows quality initial quickness to compete for his landmarks on wide-zone calls. Rucci’s size, bloodlines (father, Todd, spent eight seasons in the NFL) and upside could make him a late-round target.
profiles.strengths:
• Good arm length with big hands.
  • Plays with punch-ready hands and adequate scan for games.
  • Decent rush control when his punch locks in.
  • Plus quickness getting to back-side and play-side blocks.
  • Works from block to block with good timing and rhythm.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average reactive agility and overall footwork in run game.
  • Reaches and lunges at second-level targets on climbs.
  • Lacks ideal play strength to mitigate his taller pad level.
  • Can lose base width during pass slides and turns into a heel-clicker.
  • Needs to become more consistent with his punch approach and timing.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Miami): Played in all 12 games as a reserve (11 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 4 sacks).
  • 2023 (Miami): Played in 5 games with 3 starts (8 tackles, TFL, PBU). Missed the second half of the season due to injury.
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Led team with 5.5 sacks, 3 FFs. Tied for the team lead with 9.5 TFL. Played in 12 games with 11 starts (53 tackles, PBU). 
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big 12. Started all 12 games (46 tackles, 7.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, INT, 3 PBUs, 2 FFs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Two-year starter with NFL-caliber measurables. Kelly needs to get stronger and play with better grit to leverage his gap and win individual block battles in run support. Improved hand usage and refined counters might bolster his chances of creating pressure, but it’s hard to envision much sack production given his lack of quickness and explosive power. Kelly will have to battle for a roster spot as an even-front end.
profiles.strengths:
• Pro frame with very long arms.
  • Comes off the snap intent on keeping pads low. 
  • Times up long-arm move to separate in early stages of the rush.
  • Attacks tackle’s outside hand with long-arm chop to open the edge.
  • Reads pocket climb and works back under to harass quarterbacks.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Rushes and corners beyond pocket depth too often.
  • Below-average get-off with a pedestrian closing burst. 
  • Inside moves and counters lack suddenness.
  • Needs to better develop his core and upper-body strength.
  • Sloppy with his stack-and-shed technique.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in 13 games with 5 starts at LG.
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big Ten. Started all 16 games at LG.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten. Started 11 games at LG.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Prototypical guard for physical run schemes with thick limbs, a broad frame and plus core strength. Ioane plays with excellent contact balance and technique on both base blocks and double teams. He uses his hips and hands for leverage and displacement when drive blocking. However, he lacks athleticism and foot quickness to operate effectively as a move blocker. He pass sets with good posture and a firm punch and can anchor against power. Though quicker at a lighter weight in 2025, he will struggle with twitchy interior defenders who cross his face in the run game and attack his edges in protection. Despite scheme dependence, Ioane projects as an early starter with a high floor.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He worked hard to eliminate some extra weight and re-shape his body in the offseason and I think he played more consistently because of it. – AFC area scout
profiles.strengths:
• Prototypical guard build, with thick limbs and a broad frame.
  • Plays with impressive core power, body control and contact balance.
  • Creates leverage with upward hand strikes and rolls hips under his hands.
  • Uses grip strength and chopping feet to stay tight as a drive blocker.
  • Size and power create momentum to wash out angle blocks.
  • Punches with tight hands and good pop.
  • Snaps off twisters with good force.
  • Firm inside hand with ability to set quick anchors against power.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average lateral quickness and range as move blocker.
  • Loses track of stunting linemen crossing his face.
  • Lacks fluidity getting from block to block on combos.
  • Below-average adjustments to moving targets.
  • Gets beaten to the punch by twitchy interior rushers.
  • Lacks reactive quickness to make sudden recoveries.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (4-63-15.8 KR).
  • 2023: Played in 9 games with 2 starts (18-267-14.8, 2 TDs receiving). Missed time at the end of the year with a lower-leg injury.
  • 2024: Ranked fourth in the FBS with 21.2 yards per reception (28-594, 7 TDs). Played in all 12 games with 4 starts (2-23-11.5, TD rushing). 
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big Ten Conference. Tied for third in the FBS with 13 receiving TDs. Led the team with 69 receptions, 937 receiving yards (13.6 per). Played in all 16 games with 14 starts for the national champions (3-74-24.7, TD rushing).
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Omar, played basketball at Louisiana Tech and was WR coach at Lawrence North High School.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Big, strong target whose two-year rise is bolstered by translatable tape. While he was a full-time slot receiver in 2025, Cooper has played outside, as well. He can stem and drive past press with his strength. He has potent early acceleration to climb past nickelbacks into top position to challenge deep. His routes lack polish and he has average in-and-out quickness at break-points, but he’s rugged once the ball is in his hands. His ability to add yards after contact could earn Cooper more carries than we saw from him at Indiana. Fighting for catch space and blocking for the running game are areas where he needs improvement. Cooper is an ascending slot bully with Day 2 value.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 20 touchdown catches since the start of the 2024 season.
  • Welcomes physical play and wins through contact.
  • Versatile enough to be more than a slot option.
  • Creates lateral separation when beating press.
  • Digs hard through drive phase before snapping head around.
  • First and second acceleration catches defenders off-guard.
  • Explosive leaper who can pluck high throws at their apex.
  • Rugged runner who can break free from multiple tacklers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inefficient getting in and out of intermediate breaks.
  • Average contested-catch success for his physical profile.
  • Needs quicker recognition and adjustment on underthrows.
  • Acceleration out of the stem is average.
  • Disappointing effort and physicality when asked to run block.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 13 games as a reserve for the national champions (5-61-12.2, TD).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games with 10 starts (24-284-11.8, 3 TDs).
  • 2024: Played in all 14 games with 10 starts (21-248-11.8, 4 TDs).
  • 2025: Started all 14 games (20-261-13.1, TD).
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Chris, played lacrosse at Rutgers. Oscar thought he might play lacrosse in college, too, until becoming a major football recruit his junior year of high school. Brother, Harry, walked onto the Georgia football team as a TE for 2024.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Delp is a fluid athlete with the forward lean, short-area quickness and pure speed to beat linebackers on intermediate routes. His soft hands and smooth catch skills show up on the move, though his short arms and inconsistent finish through contact limit his reliability. He has enough toughness and technique to help in the run game as he improves his strength. Delp projects as a Day 3 prospect with three-down potential and untapped upside as a pass catcher.
profiles.strengths:
• Good forward lean and early acceleration into his routes.
  • Short-area quickness with the ability to uncover on outs, stop routes and crossers.
  • Pure speed to beat linebackers matched on him in man coverage.
  • Catches with soft hands and adequate extension to meet the throw.
  • Uses choppy settle steps and good hand strikes into base blocks.
  • Creates leverage with proper bend and lift technique.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Short arms lead to challenges rescuing off-frame throws.
  • Inconsistent finishing catches through heavy contact.
  • Average elusiveness to add yards after the catch.
  • Needs to get stronger in his upper body for blocking duties.
  • Caught leaning too far forward when getting into blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Washington): Offensive Scout Team MVP. Redshirted.
  • 2023 (Washington): Freshman All-American. Second-team All-Pac-12 Conference. Started all 15 games (first 2 at LG, final 13 at C). 
  • 2024: Started all 13 games at C.
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Started 14 games at C. Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Brailsford has shown notable grit and consistency. He can be out-leveraged and shoved around at the point of attack, but his mobility gives him a distinct advantage on the move. A lack of functional mass/length could lead to his pass protection being exposed by NFL power and rush talent. Brailsford’s tenacity and execution give him a chance, but he’s a one-position prospect with zone-scheme dependence. He might need to earn a starting job to stick around in the league.
profiles.strengths:
• Tenacity and toughness allow him to punch above his weight class.
  • Elite quickness to reach, scoop, cutoff, climb and pull with success.
  • Keeps defenders occupied with consistent foot drive through contact.
  • Always active and engaged with a commitment to blocking schemes.
  • Fits up blocks with a feel for angles to leverage the run lane.
  • Meets pass rushers with first hands on most reps.
  • Hand resets and lower-body flexion allow for quicker anchors.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Smallish frame falls below NFL standards.
  • Lacks mass to bring much pop into first contact.
  • Out-leveraged and pulled off his spot by big nose tackles.
  • Struggles playing with width to protect both A-gaps.
  • Bull rushers can build downhill momentum against him.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Notre Dame): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (Notre Dame): Played in 1 game as a reserve C.
  • 2023 (Notre Dame): Started all 13 games at LG.
  • 2024 (Notre Dame): Played in all 16 games with starts in the final 13 games at C.
  • 2025: Second-team All-Big Ten Conference. Named the Offensive MVP of the Rose Bowl, the first time the award has gone to an OL since 1944. Team was finalist for the Joe Moore Award (nation's top OL). Started all 16 games for the national champions. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Coogan is a veteran center with good size, intelligence, communication skills and leadership that will appeal to offensive line coaches. He’s technically sound and is consistent in centering opponents while latching in with grip strength to increase stickiness. He’s best in a gap scheme and inside zone, but his effectiveness can fade when the job stretches beyond the A-gaps. In protection, he lands well-timed punches and utilizes instinctive hand resets to regain positioning. However, forward lean and shorter arms will invite counters. Coogan has the potential to become a starter, but there are limitations in his game that make scheme fit and protection help important.
profiles.strengths:
• Dips hips and drives through down-block targets.
  • Keeps hands tight, providing added control at the point.
  • Stays square with eyes to the linebacker on work-up blocks.
  • Slides hips into place to secure on ace blocks.
  • Uses independent hands with good timing and pop.
  • Gets to resets quickly to help regain his positioning. 
  • Base width never changes when mirroring.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Could struggle finding landmarks in outside zone.
  • Below-average second-level adjustments.
  • Can be steered and shed by longer nose tackles.
  • Forward-leaning pass sets invite counters.
  • Below average cut-off quickness when recovering.
  • Anchor gives way against powerful bull rushers.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Florida State): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Florida State): ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year. Played in all 13 games as a reserve (31 tackles, 6 TFLs with 5 sacks, 3 PBUs, FF).
  • 2023 (Florida State): Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started all 14 games (44 tackles, 14.5 TFLs with 7 sacks, 10 PBUs, 2 FFs).
  • 2024 (Florida State): Started 12 games (35 tackles, 11 TFLs with 4 sacks, blocked kick).
  • 2025: Started all 13 games (34 tackles, 5 TFLs with 1 sack, 6 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with three years of starting experience between Florida State and LSU. Payton is a linear mover with long limbs and adequate foot quickness. He lacks decisiveness at the point of attack and will struggle to stand firm against NFL drive blockers. Payton has enough burst to create opportunities at the corners, provided he continues to refine his hand work. His inside rush transitions are fluid and will be even more effective if he brings his edge rush to greater life. Payton’s traits give him a chance to become a backup with average upside.
profiles.strengths:
• Long limbs with a frame capable of adding more muscle.
  • Discards base blocks with sharp punch-and-pull technique.
  • Length to leap and tackle from distance on back-side chase.
  • Adequate take-off in his race to the corner.
  • Utilizes chop-and-rip move to trim the edge.
  • Presses up on tackle before hitting smooth inside counters.
  • Effectively disguises an inside spin counter.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hip tightness turns him into a linear rusher.
  • Too many similar attacks down the middle of the tackle.
  • Unable to bend enough to avoid redirection past the arc.
  • Doesn’t generate enough leverage in his speed-to-power.
  • Below-average play recognition and in-line anchor.
  • Takes shoddy angles into contact as a tackler.

profiles.bio:
• High school: Top 10 overall prospect nationally. First-team All-American, Alabama Player of the Year as a senior (90 tackles, 23 TFLs, 8 sacks). 92 tackles, 26 TFLs, 11 sacks as a junior. Team won 4 straight state titles.
  • 2023: Freshman All-American. Played in 12 games with 2 starts (26 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, FF). 
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Played in 11 games with 10 starts (7 at DE, 3 at DT; 28 tackles, 8.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, FF). Played 5 snaps as a FB in jumbo package.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-ACC. Started 12 games (30 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 2 sacks).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Woods is a young interior defender with room to add play strength as he fills out his frame. He’s not a pure one- or two-gap fit, but he’s capable in both schemes. He plays with good lower-body explosiveness into initial contact, keeping his hands and feet synced to work around blocks when needed. He’s more of an active brawler than double-team eating tree stump. Shorter arms allow blockers to crowd his frame and force him to fight harder at the point. Yet, his ability to overtake and win as the rep progresses is impressive. He lacks quick-win talent as a solo rusher, but he’s fully functional as part of a pocket-collapsing collective. His 2024 tape might be a better representation of his upside, but Woods clearly has the potential to become a solid starter in an even front.
profiles.strengths:
• Powerful and explosive athlete.
  • Lateral quickness frequently defeats attempted reach blocks. 
  • Ties hands with feet to slide across blocker’s face and into gaps.
  • Explodes hips through initial contact at point of attack.
  • Good feel for finding the seam to split the double team.
  • Good anticipation and shed quickness to tackle as two-gapper.
  • Sturdy base allows for more consistent recovery.
  • Sets booming picks on blockers in twist game.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Plays lighter but gives more ground against single blocks.
  • Took chances that failed to pay off in the run game.
  • Short arms prevent him from keeping blockers out of his frame.
  • Average twist quickness to set off a schemed rush.
  • No real primary moves to reliably open an edge.

profiles.overview: Free safety or zone nickelback who showed impressive instincts/ball skills on tape but tested poorly at his pro day. Dunnam displays good anticipation and recognition of play design both pre- and post-snap. He can break simultaneously with wideouts and close on intended targets before the quarterback starts his throwing motion. He lacks top-end speed and is missing size/consistency as a run defender/open-field tackler. Dunnam will need to prove himself as a functional zone defender to compete for a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Has vision and athleticism to play high safety or in the slot.
  • Elite instincts help to feed his greedy mindset against offenses.
  • Plays with ideal decisiveness in both man and zone looks.
  • Anticipates route breaks and dashes into the passing lane.
  • Possesses ball skills and sticky hands of a receiver.
  • Adjusts his pursuit angles at full speed while running the alley.
  • Tackles receiver quickly to stop any run after catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks top-end speed and could struggle with vertical matchups in man.
  • Undercuts routes at steep angles, leaving him susceptible to chunk plays.
  • Slender frame shows up in run support.
  • Inconsistent to close space properly before breaking down to tackle.
  • Becomes a block magnet when perimeter blocks land.
  • Comes in way too hot as an open-field tackler, leading to misses.
  • Lacked speed and explosiveness in pro-day testing.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 8 games as a reserve and on special teams (2 tackles).
  • 2023: Played in 9 games as a reserve and on special teams (4 tackles).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 7 starts (31 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 3.5 sacks, INT, FF). 
  • 2025: Played in 10 games with 9 starts (35 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 2 sacks). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A fifth-year senior, Hutchins has started just 16 games. While he’s light on starting experience, his game is more mature. He’s undersized but stronger than his measurables might suggest. He’s physical in his block take-ons and sets edges with an adequate anchor. Hutchins creates pressure opportunities with his footwork and bend, but a lack of explosiveness in his get-off tends to limit his overall sack production. He’s an above-average athlete with good short-area burst when pursuing runners and quarterbacks. Hutchins should compete for a backup role as a stand-up edge and become a plus contributor on special teams.
profiles.strengths:
• Plays bigger and stronger at the point than his size would indicate.
  • Press strength to separate from tackles on contact.
  • Adequate ability to set an edge and anchor his ground.
  • Uses spin counter to free himself from blocks.
  • Hip bend and hard-driving feet create momentum at the corner.
  • Sequences an outside Euro-step with a chop-rip move.
  • Upper-body turn allows him to flip hips past tackles.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Undersized and lacking typical length for stand-up edge.
  • Inconsistent matching early lateral steps to secure contain.
  • Gets swallowed by big bodies when trapped in the box.
  • Below-average playing through contact.
  • Average get-off fails to stress tackles.
  • Long tackles can sideline his rush plans.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 10 games as a reserve (7 tackles, TFL with 0.5 sack). Missed 3 games due to a hamstring injury.
  • 2023: Played in 9 games as a reserve (9 tackles, 2.5 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU). Missed 4 games due to injury.
  • 2024: Second-team All-SEC. Led team with 12.5 TFLs, 9 sacks. Played in all 13 games with 11 starts (23 tackles, PBU, 2 FFs).
  • 2025: First-team All-SEC. Started 10 games (26 tackles, 9.5 TFLs with 6.5 sacks, PBU, 2 FFs, safety). Missed 3 games with a leg injury suffered during a scoop-and-score TD versus Tennessee. 
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Harvey, played football at Florida.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Twitched-up rush linebacker whose lack of size and length at the point of attack could be offset by his rush talent. Thomas has added good mass over the years but still gets engulfed and displaced by big, downhill blockers. He’s more dangerous on the move, slipping into gaps and disrupting edges before they’re set. He’s an explosive speed rusher with the ability to shave the edge tightly or create surprising push with leverage and speed-to-power conversion. He needs to improve his hand work to create openings and counter long, athletic tackles with quick pass slides. Thomas should benefit from a wider alignment as an odd-front edge with the potential to earn a starting job within his first two seasons.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He gets beat up for being small and not long enough but I think he’s going to be a nightmare for tall tackles because he can bend and he’s really explosive.” – NFC scouting director
profiles.strengths:
• High-octane rusher with explosive take-off up the field.
  • First three steps to the top of the rush are fast and furious.
  • Has the bend and ankle flexion to dip under taller tackles.
  • Will surprise tackles with his ability to convert speed to power.
  • Carves out a more shallow path into the pocket against plodding tackles.
  • Darts across blocker’s face and into gaps with excellent pad level.
  • Able to chase and capture running backs with exceptional pursuit speed.
  • Recovers from awkward angles to tackle.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Gets hung up on base blocks due to lack of length.
  • Has trouble maintaining his hand stack and holding his ground.
  • Was engulfed and pushed around in Oklahoma’s loss to Texas.
  • Long tackles are able to widen out his entry points on vertical rushes.
  • Hand fighting could use more polish at the junction point.
  • Missed multiple games in 2022, 2023 and 2025.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts (28-296-10.6, 6 TDs).
  • 2023: First-team All-American Athletic Conference. Tied for the team lead with 7 receiving TDs (34-518-15.2). Started all 14 games.
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Played in 7 games with 5 starts (24-359-15.0, 4 TDs). Missed the rest of the season with a torn ACL.
  • 2025: Played in 12 games with 7 starts (27-322-11.9, 2 TDs). Set school career records for TEs with 113 receptions, 1,495 receiving yards.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Russell, played DT at Miami and was the No. 1 pick of the 1991 NFL Draft by the Cowboys, winning 3 Super Bowls with the team and playing 10 years overall.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Pass-catching tight end whose father, Russell, was the No. 1 overall pick of the 1991 NFL Draft and spent 10 years in the league. Maryland’s acceleration into the route is average and he coasts vertically instead of driving to separate. He runs routes with adequate leverage and breaks them off at crisp angles. He has the catch radius and body adjustments to make spectacular catches, but he needs to bring in contested tries at a higher rate. As a subpar run blocker, Maryland must elevate his play as a pass-catcher to compete for a roster spot as an “F” tight end.
profiles.strengths:
• Uses leverage to draw defenders out of his route path.
  • Snaps off sharp cuts on in-breaking routes.
  • Able to make athletic in-air adjustments to his back shoulder.
  • Effective use of catch radius to snare throws outside his frame.
  • Should get some speed back with another year removed from ACL surgery.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Slow getting off the line and on top of off-man coverage.
  • Lacks acceleration to generate early vertical separation.
  • Doesn’t appear to run many routes at his true play speed.
  • Won’t make many tacklers miss after the catch.
  • Lacks technique and tenacity to block in-line on the pro level.

profiles.bio:
• 2019 (Marshall): Enrolled but did not play. Grayshirted.
  • 2020 (Lackawanna College): Did not play.
  • 2021 (Snow College): Did not play.
  • 2022 (Snow College): Rushed for 355 yards, 6 TDs in 9 games.
  • 2023 (Utah State): Played in all 13 games with 3 starts (118-736-6.2, 5 TDs rushing; 11-52-4.7 receiving).
  • 2024 (Utah State): Second-team All-Mountain West Conference. Led team with 1,109 rushing yards (198 carries, 5.6 per), 8 rushing TDs. Played in all 12 games with 10 starts (22-99-4.5 receiving). Entered the transfer portal in spring 2024 but decided to return.
  • 2025: Led team with 470 rushing yards (96 carries, 4.9 per, 3 TDs). Played in all 12 games with 7 starts (19-118-6.2 receiving). Received waiver from NCAA to play another season because he played in junior college.
  • Miscellaneous: Cousin, Rian Wallace, played LB at Temple and won Super Bowl LX with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Faison is an older prospect, but he possesses the talent and toughness to succeed. He’s an instinctive runner with the size, vision and wiggle to create yards from broken tackles. He rarely rushes the action, setting up blocks and cutting off the carnage. He’s patient but unpredictable, making it hard for linebackers to square him up. His 2025 production might look average, but his tape shows NFL ability on all three downs.
profiles.strengths:
• Smooth runner with the bend to cut sharply and force misses.
  • Doesn’t need to be cleanly blocked up to make it happen. 
  • Displays impressive vision, instincts and creativity.
  • Changes tempo and pathways, making it hard to square him up.
  • Fights through contact with a well-balanced base.
  • Drops and drives through his pads when it’s time to finish.
  • Natural pass catcher capable of adjusting to the throw.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Patient but needs to be quicker in anticipating lane development as a pro.
  • Pulls zone runs off the track before giving the line a good pressing.
  • Lacks breakaway speed to finish runs from distance.
  • No special-teams play in his college football background.
  • Will be a 26-year-old rookie.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (3 tackles).
  • 2022: Played in 13 games as a reserve (13 tackles).
  • 2023: Played in 14 games with 1 start for the national champions (27 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU, FF). Injured leg in semifinals, missed championship game.
  • 2024: Played in 11 games with 2 starts (29 tackles, 3.5 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, 2 PBUs).
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 13 games (35 tackles, 3 TFLs with 1.5 sacks, 2 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Benny is a tricky evaluation as a 3-technique. He has good length and is consistent entering into block battles. He’s an effective two-gapper who locates the ball-carrier and quickly sheds.
