On the flip side, he’s not a true wide-body and struggles to drop a sudden anchor when challenged by downhill double teams. He lacks ideal explosiveness and is unlikely to be much of a disruptor. Benny is capable of competing for a backup role as an early down interior lineman who can play in one- or two-gapping fronts.
profiles.strengths:
• Uses length and accurate hands to stay separated from blockers.
  • Two-gaps with lockout and gets his head around to find the runner.
  • Possesses the strength and length to quickly shed blocks.
  • Competent arm-over move to slip past guards and into gaps.
  • Works from blocker to blocker with active hands.
  • Adequate lateral foot quickness to challenge edge as a rusher.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average mass and only one season as a full-time starter.
  • Doesn’t capture the neutral zone with snap quickness.
  • Allows pads to rise high on lateral movements.
  • Has trouble finding his anchor against double teams.
  • Plays with inconsistent body control on the move.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 5 games as a reserve (6 tackles, PBU).
  • 2023: Tied for third in the FBS with 4 FFs. Played in 12 games with starts in the final 6 games (60 tackles, 9.5 TFLs with 2 sacks).
  • 2024: First-team All-MAC. Led the FBS with 7 FFs, ranked second with 156 tackles (behind teammate Shaun Dolac with 168). Started all 13 games (16.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, INT-returned for TD, PBU). Graduated magna cum laude with his degree in psychology.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-MAC. Ranked second in the FBS with 6 FFs. Ranked third with 142 tackles. Led team with 13.5 TFLs. Set NCAA record with 17 career FFs (breaking record of 16 set by former Buffalo Edge Khalil Mack). Started all 12 games (5 sacks, PBU). Named to the AFCA Allstate Good Works Team for his community service efforts. Finalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy, aka the Academic Heisman.
  • Miscellaneous: Founder/Director of Virginia Homework Helpers, a free K-12 tutoring program.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Inside linebacker with a nose for the football and loads of production to prove it. Murdock plays firm at the contact point with physicality and toughness. He’s ready for battle when the ball comes downhill, but he lacks the closing burst to stay ahead of blocking schemes and shut down the outside run before it turns the corner. He’s a consistent tackler with good stopping power when he’s in position. His coverage features too many mistakes and a lack of recovery talent. Murdock lacks speed and third-down value, but he’s tough, makes plays and appears suited for core special-teams duties.
profiles.strengths:
• Jarring production includes 39.5 tackles for loss in the past three seasons.
  • Set NCAA record for forced fumbles (17) with intent and technique.
  • Plays with heaviness in his hands and pads as a striker.
  • Able to absorb blocks with balance and hold his ground.
  • Can work around a block or greet it with a smack.
  • Pursues with leverage and is a successful tackle-finisher when he’s in position.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hip tightness restricts his agility and lateral quickness.
  • Below-average reaction time and flow to stay ahead of blocks.
  • Missing desired sideline-to-sideline speed to close and capture to the perimeter.
  • Slow to gather his weight and change direction in the open field.
  • Suffers from coverage confusion and loses track of targets, leading to big plays.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Miami OH): Played in 11 games with 1 start (1-28-28.0).
  • 2023 (Miami OH): Played in 12 games as a reserve (1-34-34.0, TD). Five special teams tackles.
  • 2024 (Miami OH): Second-team All-MAC. Ranked seventh in the FBS, averaging 19.9 yards per reception (41-816). Led team with 9 receiving TDs. Team's Most Improved Offensive Player of the Year. Played in 13 games with 11 starts.
  • 2025: Led team with 57 receptions (705 yards, 12.4 per, 6 TDs). Started all 14 games (2-35-17.5, 2 TDs rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tall, competitive wideout who proved he could jump from the MAC to the Big 12 and remain productive. Virgil saw starting reps in just two seasons, but he plays like a more experienced wideout. He’s light on his feet to elude press. He can run challenging routes underneath, but he could use more attention to detail on some simpler routes. He has strong hands and good body control to win when contested. He’s not special in any one area but is solid in most. Virgil could compete for a role as a WR4 with special-teams value.
profiles.strengths:
• Light on his feet with the ability to skip past press.
  • Runs routes with impressive short-area footwork.
  • Good awareness of spacing against zone.
  • Works aggressively back to the throw.
  • Makes well-timed adjustments late in the catch phase.
  • Hands are sticky and do their job to finish through contact.
  • Possesses slip-and-go talent to add yards after short catches.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Fairly easy to find and redirect for defenders playing short zone.
  • Lacks threatening upfield burst in his drive phase.
  • Struggles to bypass and quickly stack off-man corners on verticals.
  • Below-average hip sink for clean in-and-out at break points.
  • Routes are often too rounded, creating drift upfield.

profiles.overview: Slightly undersized but wearing good muscle mass, Konga is built for life as a one-gapping 3-technique. His testing numbers were eye-popping, but his career production does not align with the athletic traits. He has good first-step quickness to challenge gaps but is unable to withstand a stout drive-blocker or double-team looks. A right-handed club is his go-to rush move but it feels like there is more meat on the bone as a pass rusher for a team willing to make development a priority. Konga might need to prove himself as a situational rusher to land a spot on an NFL roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Unusually fast/explosive athletic testing for an interior defender. 
  • Initial quickness creates penetration opportunities for slanting fronts.
  • Has burst to race down the line and squeeze the run lane.
  • Uses a clubbing right hand to open rush lanes.
  • Effort and athleticism help generate his secondary rush.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Disappointing sack production relative to his athletic gifts.
  • Lacks functional anchor to fight off double-teams.
  • Needs to get better at using hands to stay separated from blocks.
  • Linear and too upright as a pass rusher.
  • Unable to generate an above-average bull-rush charge.

profiles.overview: Towering four-year starter at tackle who struggles with leverage. Mahlman’s lack of length contributes to protection breakdowns when he fails to land first hands. As a run blocker, he uses hand strikes to mitigate a lack of bend but he doesn’t have the body control to execute from entry to whistle at a consistent level. It’s tough for tall tackles to bump inside to guard, but such a move might provide Mahlman his best shot at a roster spot, provided he adds to his core strength.
profiles.strengths:
• Four-year starter with experience at both tackle spots.
  • Slides in protection with ready hands and flat back.
  • Recovers his hands into inside positioning when they’re swatted away.
  • Consistently looks for additional work as a run blocker.
  • Strikes into run block with leveraged hands that carry plus grip strength.
  • Does an adequate job of rolling hips into his block sustain.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hands lack needed precision to make up for his lack of length.
  • Oversets to his outside foot and gets beaten back inside by the rush.
  • Gives up too much ground against early bull-rush charges.
  • Gets stacked and pulled off-balance by twitchy edge defenders.
  • Inconsistent hands as a run blocker, diminishing his control and sustain.
  • Stiff-kneed when climbing to second level cut-off blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Wisconsin): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2021 (Wisconsin): Played in 2 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2022 (Wisconsin): Played in 13 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2023 (Wisconsin): Played in 9 games with 1 start (7-57-8.1, TD receiving).
  • 2024 (Wisconsin): Played in all 12 games with 9 starts (11-74-6.7 receiving). 
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Started all 16 games for the national champions (32-387-12.1, 2 TDs receiving; 2-2-1.0, 2 TDs rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Nowakowski’s focus on the task never wavers. He’s reliable and tough at the point of attack and holds up well in pass protection. He lacks height/length but is well-built and plays with better technique, strain and finish than many offensive linemen in this class. He became a productive pass-catcher in 2025, but he could struggle to separate or win the seam against NFL man coverage. His character and work ethic are outstanding, and he should help elevate run-game execution wherever an offense lines him up.
profiles.strengths:
• Fits up run blocks with good timing, accuracy and balance.
  • Gets hips unlocked and rolls into drive blocks.
  • Strains as a base blocker and works until the whistle.
  • Has frame/toughness to square off against edge defenders.
  • Impressive technique and core strength make him trustworthy in protection.
  • Catches with reliable hands and consistent focus.
  • Unfazed playing through route and catch contact.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Requires more instinctive hand resets as a run blocker.
  • Long edge rushers can stab and discard his protection.
  • Struggle to separate from man coverage.
  • Gives breaks away and lacks burst out of his turns.
  • Below-average run-after-catch quickness.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Jones College): 81-495-6.1, 6 TDs rushing in 10 games.
  • 2022 (Jones College): First-team NJCAA All-American, NJCAA Offensive Player of the Year. Won the inaugural Walter Jones Trophy (top Junior College player). Led NJCAA in rushing with 1,302 yards, 18 TDs on 237 carries. 19-128 receiving.
  • 2023: Led team with 11 rushing TDs (127-588-4.6). Played in all 13 games as a reserve (19-115-6.1 receiving).
  • 2024: Led team with 706 rushing yards (130 carries, 5.4 per, 7 TDs). Played in 11 games with 10 starts (21-199-9.5, TD receiving).
  • 2025: First-team All-American Athletic Conference. Ranked third in the FBS with 6.9 yards per carry. Led team with 1,045 rushing yards (151 carries, 6.9 per), 9 rushing TDs. Started 11 games (18-114-6.3, 2 TDs receiving). Set school career record with 5.7 yards per carry.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior whose splashy early season performance against Texas A&M put him on the map. Henry is a slasher with a wiggly lower half, allowing him to make sudden cuts and elude tacklers in tight quarters. He’s quicker than fast and struggles to consistently read/react to the development of run lanes. While his burst can create occasional chunk gains, he too often does not keep runs on their designed tracks. He’s yet to show he can be a major factor on third downs and fumbled six times in the last three seasons, which could be impediments in his pursuit of a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Rushed for 177 yards and two TDs against Texas A&M.
  • Gains good lateral ground with swift jump-cuts to escape trouble.
  • Bendy in ankles and hips to quickly cut at crisp angles.
  • Burst takes him to his top speed in a hurry.
  • Slippery lowers and short-area wiggle create missed tackles.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks tempo and rhythm in getting to run actions.
  • Hurries runs and either misses the entry point or runs into blocker.
  • Doesn’t take much for him to pull runs off-track and bounce them wide.
  • Lacks instincts and feel for setting up tacklers.
  • Missing the power and running style to collide and fall forward.
  • The tape suggests he is not a third-down option.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in the final 9 games as a reserve (15 tackles, 0.5 TFL).
  • 2023: Played in 12 games with 2 starts (38 tackles, TFL, PBU).  
  • 2024: Tied for fifth in the FBS with 4 FFs. Played in all 13 games with starts in the final 11 contests (66 tackles, 5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, INT, PBU). 
  • 2025: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (59 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, INT, 2 PBUs, FF).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Spears-Jennings is a two-year starter with NFL traits. He has the size and toughness of a pro safety. He’s quick to dive in and fill the run near the line. He’s a sound tackler once he’s lined up but inconsistent tracking angles and a lack of body control cause him to mistime his target. He has plus coverage tools but lacks feel in man coverage and suffers from a lack of awareness playing from depth. The traits and special-teams talent should buy him time to prove himself a competent backup playing near the line.
profiles.strengths:
• Outstanding size with above-average athleticism.
  • Erases space downhill and fills the front like a linebacker.
  • Crashes weight into targets to immediately stop runs.
  • Explosive pedal-to-drive transitions in space.
  • Striking power to intimidate receivers over the middle.
  • Has a chance to star on punt- and kick-cover teams.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs to do a better job of playing off of blocks.
  • Long strider who loses pursuit leverage running the alley.
  • Rushes in hot and runs past entry points to tackle.
  • Gets late starts gaining depth from split-safety.
  • Below-average break anticipation in man coverage.
  • Responsible for red-zone coverage busts against Ole Miss and Tennessee.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Maryland): Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve (17-71-4.2, 2 TDs rushing; 1-1-1.0 receiving; 1-28-28.0 KR).
  • 2022 (Maryland): Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 989 rushing yards (188 carries, 5.3 per), 10 rushing TDs. Started all 13 games (33-298-9.0, TD receiving; 4-43-10.8 KR).
  • 2023 (Maryland): Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Led team with 680 rushing yards (142 carries, 4.8 per, 4 TDs). Started all 13 games (38-349-9.2, 3 TDs receiving; 1-18-18.0 KR). 
  • 2024 (Maryland): Led team with 607 rushing yards (134 carries, 4.5 per), 6 rushing TDs. Started all 12 games (40-273-6.8, TD receiving).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten. Led team with 1,120 rushing yards (230 carries, 4.9 per, 7 TDs). Started all 16 games for the national champions (17-165-9.7 receiving; 9-203-22.6 KR).
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Ky'el, played DB at Iowa Western Community College and Southern Miss.

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Hard-charging runner with average vision/burst but good decisiveness and the ability to finish through contact. Hemby is wired for hard running inside, but he has the one-cut quickness to succeed on zone carries. He has stop-start quickness to reset the run against penetration but rarely looks to elude tacklers once he hits it downfield. Punishing collisions are inevitable for defensive backs looking to tackle him in the open field. He’s willing in protection but must clean up mental errors. Hemby is a viable pass-catcher, which should add to his value as a likely Day 3 pick and potential three-down backup who can handle short-yardage carries right away.
profiles.strengths:
• Keeps runs on schedule and headed downhill.
  • One-cut quickness to snap it off at tight angles.
  • Shows ability to get skinny and sneak through tight crevices.
  • Accelerates through contact and consistently falls forward.
  • Tucks it tight and rarely puts the ball on the ground.
  • Reliable hands and catches when contested.
  • Shows a willingness to stand in and square up blitzers.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Inconsistent vision leads to missed opportunities.
  • Below-average burst through the hole.
  • Rarely seeks additional cuts once he makes a downhill decision.
  • Tight hips limit ability to open and stride in space.
  • Enters into contact with higher pad level.
  • Protection mistakes resulted in hard hits on the quarterback against Iowa.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Miami): Played in 11 games as a reserve (7-90-12.9, TD).
  • 2022 (Miami): Played in 9 games as a reserve (7-99-14.1).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games (28-431-15.4, 2 TDs).
  • 2024: Played in 6 games (13-135-10.4 receiving; 1-6-6.0 rushing). Missed the end of the regular season due to a knee injury.
  • 2025: Played in 12 games (43-638-14.8, 3 TDs receiving; 1-4-4.0 rushing).
  • Miscellaneous: Cousin, Chad "Ochocinco" Johnson, was a 6-time Pro Bowl WR.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Brinson is a field-stretcher, but the middle of his route tree is missing branches. He’s a long-strider with good acceleration to build speed and create opportunities for himself on vertical routes. His route-running is less effective on intermediate routes, where he’s slower in and out of breaks. Despite his catch radius and hand size, he wins fewer 50/50 balls than he should when coverage closes him down. Brinson has traits to work with but offers a more limited menu of services for teams.
profiles.strengths:
• Above-average wingspan with big hands.
  • Burst and stride length to eat cushion and blow by corners.
  • Settles and opens to quarterback quickly on zone-beaters.
  • Smart hand-fighting to swat away press and separate downfield.
  • Maintains top speed through vertical route transitions.
  • Elusive after the catch to shake the first tackler.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Upright into intermediate break points, requiring excessive gather steps.
  • Defensive backs can read/close on his curls and stop routes.
  • Below-average at bodying and shielding corners from catch point.
  • Needs earlier adjustments to underthrows for dibs on catch space.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Auburn): Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2021 (Auburn): Played in 9 games as a reserve (19 tackles, 3 TFLs).
  • 2022 (USC): Started 2 games. Missed the rest of the season with a shoulder injury.
  • 2023 (USC): Played in 12 games as a reserve (21 tackles, 6 TFLs with 4 sacks).
  • 2024 (Georgia Tech): Led team with 6.5 TFLs, 2 FFs. Started 12 games (34 tackles, 2.5 sacks, INT).
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12 Conference. Started all 14 games (38 tackles, 11.5 TFLs with 10 sacks, PBU, 2 FFs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: An edge defender with a lean, angular frame, Height will need a heavy dose of weight-room work to compete at the pro level. His rush is fast and relentless. He uses long strides to challenge at the top and can leap inside the protection. However, his lack of play strength and contact balance allow blockers to bounce him around. Height needs to improve his skill level and refine his approach if he’s going to make an impact as a designated pass rusher, but he has the talent to cause some chaos in the pocket.
profiles.strengths:
• Inside spin move can become an even more effective weapon.
  • Long-strider with the ability to quickly gain ground.
  • Rushes with consistent energy and urgency on each snap.
  • Very loose in his hips, allowing contortion around the block.
  • Uses punch-pull technique to get rid of base blocks.
  • Good back-side burst to close and tackle cutback runners.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Must add more muscle mass to hold up as a pro.
  • Lacks instincts and post-snap recognition.
  • Will struggle to hold the point and leverage gaps as a pro.
  • Missing base and contact balance to keep from getting jostled around.
  • Lacks the play strength to fight through redirect blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. Third-team All-ACC. ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year. Led team with 3 FFs, tied for the team lead with 7.5 sacks. Played in all 13 games with 11 starts (44 tackles, 12.5 TFLs, PBU).
  • 2024: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started 9 games (23 tackles, 5.5 TFLs with 3.5 sacks). Missed 4 games due to injury.
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. ACC Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-ACC. Finalist for the Lott IMPACT Trophy (nation's top defender with Integrity, Maturity, Performance, Academics, Community, Tenacity). Started all 16 games (54 tackles, 15.5 TFLs with 9.5 sacks, INT, PBU, FF).
  • Miscellaneous: Nickname is "Hurricane" (Bain). Father Rueben was called "Hurricane" by the Carol City High School PA announcer, played at Morris Brown College. Cousin, Tolbert, played DB for Miami. Brother, Reggie, was an OL grad assistant at Miami for two seasons before moving on to SMU to join former Miami coach Rhett Lashlee.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Note taker, grudge holder and block destructor with a compact frame and defensive tackle play strength. Bain is ill-tempered with his take-ons, hitting blockers with heavy hand strikes. He plays through tight ends and can anchor against tackles and double teams. However, his lack of length can lead to him being smothered if he doesn’t land the first strike. He can bend and flip his hips at the top of the rush, swipe away punches and generate a strong bull rush. His playoff run showed an ability to generate quick wins if tackles are passive in setting to him. He can rush off the edge or mismatch guards as a sub-package rusher. Bain’s explosive power and toughness should translate, giving him a high floor as an NFL starter.
profiles.strengths:
• Loose hips and violent hands create shorter rush corners.
  • Disguises speed-to-power charge, surprising tackles.
  • Can stab and shove tackles off-balance, creating inside openings.
  • Accurate two-hand swipe batters and clears the punch.
  • Power like a defensive tackle with agility like an edge.
  • Explodes punch into the chest of blocker.
  • Can eat blocks and hold his ground at the point of attack.
  • Hands and feet are in full alliance to shed and work around edges.
  • Coached by NFL rush aficionado and Hall of Famer, Jason Taylor.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Ducks head and drops eyes, driving into run blocks. 
  • Short arms will get him crowded at the point of attack.
  • Average pursuit speed out to the flanks.
  • Will take some plays off when action doesn’t come his way. 
  • Counters don't come naturally at the top of the rush. 
  • Average closing burst to the quarterback.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Redshirted. Played in 1 game (1-41-41.0). Enrolled in January.
  • 2023: Freshman All-American. Second-team All-Big Ten Conference. Ranked eighth in the FBS with 46.8 yards per punt (55-2,576, long 67, 2 touchbacks, 21 fair caught, 24 inside the 20; 1 coverage tackle). Played in all 12 games.
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big Ten. Would have ranked fourth in the FBS with 47.9 yards per punt but did not have enough kicks to qualify (43-2,060, long 61, 4 touchbacks, 9 fair caught, 6 inside the 20; 1 coverage tackle). Holder on XP/FG.
  • 2025: Third-team Associated Press All-American. Big Ten Punter of the Year, First-team All-Big Ten. Led the FBS with 48.5 yards per punt (49-2,378, long 60, 1 touchback, 11 fair caught, 20 inside the 20). Played in all 12 games (0-1 FG; 6 touchbacks on 16 kickoffs, 1 coverage tackle).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Three-year punter whose solid gross punt numbers get washed away by too many returns. Eckley hits the ball with good consistency, but his punts are often low line drives that are tough for gunners to cover. He punts with good touch and was outstanding in burying opponents deep in their own territory last season. Eckley’s chances of making a roster will be tied directly to his ability to develop NFL-caliber hang time.
profiles.strengths:
• Hits the ball with good consistency of force.
  • Led the FBS with 48.5 yards per punt in 2025.
  • Excellent at landing short-field punts inside the 10 over the last two seasons.
  • Adequate touch-to-toe time in his operation.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Poor hang-time numbers throughout his career.
  • Regularly outkicks his coverage.

profiles.overview: Developmental offensive lineman whose inconsistencies could begin to correct themselves with more technique work and experience. Mosesso needs to add mass but carries an NFL frame with good lean mass. His athletic ability, hand strength and contact pop are elements that create projection potential at either tackle or guard. He seems to lack instincts/understanding of how to get to his actions with proper footwork and positioning at this juncture. Mosesso’s issues appear to be correctable with better technique, so a team willing to play the long game with him could benefit in the future.
profiles.strengths:
• Pass sets feature good posture and adequate balance.
  • Strong hands are quick and active in protection.
  • Mirrors rush movement with athletic basketball slides
  • Has the feet and hips to recover into position when needed.
  • Initial quickness to climb up and cut off back-side linebacker.
  • Drives hands into run blocks with proper placement/leverage.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Technique and instincts need a good deal of work.
  • Issues with footwork/body control to his landmarks as a run blocker.
  • Lacks proper timing on his work-up blocks to the linebacker.
  • Needs improved punch-timing to prevent being driven into the backfield.
  • Hasn’t learned to properly reset his hands when needed.
  • Struggled to redirect Missouri’s edge rushers up and around the pocket.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted as a walk-on.
  • 2022: Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2023: Played in all 13 games as a reserve and on special teams.
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Started all 13 games at C. Received a scholarship.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12. Started all 12 games at C.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Hecht lacks ideal mass and length but it will be hard to find a center in this year’s draft with better technique. He plays with well-placed inside hands that help maximize his leverage and core strength. All schemes are available to him but his athleticism will shine when activated in space. He stays sticky to blocks once he connects, but his lack of length will put him on the wrong side of the battle from time to time in both the run and pass phases. Hecht needs to add more muscle mass to his frame but he has the consistency and tape of a future starter.
profiles.strengths:
• Impressive blend of athleticism, agility and core strength.
  • Gets into run fits with proper footwork and body control. 
  • Excellent hand placement/resets to help control and guide the block.
  • Agile feet for smooth skip pulls around the corner and into space to lead the charge.
  • Uses strong hands and active feet to stay connected to his blocks. 
  • Works well with teammates on double-teams and on twist pickups.
  • Pass protects with inside hands and a wide base to mirror.
  • Eyes work quickly to new targets when diagnosing rush games.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Doesn't have much knock-back pop into initial contact. 
  • Can be extended and pulled off-balance by salty two-gappers. 
  • Average snap-to-step quickness to slide laterally and slow A-gap shots.
  • Can be impatient climbing and stalking second-level linebackers.
  • Beat to the punch at times due to below-average arm length. 
  • Has some trouble protecting his edges in pass pro.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 12 games as a reserve and on special teams (2-34-17.0).
  • 2023: Played in all 12 games with 10 starts (28-288-10.3). 
  • 2024: Started all 12 games (40-334-8.3, 2 TDs). 
  • 2025: Second-team All-ACC. Started all 12 games (49-545-11.1, 2 TDs). 
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Luke, played football at Duke. Mother, Brooke, played volleyball at Montana State. Maternal grandfather, Phil Olsen, played football at Utah State and in the NFL. Maternal great uncle is the late Pro Football Hall of Famer and actor Merlin Olsen. Paternal grandfather, John Roush, played football at Ohio. Cousin, Hans Olsen, played football at BYU.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: In a draft landscape full of pass-catching tight ends, Roush stands out as one of the few plug-and-play “Y” tight ends (in-line blocking TE) available. He can make cut-off blocks in zone and combo blocks in gap schemes. He holds his own in pass protection, too. As a receiver, he’s not stiff, but he lacks elusiveness underneath. He needs to apply more of his tough playing style to win combat catches and expand his role beyond run blocker/zone beater. While his catch production might draw questions, his size, toughness and pro-ready blocking profile could push him into Day 2 consideration.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: "He’s big, tough and sound as a blocker and he’s a really smart kid, too. Picks up everything quickly.” – NFC personnel director
profiles.strengths:
• Long line of collegiate/pro athletes in his family.
  • Relied on as an extension of the offensive line at Stanford.
  • Comes off the ball with good knee bend, pad level and inside hands.
  • Runs through initial contact to pop opponents and establish the tone.
  • Footwork and positioning to help seal the edge on wide runs.
  • Well-schooled in working up to the linebacker on combo blocks.
  • Gets in and out of breaks/stems with good efficiency.
  • Runs behind his pads after the catch and is tough to bring down.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Outside arm will reach and hook defender when he misses positioning.
  • Fails to disguise route intentions and elude man coverage.
  • Can be crossed up by throws that are outside his frame.
  • Needs to play bigger when contested.
  • Must do a better job of using size/strength to carve out catch space.
  • Holding penalties were an issue for him in 2024.

profiles.overview: Scott looks the part with good size and a muscular frame. The speed and explosive leaping ability he displayed at his pro day is sure to catch the eyes of evaluators. Unfortunately, he never hit 100 carries or 450 yards rushing in a single season at Wyoming and doesn’t run with nearly enough power for the size/explosiveness he has at his disposal. Scott is best as a linear runner when he’s allowed to build speed and make more subtle change-of-direction cuts. He will have to compete for a spot in camp, but he has the traits and athleticism to warrant consideration on special teams.
profiles.strengths:
• Excellent blend of size and top-end speed.
  • Showed tremendous leaping ability at his pro day.
  • Displays good change-of-direction quickness.
  • Adequate burst to challenge in a race to the corner.
  • Has size and strength to protect his quarterback.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Runs a little too tall through the line and into contact.
  • Average feel for run-lane development inside.
  • Reacts to linebackers instead of setting them up.
  • Has runs where he will tap breaks slightly through contact.
  • Below average as a pass catcher out of the backfield.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Mississippi State): Redshirted. 
  • 2022 (Mississippi State): Played in 5 games as a reserve (6-11-54.5, 23 yards, INT).
  • 2023: Played in 6 games with 4 starts (66-117-56.4, 864 yards, 2 TDs, 4 INTs passing; 35-69-2.0, TD rushing).
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 10 starts (229-368-62.2, 3,071 yards, 28 TDs, 8 INTs passing; 63-230-3.7, 4 TDs rushing).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-Big 12 Conference. Ranked fifth in the FBS with 31 passing TDs (versus 12 INTs), sixth with 3,681 passing yards and eighth with 304 completions (504 attempts, 60.3%). Started all 12 games (56-17-0.3, 3 TDs rushing). Finalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy, aka the Academic Heisman. Big 12 Scholar-Athlete of the Year.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Stan, played football and baseball at Texas Tech. He was a first-round pick of the Montreal Expos in the 1990 Major League Baseball draft. Cousin, Jarrett Stidham, played QB at Baylor and Auburn and is now in the NFL.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with pro traits and arm talent. Robertson possesses a quick release and good velocity, but his subpar touch, timing and accuracy are notable on the first two levels. He’ll need better eye discipline to keep linebackers and safeties from jumping passing lanes. He’s composed in the face of pressure and can make off-platform throws when needed. He’s mobile but won’t beat many teams with extended plays. A shift away from spread-based reads to a more balanced attack featuring traditional tight ends could help, but Robertson’s struggles with accuracy and ball placement could be tough to overcome.
profiles.strengths:
• Good blend of height, weight and arm strength.
  • Release quickness and velocity to beat coverage into tight windows.
  • Trusts his offensive line to do its job in protection.
  • Adequate poise to stand and deliver in the face of pressure.
  • Can make all the throws and is decisive in attacking Cover 2 windows.
  • Adequate scrambler/runner with toughness to grab extra yards.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Below-average accuracy working outside the numbers.
  • Deep throws come out too flat and with inconsistent depth.
  • Completion percentage hurt by habit of rushing throws unnecessarily.
  • Rips gas at short and intermediate targets when touch is needed.
  • Struggles to find proper placement on anticipatory throws.
  • Needs to work on sliding and eliminating head-first dives.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Florida): Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve (3 tackles).
  • 2022 (Florida): Played in 8 games as a reserve (14 tackles).
  • 2023 (Florida): Tied for the team lead with 2 FFs. Played in all 12 games with 10 starts (53 tackles, 4 TFLs with 1 sack, 2 FFs).
  • 2024: Played in 11 games with 10 starts (43 tackles, 7.5 TFLs, INT, 4 PBUs). Head coach Mike Elko told reporters in June 2025 that Williams played most of the 2024 season with a torn meniscus.
  • 2025: Played in 7 games with 3 starts (19 tackles, 4 TFLs with 1 sack, INT, FF). Missed several games due to injury.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Tall linebacker who lacked standout production in his two seasons at Texas A&M. Williams’ instincts and play speed are average but he’s usually in position to compete as a run defender. He attacks blocks with pop but needs to improve at playing off blocks or slipping them altogether. He’s a fluid athlete in space with the potential to be a plus defender in zone and man coverages. Williams’ subpar tackling combined with durability concerns create a significant gap between his ceiling and floor.
profiles.strengths:
• Attacks lead blockers with good downhill force.
  • Quick to flow into run fits and squeeze the lane.
  • Adequate pursuit speed and short-area burst.
  • Gains depth quickly on spot drops in coverage. 
  • Smooth in space to flow with quarterback’s eyes or cover man.
  • Praised by staff for his character.
  • Showed toughness, playing through a torn meniscus for most of 2024.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Instincts and recognition of blocking schemes are average. 
  • Climbing blockers tend to stick to him once they land.
  • Below-average block-slipper in space.
  • Struggles to consistently square up tackle targets. 
  • Excessive arm tackling leads to high miss count.

profiles.bio:
• 2020 (Oklahoma): Played in 7 games as a reserve (58-370-6.4, 3 TDs rushing; 13-201-15.5, TD receiving).
  • 2021: Did not play, dismissed from Oklahoma's football team. Arrested for robbery, conspiracy to commit robbery and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon in April 2021. Pled guilty to larceny while the other charges were dismissed. Spent 3 months in prison and a year on probation.
  • 2022 (Texas College): Practiced but held out of games.
  • 2023 (Butler Community College): 125 yards, 4 TDs rushing; 5-104 receiving in 6 games.
  • 2024 (New Mexico State): Second-team All-Conference USA. Led team with 823 rushing yards (152 carries, 5.4 per, 3 TDs). Played in all 12 games with starts in the final 11 contests (23-377-12.0, 3 TDs receiving).
  • 2025: Led team with 725 rushing yards (165 carries, 4.4 per), 12 rushing TDs. Played in 11 games with 10 starts )19-126-6.6 receiving).

– by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: McGowan is quick to process and has enough wiggle to create when needed. However, his lack of explosive carries and fumble totals are concerning. McGowan is effective in short-yardage situations and flashes the skill to handle backup carries, but his age and lack of third-down value could work against him on draft day.
profiles.strengths:
• Quick to process the front and find lanes without slowing.
  • Patient with block development.
  • Knee-bender with good tempo in stacking cuts.
  • Good decisiveness whether running inside or outside.
  • Natural instincts for creating space from tacklers.
  • Battles and rejects tacklers, using base strength and balance.
  • Willing to square up in blitz pickup.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs to incorporate more urgency to hit the hole quicker.
  • Had just 13 of 165 carries go for 10+ yards in 2025, with a season long of just 20 yards, per PFF.
  • Five fumbles in the last two seasons.
  • Lacks focus and technique to be a third-down option.

profiles.overview: Traore is a "F" tight end with good athleticism, average size and a need for development. His route-running is unfocused but fixable. He has soft hands and good body control from his background as a goalkeeper. While he has decent vertical speed, he must improve his separation burst out of breaks to uncover against man coverage. He’s not built for in-line blocking but has impressive moments when lead-blocking in space. Traore is a practice squad candidate with enough upside to find a roster spot down the road.
profiles.strengths:
• Late comer to the sport with athleticism and passion to keep improving.
  • Gets off the snap and up the seam with enough speed to threaten.
  • Hands are soft and confident when attacking the high point.
  • Former goalkeeper with good body control.
  • Finds a second gear in the open field.
  • Fits up run blocks with balanced base and inside hands.
  • Good feel for leverage on lead pulls in space.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Upright and elongated getting through his routes.
  • Incoming break points are too easy for coverage to decipher.
  • Average acceleration to separate coming out of turns.
  • Slow to pluck and tuck the throw, leading to missed catches.
  • Too much coasting into the top of the route on zone-beaters.
  • Lacks necessary mass and grit for in-line blocking duties.
  • Takes inconsistent angles climbing to linebackers.

profiles.overview: Compact and twitchy, Banks is an inside linebacker with explosive athletic traits but uneven execution. He can trigger instantly from his perch and has plus range from sideline to sideline. However, he plays with too much wasted movement when diagnosing and flowing to the football. He does an excellent job of slipping blocks without sacrificing gap leverage and is a wrap-up tackler. He can get hung up on take-ons and will void zone coverages at inopportune times, though. Inconsistency is an issue but his explosiveness and special-teams potential give him a chance to make a roster.
profiles.strengths:
• Very good at dipping under and around blocks.
  • Stays wide in the hole to meet the runner.
  • Explodes through contact when possible.
  • Twitchy trigger sends him racing to the action.
  • Impressive burst and pursuit speed across the field.
  • Starred on kick-cover teams early in his career.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Too much unnecessary movement during the diagnosis phase.
  • Uses short bursts instead of measured flow to the football.
  • Lacks instincts and feel for play development.
  • Gets stuck on blocks that get into him.
  • Inconsistent maintaining zone integrity.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Wisconsin): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Wisconsin): Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (30-444-14.8, 5 TDs receiving; 13-260-12.3 rushing).
  • 2023 (Wisconsin): Played in 12 games with 2 starts (38-296-7.8, TD). 
  • 2024: Led team with 860 receiving yards (50 receptions, 17.2 per), 5 receiving TDs. Started all 13 games.
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. Finalist for the Biletnikoff Award (given to the nation's top WR). Ranked second in the FBS with 1,278 receiving yards and fourth with school-record 101 receptions; tied for third in the FBS with a school-record 13 receiving TDs. Started all 13 games. 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Bell is an inside/outside target with adequate size and field-stretching speed. He has the tools to beat press quickly and the acceleration/cut quickness to open clean windows. While he’s sudden in and out of his break points, his route-running can be a tad mechanical at times. Bell’s catch focus appeared sharper in 2025 but his career drop total rivals his touchdown total. The TDs left on the field due to underthrown passes at UConn will turn into NFL touchdowns with an accurate passer. Bell’s speed and upside should make him a productive starter.
profiles.strengths:
• Elite production, ranking among the FBS’ top three in catches, yards and touchdowns.
  • Rapid foot turnover quickly eats cornerback’s cushion.
  • Instant acceleration becomes runaway speed.
  • Sinks hips and bursts out of turns/breaks to open the throwing window.
  • Turns short slants into big plays after the catch.
  • Threatens all three levels of the field.
  • Good body control with sudden, late hands on contested sideline throws.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Wastes motion against press instead of winning clean.
  • Mechanical routes don’t always feature his true speed.
  • Body-catcher who loses focus over the middle.
  • Lacks extension and hand strength to finish when contested.
  • Fast post-catch but only average elusiveness.
  • Needs to make quicker adjustments to capture air space on 50/50 balls.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Upper Iowa): Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Northern Illinois): Redshirted as a walk-on.
  • 2023 (Northern Illinois): Played in all 13 games as a reserve (24 tackles, 4 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU).
  • 2024 (Northern Illinois): Third-team All-MAC. Team captain. Played in 12 games with 1 start (51 tackles, 8 TFLs with 5 sacks).
  • 2025: Started the first 6 games (13 tackles, 2.5 TFLs with 0.5 sacks, INT-returned for TD, PBU). Missed the second half of the year with an ankle injury.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Gill-Howard is an undersized one-gapper using suddenness and leverage to elude the clenches of bigger players. He plays with a non-stop motor and palpable sense of urgency, creating wins off the snap against the run and pass. He gives blockers no reps off. His secondary effort and block counters keeps him in the play longer. Gill-Howard lacks functional size and length, which will make him both scheme- and matchup-dependent as a pro. He needs to major in disruption and chaos to find a long-term home as a rotational, upfield tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Balance and leverage to stay upright and in the play.
  • Typically beats lateral blocks to the spot.
  • First step and closing burst are both rush weapons.
  • Sets up edge attack with well-timed slide step.
  • Works two-hand swipe and slap/swim to clear the blocker’s edge.
  • Gets to instant counters when the initial rush stalls.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Smaller with shorter arms.
  • Engulfed once bigger linemen latch on.
  • Lacks length for two-gapping and mass to fight double teams.
  • Pressure production generated by the same move/approach.
  • Missing power element to collapse the pocket.
  • Season-ending ankle injury in October required surgery.

profiles.overview: Long safety prospect with intriguing man-cover talent against “F” tight ends, which could earn him a longer look from NFL scouts. Thomas moves around the field like a big cornerback, utilizing good short-area quickness and smooth transitions in coverage. He’s capable in some split-safety looks and is impressive when asked to press pass-catching tight ends working from the slot. Thomas’ tackling must improve, but his special-teams value and coverage potential might earn him a roster spot.
profiles.strengths:
• Makes good use of arm length in playing the ball.
  • Shut down TE Max Klare in 2024 in his man-cover reps.
  • Good reactive quickness to lateral break points from off-man.
  • Quick to read the run and get downhill to fit it.
  • Special-teams star during his college career.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lack of speed limits range in coverage and in pursuit.
  • Loses ground when forced to flip and run with vertical routes.
  • Could use better eye balance between route and passer.
  • Struggles coming to balance and will overrun the tackle in space.
  • Inconsistent at centering and running through as a tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in 10 games as a reserve (9 tackles).
  • 2023: Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (53 tackles, 4.5 TFLs with 2 sacks, PBU, FF).
  • 2024: Second-team All-Big Ten. Started all 16 games for the national champions (100 tackles, 10.5 TFLs with 6 sacks, 5 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big Ten. Led team with 82 tackles. Started all 14 games (6.5 TFLs with 1 sack, INT, 3 PBUs, FF). Team captain.
  • Miscellaneous: Father, Lorenzo Styles Sr., played LB for Ohio State and in the NFL for 6 years, winning Super Bowl XXXIV with the Rams. Brother, Lorenzo Styles Jr., played WR at Notre Dame before transferring to Ohio State to play CB in 2024.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Styles began his Ohio State career as a safety, but he settled in at linebacker in 2024. He’s improved in diagnosing play development. The former Buckeye diffuses block attempts with crisp hand strikes and leverages run fits with force/anchor strength. There are times when he slips back into a containment-based approach, but he has plenty of short-area quickness and pursuit speed to get where he needs to go. He can make an impact from multiple spots on the field and is a plus man-cover talent. Styles is an emerging player with the traits and versatility to garner longer looks by NFL evaluators. He could see his stock soar leading up to draft day.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “It’s hard to look at him and think that he was ever a safety with that frame. And he’s always been wired like a linebacker.” – AFC regional scout
profiles.strengths:
• Lines up the defensive front and makes adjustments if needed.
  • Disciplined in sifting through pre- and post-snap eye candy.
  • Pops and separates from climbing blockers with a crisp punch.
  • Constricts run fits by using size, force and technique.
  • Scrapes quickly to the action without losing leverage.
  • Impressive talent for slipping through traffic and into tackles.
  • Versatility/athleticism can be weaponized for coverage disguise.
  • Gains depth and widens to the flats with above-average quickness.
  • Impeccable tackle finisher.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Recognition of blocking schemes needs more work.
  • Can afford to crank up the urgency at times.
  • Slow to reaccelerate on stop/start movements in pursuit.
  • Tight hips prevent fluid change of direction from downhill flow.
  • Inconsistent shading zone drops to quarterback’s eyes.
  • Average instincts and physicality as a blitzer.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (11 at LT, 1 at RT).
  • 2024: Second-team Associated Press All-American. First-team All-Big 12 Conference. Started all 12 games at RT.
  • 2025: First-team Associated Press All-American. Won the Outland Trophy (nation's top interior lineman). Big 12 OL of the Year. First-team All-Big 12. Polynesian College Co-Player of the Year with USC WR Makai Lemon. Started 12 games at RT. Team captain.
  • Miscellaneous: Brother, Logan, was an All-Big 12 Edge at Utah and is also a prospect in the 2026 draft class. Uncles Gabe Reid (BYU), Spencer Reid (BYU), Teni Palepoi (Utah) and Anton Palepoi (UNLV) played college football and in the NFL.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fano lacks ideal proportional build but compensates with loose hips, quick feet and high-end athleticism. He has the tools to mirror speed rushers, wall off the top of the pocket and find a late anchor when taking the worst of a bull rush. He needs to stay square longer to prevent inside moves and refine his punch approach/timing. His athletic profile is designed for move-based blocking schemes where he can pull, reach and climb while beating opponents to the spot with quickness/feel for hitting landmarks on time. He gives good effort as a downhill blocker but issues with pad level and core strength lead to him being overtaken as the rep progresses. Fano’s level of NFL success might be tied to scheme fit and individual matchups.
profiles.strengths:
• Three-year starter with experience at both tackle spots.
  • Has extensive reps in prominent run-blocking schemes.
  • Good hand-strike quickness when allowed to fire out.
  • Accelerates feet and runs through angle blocks on contact.
  • Has footwork and body control to stay connected on move blocks.
  • Athleticism/adjustments can spring runs and screens in space.
  • Flies out of his stance and in front of the rusher with quickness.
  • Above-average mirroring the rush with foot quickness.
  • Able to unlock hips and ride edge rushers around the pocket.
  • Good at finding his footing after early push from speed to power.
  • Feints punches to draw and dry out rusher’s hand swipe attempts.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lean through his chest, waist and thighs by NFL standards.
  • Lacks upper-body and core strength to sustain in-blocks at pro level.
  • Pad level rides way too high on drive blocks.
  • Can be pressed and displaced by heavy-handed ends.
  • Loses “first in” battles to the frame with his pass punch.
  • Will overset instead of working inside/out against speed rushers.
  • Opens outside half too quickly, creating opportunities for inside moves.
  • Must guard against lunging with inside hand and hugging with outside hand.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. Set school record for freshman with 12.5 TFLs. Played in 13 games with 3 starts (32 tackles, 5.5 sacks, 2 PBUs).
  • 2024: Second-team All-ACC. Tied for second in the FBS with a school-record 6 FFs, ranked fifth with 19.5 TFLs, ninth with 11 sacks. Started all 14 games (57 tackles, PBU).
  • 2025: Honorable Mention All-ACC. Started 12 games (37 tackles, 9.5 TFLs with 5 sacks, PBU). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Powerful edge defender with NFL length whose 2025 tape might be closer to his pro projection than his gaudy 2024 numbers. Parker’s hand work is above average in both phases. He strikes early to set very firm edges, then sheds quickly to finish tackles. Average short-area burst limits his ability to pursue the run in space and threaten tackles in a race to the top of the rush. He can long-arm tackles into the pocket when he catches them right, but he fails to find quick solutions when that approach stalls. His rush production will be muted until he expands his approach but improvement is likely. Parker profiles as an average to above-average starter.
profiles.sourcesTellUs: “He had better numbers in 2024 but also he just played better. I felt like he saw more attention (in 2025) and didn’t always respond well.” – NFC scouting director
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 11 sacks, 19.5 tackles for loss and 6 forced fumbles in 2024.
  • Possesses upper-body strength to press and stack tackles.
  • Builds a wall as edge-setter, turning runs back inside. 
  • Effective use of hands to quickly get off blocks.
  • Long-arm rush can devastate tackles and roll them into the pocket.
  • Attacks and dislodges blocker's outside hand to open the corner. 
  • Keys backfield to bring his rush with the quarterback's movements.
  • Drives and steers blockers out of the way inside the pocket.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks firm pop into first contact versus run blocks.
  • Gets widened out when drive-blockers land first.
  • Below-average pursuit speed chasing from the back side.
  • Short-strider lacking burst in his upfield climb and cornering.
  • Static frame for tackles to find with their punch.
  • Slow to reset secondary effort when bull rush stalls.
  • Needs to diversify his rush tools and menu.

profiles.overview: High-motor interior lineman with below-average mass but above-average athletic testing to compensate. Burke is a decorated, three-year starter who plays with good hands to separate and shed at the point. He’s been successful at working from edge to edge as a rusher against single blocks but lacks longer levers to work around bigger bodies. While he’s played at a consistent level over the last two seasons, the jump in competition could make finding a roster spot a big challenge as a pro.
profiles.strengths:
• Posted 17.5 tackles for loss and 11 sacks in the last two seasons.
  • Good first-step quickness and burst off the snap.
  • Plus lateral movement down the line of scrimmage.
  • Above average use of hands in both phases.
  • Good cross-face pass rush success on the move.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Faces a huge step up in competition.
  • Doesn’t impose his will consistently enough.
  • Below average knock-back pop into first contact.
  • Will struggle to hold ground against angle pressure.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in all 13 games as a reserve (4 tackles).
  • 2023: Played in the first 6 games as a reserve (5 tackles). Missed the rest of the season due to injury.
  • 2024: Played in 12 games with 7 starts (19 tackles, INT, 2 PBUs).
  • 2025: Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 10 PBUs. Started 11 games (47 tackles, INT). Missed games with shoulder, hand injuries.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Low-cut cornerback with fast feet, good balance and a highly competitive spirit. Hall loves staying as tight to the route as possible and supports the run with ideal aggression. He has adequate press strength and is solid matching releases, hugging man routes and quickly closing to tackle from zone. Though he plays fast, he lacks long speed and receivers can separate from him on vertical routes. He is twitchy to close but is more of a responder than an anticipator, limiting his on-ball production. Hall’s toughness against the run helps his cause as a likely Day 3 pick at nickelback.
profiles.strengths:
• Low-cut with oily hips and twitchy feet.
  • Fast, agile feet in his mirror and transitions.
  • Balanced mover with sudden change-of-direction quickness.
  • Usually stays tight to route stems and turns from tight press-man.
  • Crowds receiver and closes his catch window when contesting downfield.
  • Urgency and physicality show up consistently at the catch point.
  • Quick close-and-tackle limits yards after catch.
  • Serious run supporter who usually defeats his blocker.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Has takeaway twitch but rarely seen challenging into passing lanes.
  • Needs quicker depth gain from zone relative to route concepts.
  • Face-guards from start to finish instead of locating the ball when his back turned.
  • Still has some technical issues to clean up in man.
  • Sometimes leans into receivers instead of using feet to close distance.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Arizona): Played in 5 games as a reserve (7 tackles).
  • 2023 (Arizona): Honorable Mention All-Pac-12 Conference. Tied for eighth in the FBS with 1.2 passes defensed per game (15 total). Played in all 13 games with 11 starts (25 tackles, INT).
  • 2024 (Arizona): Second-team All-Big 12 Conference. Tied for the team lead with 6 PBUs. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts (44 tackles, 2 TFLs).
  • 2025: Started 7 games (19 tackles, TFL, 2 INTs, 3 PBUs). Missed time with rib and hamstring injuries.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Davis is more disruptive than productive with size, length and strength to reroute releases from press. He slams catch windows closed when he’s in the neighborhood. While his physical traits make a wideout’s job tougher, their route-running prowess can do the same to Davis. He’s average matching breaks and more complicated routes tend to shake him. His long arms help him defend throws from deep zone and make tackles in the open field. An NFL staff should be able to coax more consistent run support from him. He’ll be tagged as a zone corner, but his eyes and range could earn him free safety consideration.
profiles.strengths:
• Very tall with an impressive wingspan and plus ball skills.
  • Able to knock releases off course with his length.
  • Will squat on and jump short routes when he senses it.
  • Impossible to throw over him when he’s in phase downfield.
  • Keys quarterback to squeeze routes from zone shuffle.
  • Gains speed quickly when his legs unfurl.
  • Expansive tackle net to bring in open-field runners.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Pops upright as his pedal progresses.
  • Hitch in his transition when break catches him off-guard.
  • Willing to grab instead of trusting technique and size.
  • Athletic but struggles guarding multi-breaking routes.
  • Inconsistent body control as a tackler.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Ball State): First-team All-MAC. Led team with 7 receiving TDs (35-373-10.7). Played in all 12 games with 5 starts.
  • 2023 (Ball State): Third-team All-MAC. Played in all 12 games with 9 starts (34-295-8.7, 3 TDs). 
  • 2024 (Ball State): Second-team All-MAC. Ranked sixth in the FBS with 94 receptions. Led team with 839 receiving yards (8.9 per), 8 receiving TDs. Played in all 12 games with 8 starts.
  • 2025: First-team All-Big 12 Conference. Led FBS TEs with 74 receptions (727-9.8, 6 TDs) Started all 13 games. Spent the spring with Wisconsin before entering the transfer portal in April.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Long, angular pass-catching tight end with impressive production throughout his career. Koziol’s monotonous route-running and average play speed lead to an excessive number of contested catches, but his soft hands and overall ball skills help to bring them in at an impressive rate. He appears to lack the technique and toughness necessary to become a functional run blocker against pro competition. Koziol has a chance to become a TE3, but he needs to fine-tune his route-running and play with better short-area quickness to stick around as a catch-only option.
profiles.strengths:
• Consistent production in all categories as a pass-catcher.
  • Tall target with impressive length and expansive catch radius.
  • Plays with plus catch focus to bring in contested throws.
  • Hands are soft and natural to gather throws.
  • Catches with hand extension away from his frame.
  • Able to swerve and elude early tackle tries, stacking yards after the catch.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs more muscle mass and general play strength.
  • Far too easy to reroute his release with force.
  • Monotonous route tempo makes it easier to squeeze his route.
  • Lacks suddenness and burst getting in and out of turns/breaks.
  • Slow to sink and open to his quarterback on stop routes.
  • Mentality is too passive as a potential NFL run blocker.

profiles.bio:
• 2023: Freshman All-American. SEC All-Freshman Team. Started all 13 games (74 tackles, 8.5 TFLs with 3 sacks, FF).
  • 2024: Led team with 82 tackles. Started all 13 games (9.5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, INT, 5 PBUs). Team captain. 
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Led team with 73 tackles. Started all 13 games (7.5 TFLs with 1 sack, 3 PBUs). Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: York is a defensive quarterback who aligns the front and leads by example with all-day urgency. He’s compact with thick thighs and good play strength but struggles to hold up against/shed climbing blocks that find him. His short-area movement is choppy but efficient with quick acceleration to chase outside runs, but he lacks sustained speed. He’s in constant “trigger and close” mode but needs better diagnostic patience to avoid missed run fits. He will struggle holding up in man coverage. Linebackers with York’s size/length typically face uphill roster climbs, but his tape appears good enough to warrant a backup role with instant special-teams value.
profiles.strengths:
• Compact with a thick base and good balance.
  • Plays the game with an abundance of energy and urgency.
  • Scrapes with pace similar to the run concept.
  • Stays low to dip and slip incoming blocks.
  • Closes quickly on ball-carriers in short spaces.
  • Accelerates through contact to deliver pop on tackles.
  • Diagnoses screens quickly and hustles to shut them down.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Needs more patience downhill to avoid losing gap leverage.
  • Undersized and gets knocked around by big-bodied blockers.
  • Struggles shedding blocks once they sink into him.
  • Short arms limit consistent wrap finishes as a tackler.
  • Has issues losing track of zone threats.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Boise State): Redshirted. Played in 2 games as a reserve (5-2-0.4 rushing).
  • 2022 (Boise State): Mountain West Conference Freshman of the Year. Played in 13 games with 10 starts (166-271-61.3, 2,042 yards, 14 TDs, 6 INTs passing; 81-588-7.3, 10 TDs rushing). Offensive MVP of the Frisco Bowl win over North Texas (137 yards, TD passing; 119 yards, 2 TDs rushing).
  • 2023 (Boise State): Played in 13 games with 12 starts (121-212-57.1, 1,752 yards, 11 TDs, 9 INTs passing; 78-436-5.6, 9 TDs rushing). Offensive MVP of the Mountain West Conference Championship Game (12-15, 226 yards, 2 TDs passing; 90 yards, 2 TDs rushing). Entered the transfer portal after the championship game.
  • 2024: Started all 13 games (230-381-60.4, 3,154 yards, 15 TDs, 9 INTs passing; 156-602-3.9, 8 TDs rushing).
  • 2025: Ranked ninth in the FBS with 13.7 yards per completion. Played in all 12 games with 11 starts (198-326-60.7, 2,714 yards, 19 TDs, 11 INTs passing; 139-777-5.6, 8 TDs rushing).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A long, rangy, dual-threat quarterback with upside, Green’s ability to generate explosive plays as a runner and passer helped keep his offense afloat. In-game consistency has been a sticking point, though. He has a long, unorthodox delivery and tends to baby too many throws. He can generate enough velocity and distance to stress defenses over the second and third levels. Green puts the ball in harm’s way at an alarming rate, which will translate to greater trouble against more talented defenders and more complicated coverage reads. His ability to win with his legs on called runs or pocket breaks pushes his value beyond his passing profile. Green’s upside will be tantalizing but his ceiling will only track with his growth as a passer.
profiles.strengths:
• Rare size/athleticism for the position.
  • Provides dual-theat attack options and can work off script.
  • Tall with an elevated release point for layered throws between the numbers.
  • Does an admirable job of tying feet to eyes through progressions.
  • Gets through progressions smoothly when he finds his rhythm.
  • Throws with adequate velocity for tight-window throws.
  • Can outstride pursuit and turn scrambles into first downs.
  • Ability as a runner gives his offense a chance when passing is off.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Disappointing passing results when he breaks the pocket.
  • Processing and timing need improvements on the next level. 
  • Struggles with post-snap recognition of zone lurkers underneath.
  • Needs to more consistently quiet his feet to improve accuracy.
  • Needs to get better at manipulating and holding coverage with his eyes.
  • Throws with a long-limbed delivery that slows his operation and release.
  • Aims throws that turn into misfires or underthrown interceptions.
  • Too willing to move backwards instead of climbing when under pressure.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Valdosta State): Played in all 11 games with 6 starts (22-431-19.6, 6 TDs).
  • 2023 (Valdosta State): Started all 14 games (38-596-15.7, 4 TDs). 
  • 2024: Second-team All-Sun Belt Conference. Led team with 56 receptions, 961 receiving yards (17.2 per), school-record 9 receiving TDs. Played in all 12 games with 10 starts. 
  • 2025: First-team All-Sun Belt. Led team with 71 receptions, 1,004 receiving yards (14.1 per), 6 receiving TDs. Played in 12 games with 11 starts.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Long-legged, vertical-minded wideout with the speed and ability to stress corners from snap to whistle. Hurst is quick to beat press and hit the accelerator into his route work. He has the hips, feet and balance to run a more robust route tree than what we saw from him in college. He’s an above-average ball-tracker deep and a dangerous catch-and-run option. The hands are average and he needs to become more assertive on 50/50 balls on all three levels. Hurst appears capable of surviving the jump in competition and projects as a “Z” receiver with quality upside.
profiles.strengths:
• Quick to shake press with his stutter-and-go release.
  • Above-average acceleration for a long-legged wideout.
  • Downhill speed features a second gear to run under deep throws.
  • Tracks and adjusts paths to deep throws with consistent focus.
  • Good footwork for quick in-and-outs at break points.
  • Hip sink to stop quickly on comebacks and zone-beaters.
  • Juice to eliminate pursuit angles with the ball in his hands.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Struggles to bring in tough catches despite his wingspan.
  • Inconsistent stacking cornerbacks on deep routes.
  • Doesn’t impose his size on catch points nearly enough.
  • Will face a huge step up in coverage quality in the pros.
  • Very minimal run-blocking on tape.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Long Beach City College): 31 tackles, 2 INTs, 8 PBUs in 8 games.
  • 2022 (Long Beach City College): 42 tackles, 3 INTs, 4 PBUs in 11 games.
  • 2023 (Washington): Played in 14 games with 1 start (26 tackles, TFL, INT, 6 PBUs).
  • 2024 (Washington): Honorable Mention All-Big Ten Conference. Led team with 10 PBUs. Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (43 tackles, 2 TFLs, INT, FF). Team's Defensive Skill Player of the Year.
  • 2025: Started 7 games (20 tackles, 2 TFLs, 6 PBUs). Stopped for speeding and cited for driving with a revoked license in November.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Dixon is a perimeter corner with the size and athleticism to work in multiple coverages. From press, he’s fairly sticky in the early stages and does a good job of anticipating breaks when playing off-man. However, he lacks top-end speed to stay connected to vertical threats as the route stretches out. Dixon needs to protect his leverage more effectively and allow fewer opportunities for explosive plays over the top. He does use his size and efficient burst for on-ball chances, though. He won’t stand out in any one area but is good enough in most to compete for a spot as a backup.
profiles.strengths:
• Above-average athlete with agile feet.
  • Smooth pedal mirroring release from press-man.
  • Anticipates and shadows the break points.
  • Transitions forward quickly from the top of his drop.
  • Faces up and finds the football when phasing vertical routes.
  • Size and length are disruptive when he’s contesting.
  • Runs through pass-catchers with jarring force.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks consistent decisiveness and route balance in short zone.
  • Has trouble staying tight to the route from trail positioning.
  • Plays upright in off coverages, creating imbalance in transitions.
  • Missing the same energy he shows as a run tackler when striking receivers.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted.
  • 2022: Played in 2 games as a reserve (0.5 TFL).
  • 2023: Played in all 14 games with 13 starts (38 tackles, 1.5 TFLs with 1 sack, PBU).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (40 tackles, 7.5 TFLs with 2.5 sacks, PBU). 
  • 2025: Started 12 games (16 tackles, 3 TFLs with 2 sacks, PBU, FF, blocked kick). Missed the start of the year recovering from a high ankle sprain on which he had tightrope surgery. Team captain.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Keenan is a girthy nose tackle with average talent and upside. He has the frame/play strength to take on blocks and fight for ground with reasonable success. However, a lack of length limits his ability to command the point of attack with a quick punch-and-shed. He’s more block-beater than block-eater and won’t offer much as a rusher. Keenan has Day 3 value as a rotational player.
profiles.strengths:
• Carries a broad build with stocky limbs.
  • Productive 2024 season with 40 tackles (7.5 for loss) and 2.5 sacks.
  • Beats center into the neutral zone with quick hand strike.
  • Leverage and base strength to hang in against double-teams.
  • Works to maintain his run fit while moving laterally.
  • Adequate short-area quickness to tackle his gaps.
  • Powerful picker on T/E and T/T twists.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Short arms allow blockers to crowd his frame.
  • Takes time to free himself from connected blocks.
  • Below-average range getting down the line and stopping the run.
  • Takes blocks on but not enough block destruction.
  • Lacks ideal burst to create momentum for his bull rush.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Michigan): Redshirted.
  • 2022 (Michigan): Played in 4 games as a kicker and punter (1-41-41.0 P, 1 fair catch, 1 inside the 20; 2-2-100.0 XP; 6 touchbacks on 8 kickoffs). 
  • 2023 (Michigan): Third-team All-Big Ten Conference. Played in all 15 games for the national champions (53-2,346-44.3, long 71, 4 touchbacks, 26 fair caught, 18 inside the 20; 68 touchbacks on 99 kickoffs). 
  • 2024 (Michigan): Played in 12 games (49-2,088-42.6, long 68, 3 touchbacks, 22 fair caught, 15 inside the 20; 37 touchbacks on 59 kickoffs). 3 coverage tackles. 
  • 2025: Played in all 12 games (50-2,202-44.0, long 71, 6 touchbacks, 17 fair caught, 17 inside the 20).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Fifth-year senior with two seasons as a full-time punter at Michigan and one at Florida. Doman has good size and quality hang time on his punts, but he doesn’t definitively check boxes with his power or touch to bury opponents deep in their own territory.
profiles.strengths:
• Can punt, kickoff, hold and even step in for emergency field-goal tries.
  • Gets it from touch to toe with proper quickness.
  • Hits punts with pro-caliber hang time.
  • Adequate accuracy as a directional punter.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Hasn’t proven to be a field-flipper with his leg strength.
  • Lack of touch turns into touchbacks on short-field punts.
  • Nose-drop technique yields inconsistent results to deaden the punt.

profiles.bio:
• 2022 (Clemson): Played in all 14 games with 2 starts (22 tackles, sack, INT, 4 PBUs). Enrolled in January.
  • 2023 (Clemson): Played in 12 games with 1 start (14 tackles, TFL, 4 PBUs).
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games with 6 starts (22 tackles, 2 INTs-1 returned for TD, 4 PBUs, FF).
  • 2025: Led team with 2 INTs (1 returned for TD). Played in all 13 games with 12 starts (24 tackles, 1.5 TFLs, 4 PBUs).

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Pride did an admirable job of holding up outside against solid SEC competition but he’ll be under consideration as a slot corner in the pros. He plays with good zone awareness and average man-cover talent. He’s athletic with agile feet and is feisty at the catch-point, but he might not have the needed speed or length. Toughness is not an issue, but he will be dragged for additional yardage as a run-support tackler. Pride could go late on Day 3, but a lack of traits and explosiveness create an uphill fight for him.
profiles.strengths:
• Physical and aggressive from press.
  • Quick to crowd into receiver’s chest on deep routes.
  • Gets his head around in time to locate deep throws.
  • Plays with above-average discipline and feel in zone.
  • Above-average closing quickness from his drop.
  • Finds openings to snake his hand into the catch-point.
  • Smallish but comes downhill ready to help against the run.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Loses positioning to release fakes from press.
  • Average anticipation and transition quickness at break-points.
  • Lack of size/length limits on-ball production.
  • Allows too much room after the catch for add-on yardage.
  • Struggles to quickly bring down running backs.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (Gardner-Webb): Redshirted. Played in 1 game as a reserve.
  • 2022 (Gardner-Webb): Started all 13 games (6 at RT, 7 at LT).
  • 2023 (Florida International): Started 10 games at LT.
  • 2024 (Florida International): Started 12 games at LT.
  • 2025: First-team All-American Athletic Conference. Started 11 games at RT.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Burke is a tall tackle with plus drive-blocking talent for his body type. He uses flexible hips and ankles, along with well-placed hands, to create leverage at the point of attack. He finishes blocks with good aggression when the opportunity arises. A lack of short-area quickness limits his range as a run blocker and in pass protection. He’s scheme-dependent in the run game and will need help managing NFL edge speed, but strong hands allow for longer sustained control when he lands cleanly. There are areas of concern that might not be coachable, but Burke’s length and demeanor work in his favor.
profiles.strengths:
• Fires heavy-handed punch to fit and control run blocks.
  • Gets into first contact with surprising bend for a tall tackle.
  • Plays with finisher’s mindset when he gets chances to bury blocks.
  • Stays sticky to blocks with vice-grip hand strength. 
  • Maximizes length with a firm, well-timed punch into rushers.
  • Unlocks hips and turns out ankles to sit and anchor against power.
  • Showed improvement in identifying end/tackle twist games in 2025.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Will struggle to reach landmarks for back-side cut-off blocks.
  • Lumbering movement limits success in space and on combo climbs.
  • Can be displaced by stout 4i/5-technique take-ons.
  • Labors out of his stance and is late to his set-points against speed.
  • Average ability to recover and redirect once his edge is compromised.
  • Still overcommits and rides too deep on some end/tackle twists.

profiles.bio:
• 2021 (UTSA): Redshirted. Played in the final 3 games as a reserve (1 tackle).
  • 2022 (UTSA): Freshman All-American. Honorable Mention All-Conference USA, C-USA All-Freshman Team. Tied for 10th in the FBS with school-record 18 TFLs (breaking Marcus Davenport's mark). Led team with 8 sacks, tied for team lead with 2 FFs. Started all 14 games (59 tackles, 6 PBUs).
  • 2023 (UTSA): Conference USA Defensive Player of the Year. First-team All-C-USA. Ranked third in the FBS with 14 sacks, tied for 12th with 17.5 TFL. Started 12 games (45 tackles, INT, 3 PBUs, FF). Entered the transfer portal after the regular season.
  • 2024: Started all 16 games (35 tackles, 9.5 TFLs with 5.5 sacks, PBU, 2 FFs). 
  • 2025: Played in 12 games with 5 starts (35 tackles, 5 TFLs with 3 sacks, 3 PBUs). Finalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy, aka the Academic Heisman.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Moore is a highly productive, 46-game starter with flexible NFL positioning. He’s undersized and lacks NFL length as an edge defender, but he’s a skilled, instinctive rusher with a robust set of approaches. He won’t burn the edges with pure speed but he compensates for that with a deep bag of moves. In limited snaps, Moore showed potential at off-ball linebacker, but questions persist about his pursuit speed and ability to cover in the NFL. Some teams might label him a “tweener,” but I see a versatile prospect whose competitiveness and feel for the game should allow him to translate no matter the position he plays.
profiles.strengths:
• Finished with 46 career starts between UTSA and Texas.
  • Highly productive across the impact categories.
  • Alters entry points and strings together smart hand attacks mid-rush.
  • Instinctive inside and outside spin counters await tackles.
  • Secondary rush is a consistent weapon for sack scooping.
  • Flashed competence and upside as an off-ball linebacker.
  • Adequate athleticism when asked to drop into space.
  • Pursues to the sideline with sound leverage.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Lacks a threatening burst to the top of the rush.
  • Hands are fast and active but lack sting.
  • Edge-setting and block-shedding run hot and cold.
  • Still developing timing and key recognition off the ball.
  • Average change-of-direction quickness when it’s needed.
  • Below-average pursuit speed and open-field fluidity.

profiles.bio:
• 2022: Played in the final 7 games as a kickoff specialist (18 touchbacks on 32 kickoffs). 
  • 2023: Played in all 12 games (29-29-100.0 XP; 17-21-81.0 FG, 2-3 50+, long 54, 1 blocked; 80 points; 56 touchbacks on 70 kickoffs). 2 coverage tackles.
  • 2024: Played in all 13 games (44-44-100.0 XP: 18-21-85.7 FG, 3-4 50+, long 55; 98 points; 57 touchbacks on 75 kickoffs). 
  • 2025: Third-team All-SEC. Played in all 12 games (27-28-96.4 XP; 18-22-81.8 FG, 5-6 50+, long 56; 81 points; 46 touchbacks on 60 kickoffs). Set program record with 10 career FG over 50 yards long. 1 coverage tackle.

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: Smack has a strong leg and can deliver beyond 50 yards at a high rate without having to drive balls with a lower trajectory. His repeatable process and consistent placement give him an above-average chance of making it in the league.
profiles.strengths:
• Consistent ball-striker with good lift and placement.
  • Made 77% (10 of 13) of his kicks from 50+ yards out.
  • Capable as an emergency punter if needed.
  • Good size with ability to cover and tackle on kickoffs.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Missed 47-yard kick in overtime loss to Tennessee in 2024.
  • High percentage of misses were off the right hash.
  • Missed three field goals in the first game of 2025, including 39- and 40-yard tries.

profiles.bio:
• 2021: Redshirted. Played in 4 games as a reserve.
  • 2022: Started 11 games at LT.
  • 2023: Started 13 games at LT. 
  • 2024: Third-team All-SEC. Started all 13 games at LT.
  • 2025: Shared the Jacobs Blocking Trophy (top SEC OL) with Alabama's Kadyn Proctor. First-team All-SEC. Started all 13 games (11 at LT, 2 at C). 

-- by Chad Reuter
profiles.overview: A four-year starting left tackle with deep family ties to Texas A&M, Zuhn will likely slide inside to center or guard as a pro due to a lack of functional length. He has first-step quickness to reach lateral landmarks but lacks ideal athleticism to play in space and is more consistently effective working double-teams and combo blocks. His anchor and savvy help mitigate his lack of length, but he could struggle to mirror and recover quickly enough when beaten by athletic rushers or twists. Zuhn projects as “solid” more than “standout” but he could have a long career as a starter at center or guard while offering emergency help as a tackle.
profiles.strengths:
• Four-year starter and team captain in 2025.
  • Mirrors rusher while maintaining proper base width.
  • Has enough anchor for a move inside.
  • Hits hand resets with independent hands when needed.
  • Quick first step laterally creates advantages on reach blocks. 
  • Keeps looking for someone to block until the whistle blows.
  • Fires stiff under-hooks and unlocks hips into his base blocks.
  • Displayed good radar and fitted contact as a lead-pulling center in limited snaps.
profiles.weaknesses:
• Average range in pass slides to patrol both A-gaps.
  • Lacks recovery agility when rushers beat him on his edge.
  • Below-average quickness and athleticism in space.
  • Two-gappers create early separation with length.
  • Leans into run blocks, creating imbalance and tougher adjustments.
  • Inconsistent technique and timing on his work-up blocks.

profiles.bio:
• 2020: Redshirted. Played in 3 games as a reserve walk-on (8 tackles).
  • 2021: Led team with 7 PBUs. Played in all 12 games with 5 starts (31 tackles, TFL, 7 PBUs).
